6.16.5.b.m: in the dark fortnight, with the seventh addressed to Indra and Agni;

6.16.6.a.m: in both [fortnights], with the eighth: 'I have praised Dadhikrāvan.'

6.16.7.a.s: mamāgne varco vihaveṣvastviti catasraḥ purastādagnīṣomīyāyāḥ pūrvapakṣe /
6.16.7.a.d: ममाग्ने वर्चो विहवेष्वस्त्विति चतस्रः पुरस्तादग्नीषोमीयायाः पूर्वपक्षे ।
6.16.7.a.m: In the bright fortnight, four [verses beginning]: 'May splendour be mine, O Agni, in invocations' [are recited] before the verse to Agni and Soma;

6.16.7.b.m: likewise, before the verse to Indra and Agni in the dark fortnight.

6.16.8.a.s: agna āyūṃṣi pavasa iti ṣaḍbhiḥ saṃvatsaresaṃvatsare sadā vā
6.16.8.a.d: अग्न आयूंषि पवस इति षड्भिः संवत्सरेसंवत्सरे सदा वा
6.16.8.a.m: With the six [verses]: 'O Agni, you purify life-breaths,' [he venerates] year by year, or constantly.

6.16.9.a.m: Or year by year he should offer the oblations to Agni Pavamāna in place of these.

6.16.10.a.m: The [recitation] from: 'Giver of life, O Agni' up to [the formula addressed to] Citrāvasu is established.

6.16.11.a.m: In the evening, he venerates thrice with [the formula containing] Citrāvasu;

6.16.11.b.m: in the morning, thrice with [that containing] Arvāgvasu: 'O Arvāgvasu, may I safely attain your far shore.'

6.16.12.a.s: indhānāstvā śataṃ himā ityupasthāyendhānāstvā śataṃ himāḥ /
6.16.12.a.d: इन्धानास्त्वा शतं हिमा इत्युपस्थायेन्धानास्त्वा शतं हिमाः ।
6.16.12.a.m: Having venerated with: 'Kindling you for a hundred winters,' [and again] with: 'Kindling you for a hundred winters,'

6.16.12.b.s: agneḥ samidasyabhiśastyā ma pāhi somasya samidasi paraspā ma edhi yamasya samidasi mṛtyormā pāhīti catasraḥ samidha ekaikasminnādhāya saṃ tvamagne sūryasya varcasāgathā ity anuvākaśeṣeṇopasthāya vayaṃ soma vrate tava manastanūṣu bibhrataḥ prajāvanto aśīmahīti mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe
6.16.12.b.d: अग्नेः समिदस्यभिशस्त्या म पाहि सोमस्य समिदसि परस्पा म एधि यमस्य समिदसि मृत्योर्मा पाहीति चतस्रः समिध एकैकस्मिन्नाधाय सं त्वमग्ने सूर्यस्य वर्चसागथा इत्य् अनुवाकशेषेणोपस्थाय वयं सोम व्रते तव मनस्तनूषु बिभ्रतः प्रजावन्तो अशीमहीति मुखं विमृष्टे
6.16.12.b.m: having placed four kindling-sticks, one on each [fire], with: 'You are the kindling-stick of Agni; protect me from curse; you are the kindling-stick of Soma; be my guardian against enemies; you are the kindling-stick of Yama; protect me from death,' and having venerated with the remainder of the anuvāka: 'You have united, O Agni, with the splendour of the sun,' he wipes his mouth with: 'O Soma, in your observance, keeping our mind in our bodies, may we attain [blessings] having offspring.'

6.17.1.a.m: He looks at the houses with: 'I look upon offspring.'

6.17.2.a.m: He venerates the cow-pen with: 'You are water, may I partake of your water.'

6.17.3.a.m: Standing between the fires, he mutters: 'O wealthy ones, rest.'

6.17.4.a.m: He touches a male calf with: 'You are united, having all forms.'

6.17.5.a.m: He touches a female calf with: 'You are united, having all forms.'

6.17.6.a.m: Or [he touches] a male calf with: 'You are the world, nourish a thousandfold nourishment.'

6.17.7.a.s: upa tvāgne divediva iti tisṛbhirgāyatrībhirgārhapatyamupatiṣṭhate 'gne tvaṃ no antama iti catasṛbhiśca dvipadābhiḥ
6.17.7.a.d: उप त्वाग्ने दिवेदिव इति तिसृभिर्गायत्रीभिर्गार्हपत्यमुपतिष्ठते ऽग्ने त्वं नो अन्तम इति चतसृभिश्च द्विपदाभिः
6.17.7.a.m: With three gāyatrī verses: 'To you, O Agni, day by day,' and with four two-footed verses: 'O Agni, you are our nearest,' he venerates the gārhapatya.

6.17.8.a.s: sa no bodhi śrudhī havamuruṣyā ṇo aghāyataḥ samasmādityeṣā caturthī bhavati
6.17.8.a.d: स नो बोधि श्रुधी हवमुरुष्या णो अघायतः समस्मादित्येषा चतुर्थी भवति
6.17.8.a.m: "Be conscious of us, hear our call, protect us from this person intending evil" is the fourth [verse].

6.17.9.a.s: ūrjā vaḥ paśyāmyūrjā ma paśyateti gṛhān prekṣate paśūnvā
6.17.9.a.d: ऊर्जा वः पश्याम्यूर्जा म पश्यतेति गृहान् प्रेक्षते पशून्वा
6.17.9.a.m: With "With strength I look upon you; look upon me with strength," he looks upon his house or upon his cattle.

6.17.10.a.m: "May the great help of the three be [ours], heavenly, of Mitra, of Aryaman,

6.17.10.c.m: "For not at all at home, nor on the roads, in the wilderness,

6.17.10.e.m: "For they, the sons of Aditi, bestow perpetual protection

6.17.10.f.m: and desirable gifts upon the worshipper,"—with this triplet dedicated to Prajāpati he attends [the fire].

6.17.11.a.m: If he should desire concerning anyone, "May he return safely," he should look after him with these [verses].

6.17.11.b.m: He indeed returns safely: this is a rule unconnected with a sacrifice.

6.17.12.a.s: mā naḥ śaṃso araruṣo dhūrtiḥ praṇaṅmartyasya /
6.17.12.a.d: मा नः शंसो अररुषो धूर्तिः प्रणङ्मर्त्यस्य ।
6.17.12.a.m: "May neither the utterance nor the mischief of the niggardly mortal perish us;

6.17.12.c.m: "He who is wealthy, who drives away disease, who finds wealth and increases prosperity—

6.17.12.e.s: pari te dūḍabho ratho 'smām̐ aśnotu viśvataḥ /
6.17.12.e.d: परि ते दूडभो रथो ऽस्माम्̐ अश्नोतु विश्वतः ।
6.17.12.e.m: "May your chariot, difficult to harm, encompass us from every side,

6.18.1.a.s: tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ somānaṃ svaraṇaṃ mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ pra sa mitra kadā cana starīrasi kadā cana prayucchasi pari tvāgne puraṃ vayamityupasthāya
6.18.1.a.d: तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं सोमानं स्वरणं मित्रस्य चर्षणीधृतः प्र स मित्र कदा चन स्तरीरसि कदा चन प्रयुच्छसि परि त्वाग्ने पुरं वयमित्युपस्थाय
6.18.1.a.m: Having attended with "That desirable [splendor] of Savitṛ…", "The soma, the heavenly…", "Of Mitra, who supports the peoples…", "Forth that, O Mitra…", "Never are you barren, never do you neglect…", and "Around you, O Agni, we, as a fortress…",

6.18.2.a.s: nimṛdo 'si nyahaṃ taṃ mṛdyāsaṃ yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣma iti dakṣiṇasya padaḥ pārṣṇyā nimṛdnīyādyadi pāpīyasā spardheta /
6.18.2.a.d: निमृदो ऽसि न्यहं तं मृद्यासं यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्म इति दक्षिणस्य पदः पार्ष्ण्या निमृद्नीयाद्यदि पापीयसा स्पर्धेत ।
6.18.2.a.m: with "You are the trampler-down; may I trample down him who hates us and whom we hate," he should trample down with the heel of the right foot, if he is competing with an inferior.

6.18.2.b.s: prabhūrasi prāhaṃ tamabhibhūyāsaṃ yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣma iti dakṣiṇataḥ pado nigṛhṇīyādyadi sadṛśena /
6.18.2.b.d: प्रभूरसि प्राहं तमभिभूयासं यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्म इति दक्षिणतः पदो निगृह्णीयाद्यदि सदृशेन ।
6.18.2.b.m: With "You are superior; may I overcome him who hates us and whom we hate," he should press down with [the middle of] the right foot, if with an equal.

6.18.2.c.s: abhibhūrasyabhyahaṃ taṃ bhūyāsaṃ yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣma iti prapadena yadi śreyasā
6.18.2.c.d: अभिभूरस्यभ्यहं तं भूयासं यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्म इति प्रपदेन यदि श्रेयसा
6.18.2.c.m: With "You are the overcomer; may I overpower him who hates us and whom we hate," with the forepart of the foot, if with a superior.

6.18.3.a.s: pūṣā mā paśupāḥ pātu pūṣā mā pathipāḥ pātu pūṣā mādhipāḥ pātu pūṣā madhipatiḥ pātviti lokānupasthāya prācī digagnirdevatāgniṃ sa ṛcchatu yo maitasyai diśo 'bhidāsati /
6.18.3.a.d: पूषा मा पशुपाः पातु पूषा मा पथिपाः पातु पूषा माधिपाः पातु पूषा मधिपतिः पात्विति लोकानुपस्थाय प्राची दिगग्निर्देवताग्निं स ऋच्छतु यो मैतस्यै दिशो ऽभिदासति ।
6.18.3.a.m: Having attended the worlds with "May Pūṣan protect me as protector of cattle; may Pūṣan protect me as protector of paths; may Pūṣan protect me as over-protector; may Pūṣan protect me as lord,": "The eastern direction has Agni as deity; may he reach Agni who harms me from this direction.

6.18.3.b.s: dakṣiṇā digindro devatendraṃ sa ṛcchatu yo maitasyai diśo 'bhidāsati /
6.18.3.b.d: दक्षिणा दिगिन्द्रो देवतेन्द्रं स ऋच्छतु यो मैतस्यै दिशो ऽभिदासति ।
6.18.3.b.m: "The southern direction has Indra as deity; may he reach Indra who harms me from this direction.

6.18.3.c.s: pratīcī dik somo devatā somaṃ sa ṛcchatu yo maitasyai diśo 'bhidāsati /
6.18.3.c.d: प्रतीची दिक् सोमो देवता सोमं स ऋच्छतु यो मैतस्यै दिशो ऽभिदासति ।
6.18.3.c.m: "The western direction has Soma as deity; may he reach Soma who harms me from this direction.

6.18.3.d.s: udīcī diṅmitrāvaruṇau devatā mitrāvaruṇau sa ṛcchatu yo maitasyai diśo 'bhidāsati /
6.18.3.d.d: उदीची दिङ्मित्रावरुणौ देवता मित्रावरुणौ स ऋच्छतु यो मैतस्यै दिशो ऽभिदासति ।
6.18.3.d.m: "The northern direction has Mitrāvaruṇau as deity; may he reach Mitrāvaruṇau who harms me from this direction.

6.18.3.e.s: ūrdhvā digbṛhaspatirdevatā bṛhaspatiṃ sa ṛcchatu yo maitasyai diśo 'bhidāsati /
6.18.3.e.d: ऊर्ध्वा दिग्बृहस्पतिर्देवता बृहस्पतिं स ऋच्छतु यो मैतस्यै दिशो ऽभिदासति ।
6.18.3.e.m: "The upper direction has Bṛhaspati as deity; may he reach Bṛhaspati who harms me from this direction.

6.18.3.f.s: iyaṃ digaditirdevatāditiṃ sa ṛcchatu yo maitasyai diśo 'bhidāsatīti yathāliṅgaṃ diśa upasthāya
6.18.3.f.d: इयं दिगदितिर्देवतादितिं स ऋच्छतु यो मैतस्यै दिशो ऽभिदासतीति यथालिङ्गं दिश उपस्थाय
6.18.3.f.m: "This [lower] direction has Aditi as deity; may he reach Aditi who harms me from this direction,"—having attended the directions according to their distinguishing marks,

6.19.1.a.s: agnīnupasamādhāya dharmo mā dharmaṇaḥ pātu vidharmo mā vidharmaṇaḥ pātvāyuśca prāyuśca cakṣuśca vicakṣuśca prāṅcāvāṅcoruga urugasya te vācā vayaṃ saṃ bhaktena gamemahītyupasthāyāgna āyūṃṣi pavasa ityāgnipāvamānībhyāṃ gārhapatyamupatiṣṭhate
6.19.1.a.d: अग्नीनुपसमाधाय धर्मो मा धर्मणः पातु विधर्मो मा विधर्मणः पात्वायुश्च प्रायुश्च चक्षुश्च विचक्षुश्च प्राङ्चावाङ्चोरुग उरुगस्य ते वाचा वयं सं भक्तेन गमेमहीत्युपस्थायाग्न आयूंषि पवस इत्याग्निपावमानीभ्यां गार्हपत्यमुपतिष्ठते
6.19.1.a.m: having fed fuel to the fires, and having attended with "May order protect me from unrighteousness; may counter-order protect me from disordered conduct; and life-span, and prolonged life, and sight, and discerning sight; the upward-moving and downward-moving, far-striding; by the voice of you, the far-striding, may we attain our share," he attends the gārhapatya with the two [verses] to Agni Pāvamāna: "O Agni, you purify life-spans…"

6.19.2.b.s: putrasya nāma gṛhṇāti tāmāśiṣamāśāse tantava ityajātasya /
6.19.2.b.d: पुत्रस्य नाम गृह्णाति तामाशिषमाशासे तन्तव इत्यजातस्य ।
6.19.2.b.m: He utters the name of his son: "I pray for that blessing for my lineage," if he is unborn;

6.19.3.a.m: Whatever an agnihotra-offerer should desire, that he should ask of the fires.

6.19.3.b.m: "It bows down to him," it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

6.19.4.a.m: "Should the fires be attended, or should they not be attended?"—thus it is discussed.

6.19.5.a.m: He attends [them] at night, not in the morning.

6.19.6.a.s: na prātaragnimupa canāvarohenna prātarāhitāgniścana manyeteti vājasaneyakam
6.19.6.a.d: न प्रातरग्निमुप चनावरोहेन्न प्रातराहिताग्निश्चन मन्येतेति वाजसनेयकम्
6.19.6.a.m: "In the morning, one should not step down towards the fire; in the morning, one should not consider himself an āhitāgni": thus [says] the Vājasaneyaka.

6.19.7.a.s: bhūrbhuvaḥ suvaḥ suprajāḥ prajayā bhūyāsaṃ suvīro vīraiḥ suvarcā varcasā supoṣaḥ poṣairityevopatiṣṭheteti vājasneyakam /
6.19.7.a.d: भूर्भुवः सुवः सुप्रजाः प्रजया भूयासं सुवीरो वीरैः सुवर्चा वर्चसा सुपोषः पोषैरित्येवोपतिष्ठेतेति वाजस्नेयकम् ।
6.19.7.a.m: "Bhūr, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ! May I be rich in offspring through offspring, rich in heroes through heroes, rich in brilliance through brilliance, rich in nourishment through nourishments"—with this alone should he attend: thus [says] the Vājasaneyaka.

6.19.7.b.s: bhartuṃ vaḥ śakeyaṃ śraddhā me mā vyāgāditi vā
6.19.7.b.d: भर्तुं वः शकेयं श्रद्धा मे मा व्यागादिति वा
6.19.7.b.m: Or with: "May I be able to maintain you; may my faith not depart."

6.19.8.a.m: Some say: he should attend evening and morning only with the Vātsapra [hymn],

6.19.9.a.m: or with the hymn to the cows, or with the hymn to the horse.

6.20.1.a.m: In the morning, [the fire] is to be attended with the morning ablution.

6.20.2.a.s: adhiśrita unnīyamāne vā mamāgne varco vihaveṣvastviti catasro japitvāpāṃ pate yo 'pāṃ bhāgaḥ sa ta eṣa pratiṣiktā arātayaḥ pratiṣiktā arātayaḥ pratiṣiktā arātaya iti trirbhūmau pratiṣicya kālāya vāṃ jaitriyāya vāmaudbhettriyāya vāmannādyāya vāmavanenije sukṛtāya vām /
6.20.2.a.d: अधिश्रित उन्नीयमाने वा ममाग्ने वर्चो विहवेष्वस्त्विति चतस्रो जपित्वापां पते यो ऽपां भागः स त एष प्रतिषिक्ता अरातयः प्रतिषिक्ता अरातयः प्रतिषिक्ता अरातय इति त्रिर्भूमौ प्रतिषिच्य कालाय वां जैत्रियाय वामौद्भेत्त्रियाय वामन्नाद्याय वामवनेनिजे सुकृताय वाम् ।
6.20.2.a.m: While [the milk] is set on the fire or being scooped out, having muttered the four [verses] beginning "May my brilliance, O Agni, be present in invocations…", and having poured water out thrice on the ground with "O Lord of waters, that which is the share of the waters, that is yours; repelled are the enemies, repelled are the enemies, repelled are the enemies," [he mutters:] "For time, for victory, for breakthrough, for food-eating, for good deeds, I wash both of you [hands].

6.20.2.b.s: idamahaṃ duradmanyāṃ niṣplāvayāmi bhrātṛvyāṇāṃ sapatnānāmahaṃ bhūyāsamuttamaḥ /
6.20.2.b.d: इदमहं दुरद्मन्यां निष्प्लावयामि भ्रातृव्याणां सपत्नानामहं भूयासमुत्तमः ।
6.20.2.b.m: "Here I rinse away bad digestion; may I be foremost among rivals, among enemies.

6.20.2.c.s: apāṃ maitrādivodakamiti hastau prakṣālya śriyaṃ dhātarmayi dhehi śriyo mādhipatiṃ kuru /
6.20.2.c.d: अपां मैत्रादिवोदकमिति हस्तौ प्रक्षाल्य श्रियं धातर्मयि धेहि श्रियो माधिपतिं कुरु ।
6.20.2.c.m: "May the waters, friendly…" Having washed both hands, and having muttered: "Bestow prosperity upon me, O Creator; make me the lord of prosperity.

6.20.2.d.s: viśāmīśāno maghavendro mā yaśasā nayaditi japitvātharvyuṣṭā devajūtā vīḍu chapathajambhanīḥ /
6.20.2.d.d: विशामीशानो मघवेन्द्रो मा यशसा नयदिति जपित्वाथर्व्युष्टा देवजूता वीडु छपथजम्भनीः ।
6.20.2.d.m: "May Indra, the bountiful, ruler of the peoples, lead me with glory," and having sipped water with: "Quickly shining, impelled by the gods, steadfast, destroying curses,

6.20.2.e.s: āpo malamiva prāṇijannasmatsu śapathāṃ adhītyācamyendriyāvatīmadyāhaṃ vācamudyāsaṃ dīrghaprāṇo 'cchinno 'dabdho gopāḥ /
6.20.2.e.d: आपो मलमिव प्राणिजन्नस्मत्सु शपथां अधीत्याचम्येन्द्रियावतीमद्याहं वाचमुद्यासं दीर्घप्राणो ऽच्छिन्नो ऽदब्धो गोपाः ।
6.20.2.e.m: "as the waters rinse away filth, so have they rinsed curses from us," [he mutters:] "May I speak speech endowed with sensory power today, with long breath, unsevered, unharmed, a guardian.

6.20.2.f.s: ajasraṃ daivyaṃ jyotiḥ sauparṇaṃ cakṣuḥ suśrutau karṇau devaśrutau karṇau keśā barhiḥ śikhā prastaro yathāsthānaṃ kalpayadhvaṃ śaṃ hṛdayāyādo mā mā hāsiṣṭeti yathāliṅgamaṅgāni saṃmṛśya
6.20.2.f.d: अजस्रं दैव्यं ज्योतिः सौपर्णं चक्षुः सुश्रुतौ कर्णौ देवश्रुतौ कर्णौ केशा बर्हिः शिखा प्रस्तरो यथास्थानं कल्पयध्वं शं हृदयायादो मा मा हासिष्टेति यथालिङ्गमङ्गानि संमृश्य
6.20.2.f.m: "Perpetual divine light, vision keen like Suparṇa's, two well-hearing ears, two ears hearing the gods, hair as barhis, topknot as prastara—settle yourselves in your proper places; peace to the heart; do not abandon me!"—having touched his limbs according to their distinguishing marks,

6.21.1.a.s: varco 'si varco mayi dhehyāyukṛdāyuḥpatnī svadhā vo goptryo me stha gopāyata mā rakṣata mātmasado me stha /
6.21.1.a.d: वर्चो ऽसि वर्चो मयि धेह्यायुकृदायुःपत्नी स्वधा वो गोप्त्र्यो मे स्थ गोपायत मा रक्षत मात्मसदो मे स्थ ।
6.21.1.a.m: having attended all [the fires] with "Splendor you are, bestow splendor upon me; life-giving, life-protecting, svadhā! You are my protectors; protect me, guard me; you are seated in my body;

6.21.1.b.s: mā naḥ kaścitpraghānmā prameṣmahyupa pratnamupa bhurbhuvaḥ suvarāyurme yacchateti sarvānupasthāyottareṇānuvākenāhavanīyaṃ gharmā jaṭharānnādaṃ māmadyāsmiñjane kurutamannādo 'hamadyāsmiñjane bhūyāsamanannādaḥ sa yo 'smāndveṣṭi /
6.21.1.b.d: मा नः कश्चित्प्रघान्मा प्रमेष्मह्युप प्रत्नमुप भुर्भुवः सुवरायुर्मे यच्छतेति सर्वानुपस्थायोत्तरेणानुवाकेनाहवनीयं घर्मा जठरान्नादं मामद्यास्मिञ्जने कुरुतमन्नादो ऽहमद्यास्मिञ्जने भूयासमनन्नादः स यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि ।
6.21.1.b.m: "may no one strike us down, may we not perish; up the ancient, up bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ, grant me life-span!", [he attends] the āhavanīya with the subsequent anuvāka: "You two caldrons, two bellies, make me an eater of food today among these people; may I be an eater of food today among these people; may he who hates us be one who has no food!

6.21.1.c.s: kavī mātariśvānā paśumantaṃ māmadyāsmiñjane kurutaṃ paśumānahamadyāsmiñjane bhūyāsamapaśuḥ sa yo 'smāndveṣṭi /
6.21.1.c.d: कवी मातरिश्वाना पशुमन्तं मामद्यास्मिञ्जने कुरुतं पशुमानहमद्यास्मिञ्जने भूयासमपशुः स यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि ।
6.21.1.c.m: "You two sages, two Mātariśvans, make me possessor of cattle today among these people; may I be a possessor of cattle today among these people; may he who hates us be one who has no cattle!

6.21.1.d.s: yamāṅgirasā yaśasvinaṃ māmadyāsmiñjane kurutaṃ yaśasvyahamadyāsmiñjane bhūyāsamayaśāḥ sa yo 'smāndveṣṭi //
6.21.1.d.d: यमाङ्गिरसा यशस्विनं मामद्यास्मिञ्जने कुरुतं यशस्व्यहमद्यास्मिञ्जने भूयासमयशाः स यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि ॥
6.21.1.d.m: "You two Yamas, two Aṅgirases, make me famous today among these people; may I be famous today among these people; may he who hates us be one who has no fame!

6.21.1.e.s: agne yo no anti śapati yaśca dūre samāno agne araṇo durasyuḥ /
6.21.1.e.d: अग्ने यो नो अन्ति शपति यश्च दूरे समानो अग्ने अरणो दुरस्युः ।
6.21.1.e.m: "O Agni, he who curses us from near and he who curses from afar, a kinsman or a stranger aiming evil, O Agni,

6.21.1.f.s: vaiśvānareṇa sayujā sajoṣāstaṃ pratyañcaṃ saṃdaha jātavedaḥ //
6.21.1.f.d: वैश्वानरेण सयुजा सजोषास्तं प्रत्यञ्चं संदह जातवेदः ॥
6.21.1.f.m: "united with Vaiśvānara, sharing his pleasure, burn him up face to face, O Jātavedas!

6.21.1.g.s: agne yatte 'rcistena taṃ pratyarca yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmo 'gne yatte śocistena taṃ pratiśoca yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmo 'gne yatte tapastena taṃ pratitapa yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmo 'gne yatte harastena taṃ pratihara yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmo 'gne yatte tejastena taṃ pratititigdhi yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ
6.21.1.g.d: अग्ने यत्ते ऽर्चिस्तेन तं प्रत्यर्च यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मो ऽग्ने यत्ते शोचिस्तेन तं प्रतिशोच यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मो ऽग्ने यत्ते तपस्तेन तं प्रतितप यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मो ऽग्ने यत्ते हरस्तेन तं प्रतिहर यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मो ऽग्ने यत्ते तेजस्तेन तं प्रतितितिग्धि यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मः
6.21.1.g.m: "O Agni, with that which is your flame, flare against him who hates us and whom we hate; O Agni, with that which is your heat, heat against him who hates us and whom we hate; O Agni, with that which is your burning, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate; O Agni, with that which is your fury, seize against him who hates us and whom we hate; O Agni, with that which is your sharp glow, sharpen against him who hates us and whom we hate."

6.22.1.a.s: agne rucāṃ pate namaste ruce rucaṃ mayi dhehi /
6.22.1.a.d: अग्ने रुचां पते नमस्ते रुचे रुचं मयि धेहि ।
6.22.1.a.m: "O Agni, lord of lights, homage to your light; place light in me!"

6.22.1.b.s: arvāgvaso svasti te pāramaśīyārvāgvaso svasti te pāramaśīyārvāgvaso svasti te pāramaśīya /
6.22.1.b.d: अर्वाग्वसो स्वस्ति ते पारमशीयार्वाग्वसो स्वस्ति ते पारमशीयार्वाग्वसो स्वस्ति ते पारमशीय ।
6.22.1.b.m: "O Arvāgvasu, may I safely attain the other side! O Arvāgvasu, may I safely attain the other side! O Arvāgvasu, may I safely attain the other side!"

6.22.1.c.s: tanturasi tato mā cchitthā asau svasti te 'stvasau svasti te 'stvasau svasti te 'stviti putrāṇāṃ nāmāni gṛhṇāti tristrirekaikasya /
6.22.1.c.d: तन्तुरसि ततो मा च्छित्था असौ स्वस्ति ते ऽस्त्वसौ स्वस्ति ते ऽस्त्वसौ स्वस्ति ते ऽस्त्विति पुत्राणां नामानि गृह्णाति त्रिस्त्रिरेकैकस्य ।
6.22.1.c.m: With: "You are the continuous thread; do not break away from me. N.N., hail to you! N.N., hail to you! N.N., hail to you!" he pronounces the names of his sons, three times for each one.

6.22.1.d.s: svasti vo 'stu ye māmanustha ṣaṇmorvīraṃhasaspāntu dyauśca pṛthivī cāpaścauṣadhayaścorkca sūnṛtā ca /
6.22.1.d.d: स्वस्ति वो ऽस्तु ये मामनुस्थ षण्मोर्वीरंहसस्पान्तु द्यौश्च पृथिवी चापश्चौषधयश्चोर्क्च सूनृता च ।
6.22.1.d.m: "Hail to you who follow after me! May the six broad ones protect me from distress: heaven, earth, waters, plants, refreshment, and truthful speech!"

6.22.1.e.s: yathā ha tyadvasavo gauryaṃ citpadi ṣitāmamuñcatā yajatrāḥ /
6.22.1.e.d: यथा ह त्यद्वसवो गौर्यं चित्पदि षिताममुञ्चता यजत्राः ।
6.22.1.e.m: "Even as you, O adorable Vasus, released the cow tied by the foot, /"

6.22.1.f.s: evo ṣvasmanmuñcatā vyaṃhaḥ pra tāryagne prataraṃ na āyuḥ //
6.22.1.f.d: एवो ष्वस्मन्मुञ्चता व्यंहः प्र तार्यग्ने प्रतरं न आयुः ॥
6.22.1.f.m: "Even so release us from narrow distress; extend our lifespan further, O Agni!"

6.22.1.g.s: vayaḥ suparṇā upa sedurindraṃ priyamedhā ṛṣayo nādhamānāḥ /
6.22.1.g.d: वयः सुपर्णा उप सेदुरिन्द्रं प्रियमेधा ऋषयो नाधमानाः ।
6.22.1.g.m: "Like fair-winged birds the Priyamedha seers have approached Indra, supplicating: /"

6.22.1.h.m: "Dispel the darkness, fill our eyes [with light], release us who are bound as if in a snare!""

6.22.1.i.s: agna āyūṃṣi pavase dadhikrāvṇo akāriṣamiti dve mamāgne varco vihaviṣvastviti catasro 'gnīṣomāvimaṃ su ma ity eṣā /
6.22.1.i.d: अग्न आयूंषि पवसे दधिक्राव्णो अकारिषमिति द्वे ममाग्ने वर्चो विहविष्वस्त्विति चतस्रो ऽग्नीषोमाविमं सु म इत्य् एषा ।
6.22.1.i.m: [He recites] the two [verses beginning with]: "O Agni, you purify lifespans" and "I have praised Dadhikrāvan"; the four [verses beginning with]: "May my brilliance, O Agni, among the rival invocations..."; and this one: "O Agni and Soma, this [hymn of mine]..."

6.22.1.j.m: "That food of divine Savitṛ we choose, /"

6.22.1.k.m: "Best, all-sustaining, swift; may we meditate upon the share of Bhaga."

6.22.1.l.s: asya hi svayaśastaraṃ savituḥ kaccana priyam /
6.22.1.l.d: अस्य हि स्वयशस्तरं सवितुः कच्चन प्रियम् ।
6.22.1.l.m: "For none can diminish the highly famed, beloved /"

6.23.1.a.s: adyā no deva savitaḥ prajāvatsāvīḥ saubhagaṃ /
6.23.1.a.d: अद्या नो देव सवितः प्रजावत्सावीः सौभगं ।
6.23.1.a.m: "Today, O divine Savitṛ, impel for us fortune endowed with offspring; /"

6.23.1.c.m: "O divine Savitṛ, drive away all misfortunes; /"

6.23.1.e.s: anāgaso aditaye vayaṃ devasya savituḥ save /
6.23.1.e.d: अनागसो अदितये वयं देवस्य सवितुः सवे ।
6.23.1.e.m: "Sinless before Aditi, under the impulse of the divine Savitṛ, /"

6.23.1.g.s: sa hi ratnāni daśuṣe suvāti savitā bhagaḥ /
6.23.1.g.d: स हि रत्नानि दशुषे सुवाति सविता भगः ।
6.23.1.g.m: "For he, Savitṛ the distributor, impels treasures for the worshipper; /"

6.23.1.h.m: "We ask of him that manifold portion."

6.23.1.i.s: vāmamadya savitarvāmamu śvo divedive vāmamasmabhyaṃ sāvīḥ saubhagam /
6.23.1.i.d: वाममद्य सवितर्वाममु श्वो दिवेदिवे वाममस्मभ्यं सावीः सौभगम् ।
6.23.1.i.m: "Desirable things today, O Savitṛ, desirable things tomorrow, day by day impel for us desirable things and good fortune! /"

6.23.1.j.s: vāmasya hi kṣayasya deva bhūrerayā dhiyā vāmabhājaḥ syāma //
6.23.1.j.d: वामस्य हि क्षयस्य देव भूरेरया धिया वामभाजः स्याम ॥
6.23.1.j.m: "For with this prayer, O god, may we become partakers of the desirable, abundant possession."

6.23.1.k.s: dīkṣā tapo manaso mātariśvā bṛhaspatirvāco asyāḥ sa yoniḥ /
6.23.1.k.d: दीक्षा तपो मनसो मातरिश्वा बृहस्पतिर्वाचो अस्याः स योनिः ।
6.23.1.k.m: "Consecration, ascetic heat, the wind of the mind, Bṛhaspati of this speech—he is the womb; /"

6.23.1.l.s: vedāṃsi vidyā mayi santu cāravo 'gnīṣomā yaśo asmāsu dhattam //
6.23.1.l.d: वेदांसि विद्या मयि सन्तु चारवो ऽग्नीषोमा यशो अस्मासु धत्तम् ॥
6.23.1.l.m: "May the Vedas, may lovely knowledge be within me; O Agni and Soma, bestow fame upon us!"

6.23.1.m.s: agniryena virājati somo yena virājati sūryo yena virājati virāḍ yena virājati tenāhaṃ viśvataspari virājyāsamihaikavṛdityupasthāyāgnestṛṇānyapacinoti /
6.23.1.m.d: अग्निर्येन विराजति सोमो येन विराजति सूर्यो येन विराजति विराड् येन विराजति तेनाहं विश्वतस्परि विराज्यासमिहैकवृदित्युपस्थायाग्नेस्तृणान्यपचिनोति ।
6.23.1.m.m: Having worshipped [the fire] with: "By that by which Agni shines, by which Soma shines, by which Sūrya shines, by which Virāj shines—by that may I shine brightly everywhere, uniquely pre-eminent here!", he removes the grasses from the fire.

6.23.1.n.m: "He becomes radiant and endowed with spiritual luster here," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

6.24.1.a.m: When he is about to go on a journey, he gives the order: "Put fuel on the fires!"

6.24.3.a.s: paśūnnaḥ śaṃsya pāhi tānno gopāyāsmākaṃ punarāgamādityāhavanīyam /
6.24.3.a.d: पशून्नः शंस्य पाहि तान्नो गोपायास्माकं पुनरागमादित्याहवनीयम् ।
6.24.3.a.m: The āhavanīya with: "O praiseworthy one, protect our cattle; guard them for us until our return!"

6.24.3.b.s: prajāṃ no narya pāhi tāṃ no gopāyāsmākaṃ punarāgamāditi gārhapatyam /
6.24.3.b.d: प्रजां नो नर्य पाहि तां नो गोपायास्माकं पुनरागमादिति गार्हपत्यम् ।
6.24.3.b.m: The gārhapatya with: "O benevolent to men, protect our offspring; guard them for us until our return!"

6.24.3.c.s: annaṃ no budhnya pāhi tanno gopāyāsmākaṃ punarāgamādityanvāhāryapacanam
6.24.3.c.d: अन्नं नो बुध्न्य पाहि तन्नो गोपायास्माकं पुनरागमादित्यन्वाहार्यपचनम्
6.24.3.c.m: The anvāhāryapacana with: "O dweller in the deep, protect our food; guard it for us until our return!"

6.24.4.a.m: Standing between the fires, he mutters: "Do you two, Mitra and Varuṇa, guard these houses of ours;"

6.24.4.b.m: "Undestroyed, uninjured, may Pūṣan protect them until our return!"

6.24.5.a.m: Having worshipped [the fires] with the Virāj steps as before, having eaten, and about to depart on the journey, he says: "Put fuel on the fires!"

6.24.6.a.s: jvalata upatiṣṭhate prajāṃ me narya pāhi tāṃ me gopāyāsmākaṃ punarāgamāditi gārhapatyam /
6.24.6.a.d: ज्वलत उपतिष्ठते प्रजां मे नर्य पाहि तां मे गोपायास्माकं पुनरागमादिति गार्हपत्यम् ।
6.24.6.a.m: While they are blazing, he stands worshipping the gārhapatya with: "O benevolent to men, protect my offspring; guard them for me until our return!"

6.24.6.b.s: annaṃ me budhnya pāhi tanme gopāyāsmākaṃ punarāgamādityanvāhāryapacanam /
6.24.6.b.d: अन्नं मे बुध्न्य पाहि तन्मे गोपायास्माकं पुनरागमादित्यन्वाहार्यपचनम् ।
6.24.6.b.m: The anvāhāryapacana with: "O dweller in the deep, protect my food; guard it for me until our return!"

6.24.6.c.s: paśūnme śaṃsya pāhi tānme gopāyāsmākaṃ punarāgamād ity āhavanīyam
6.24.6.c.d: पशून्मे शंस्य पाहि तान्मे गोपायास्माकं पुनरागमाद् इत्य् आहवनीयम्
6.24.6.c.m: The āhavanīya with: "O praiseworthy one, protect my cattle; guard them for me until our return!"

6.24.7.a.s: mama nāma prathamaṃ jātaveda iti ca
6.24.7.a.d: मम नाम प्रथमं जातवेद इति च
6.24.7.a.m: And [with]: "My name is the foremost, O Jātavedas..."

6.24.8.a.s: vāgyato 'bhipravrajati mā pragāma patho vayaṃ mā yajñādindra sominaḥ /
6.24.8.a.d: वाग्यतो ऽभिप्रव्रजति मा प्रगाम पथो वयं मा यज्ञादिन्द्र सोमिनः ।
6.24.8.a.m: Restraining his speech, he sets out, [saying]: "May we not stray from the path, nor from the sacrifice, O Indra, we who possess Soma! /"

6.24.8.c.m: "Lead us higher and higher, O Agni, offered to with ghee! /"

6.24.8.d.m: "Unite [us] with increase of wealth, and make us many with offspring!"

6.24.9.a.m: Away from the fires, he releases his speech.

6.25.1.a.m: While dwelling away, at the proper time, facing the fire-enclosure, he mutters the worship of the fires:

6.25.2.a.s: ihaiva santatra sato vo agnayaḥ prāṇena vācā manasā bibharmi /
6.25.2.a.d: इहैव सन्तत्र सतो वो अग्नयः प्राणेन वाचा मनसा बिभर्मि ।
6.25.2.a.m: "Being right here, I bear you who are there, O fires, with breath, speech, and mind; /"

6.25.2.b.s: tiro mā santamāyurmā prahāsījjyotiṣā vo vaiśvānareṇopatiṣṭha iti yadyanupasthāya pravasedetayaivopatiṣṭhate
6.25.2.b.d: तिरो मा सन्तमायुर्मा प्रहासीज्ज्योतिषा वो वैश्वानरेणोपतिष्ठ इति यद्यनुपस्थाय प्रवसेदेतयैवोपतिष्ठते
6.25.2.b.m: "May lifespan not abandon me who am away from sight; I approach you with the Vaiśvānara light." If he should depart on a journey without having worshipped [them], he approaches [them] with this very [formula].

6.25.3.a.m: Having procured fuel sticks, he returns.

6.25.4.a.s: yathā ha vā itaṃ pitaraṃ proṣivāṃsaṃ putrāḥ pratyādhāvantyevaṃ ha vā etamagnayaḥ pratyādhāvanti /
6.25.4.a.d: यथा ह वा इतं पितरं प्रोषिवांसं पुत्राः प्रत्याधावन्त्येवं ह वा एतमग्नयः प्रत्याधावन्ति ।
6.25.4.a.m: "Just as indeed sons run out to meet their father who has returned from a journey, even so indeed the fires run out to meet him;"

6.25.4.b.s: sa śakalāndārūṇi vāharanneti yathaiva tatputrebhya āharanneti /
6.25.4.b.d: स शकलान्दारूणि वाहरन्नेति यथैव तत्पुत्रेभ्य आहरन्नेति ।
6.25.4.b.m: "He returns bringing splinters or firewood, just as if bringing [gifts] to his sons;"

6.25.4.c.m: "It is proper [for him to do] that," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

6.25.5.a.m: From afar, within sight of the fires, he restrains his speech.

6.25.6.a.m: If a king, a father, or a teacher should come between him and the fires, as long as the roof [of the fires] is visible, he should not pay heed to him.

6.25.7.b.m: "O Agni, may we, your neighbours, not come to harm! /"

6.25.7.c.m: "Homage be to you, the bountiful; homage to you, the approachable! /"

6.25.7.d.s: agne śumbhasva tanvaḥ saṃ mā rayyā sṛjetyabhaiti
6.25.7.d.d: अग्ने शुम्भस्व तन्वः सं मा रय्या सृजेत्यभैति
6.25.7.d.m: "O Agni, beautify your bodies; unite me with wealth!"—saying this, he approaches.

6.25.10.a.s: paśūnnaḥ śaṃsyājūgupastānnaḥ punardehītyāhavanīyamabhiprānyāgne sahasrākṣa śatamūrdhañchataṃ te prāṇāḥ sahasramapānāḥ /
6.25.10.a.d: पशून्नः शंस्याजूगुपस्तान्नः पुनर्देहीत्याहवनीयमभिप्रान्याग्ने सहस्राक्ष शतमूर्धञ्छतं ते प्राणाः सहस्रमपानाः ।
6.25.10.a.m: With: "O praiseworthy one, you have guarded our cattle; give them back to us!"—having breathed over the āhavanīya, [he continues]: "O Agni of a thousand eyes, hundred heads, a hundred are your out-breaths, a thousand your in-breaths; /"

6.25.10.b.s: tvaṃ sāhasrasya rāya īśiṣe sahasradhārasya payasaḥ /
6.25.10.b.d: त्वं साहस्रस्य राय ईशिषे सहस्रधारस्य पयसः ।
6.25.10.b.m: "You rule over thousandfold wealth, over milk flowing in a thousand streams;"

6.25.10.c.s: tasya no rāsva tasya te bhakṣīya tasya te vayaṃ bhūyiṣṭhabhājo bhūyāsmetyāhavanīyam
6.25.10.c.d: तस्य नो रास्व तस्य ते भक्षीय तस्य ते वयं भूयिष्ठभाजो भूयास्मेत्याहवनीयम्
6.25.10.c.m: "Grant us of that; of that may I partake; may we possess the most abundant share of that!" [speaking] to the āhavanīya.

6.26.1.a.s: prajāṃ no naryājūgupastāṃ naḥ punardehīti gārhapatyamabhiprāṇyāgne gṛhapate sugṛhapatirahaṃ tvayā gṛhapatinā bhṛyāsaṃ sugṛhapatirmayā tvaṃ gṛhapatinā bhūyāḥ /
6.26.1.a.d: प्रजां नो नर्याजूगुपस्तां नः पुनर्देहीति गार्हपत्यमभिप्राण्याग्ने गृहपते सुगृहपतिरहं त्वया गृहपतिना भृयासं सुगृहपतिर्मया त्वं गृहपतिना भूयाः ।
6.26.1.a.m: "O Narya, you guarded our offspring; give them back to us!"—having exhaled over the gārhapatya—"O Agni, householder, may I be a good householder with you as householder; may you be a good householder with me as householder!

6.26.1.b.s: śataṃ himā dvā yū rādhāṃsītsaṃpṛñcānāvasaṃpṛñcānau tanva iti gārhapatyam
6.26.1.b.d: शतं हिमा द्वा यू राधांसीत्संपृञ्चानावसंपृञ्चानौ तन्व इति गार्हपत्यम्
6.26.1.b.m: A hundred winters, two beings uniting wealth, not uniting our bodies!" [speaking] to the gārhapatya.

6.26.2.a.s: annaṃ no budhnyājūgupastannaḥ punardehītyanvāhāryapacanamabhiprāṇyāntarāgnī tiṣṭhañjapati yathā pravatsyadupathāne
6.26.2.a.d: अन्नं नो बुध्न्याजूगुपस्तन्नः पुनर्देहीत्यन्वाहार्यपचनमभिप्राण्यान्तराग्नी तिष्ठञ्जपति यथा प्रवत्स्यदुपथाने
6.26.2.a.m: "O Budhnya, you guarded our food; give it back to us!"—having exhaled over the anvāhāryapacana, standing between the fires, he murmurs as in the attendance [upon the fires] before going on a journey.

6.26.3.a.m: He modifies the formula: "they both have guarded, have protected."

6.26.4.a.s: mama nāma tava ca jātaveda iti catasṛbhirāhavanīyam
6.26.4.a.d: मम नाम तव च जातवेद इति चतसृभिराहवनीयम्
6.26.4.a.m: With four [verses beginning with] "My name and yours, O Jātavedas," [he attends upon] the āhavanīya.

6.26.5.a.s: prajāṃ me naryājūgupastāṃ me punardehīti gārhapatyamabhyapānyānnaṃ me budhnyājūgupastanme punardehītyanvāhāryapacanamabhyapānya paśūn me śaṃsyājūgupastān me punardehītyāhavanīyamabhyapānya pūrvavadvirāṭkramairupatiṣṭhate /
6.26.5.a.d: प्रजां मे नर्याजूगुपस्तां मे पुनर्देहीति गार्हपत्यमभ्यपान्यान्नं मे बुध्न्याजूगुपस्तन्मे पुनर्देहीत्यन्वाहार्यपचनमभ्यपान्य पशून् मे शंस्याजूगुपस्तान् मे पुनर्देहीत्याहवनीयमभ्यपान्य पूर्ववद्विराट्क्रमैरुपतिष्ठते ।
6.26.5.a.m: "O Narya, you guarded my offspring; give them back to me!"—having inhaled over the gārhapatya; "O Budhnya, you guarded my food; give it back to me!"—having inhaled over the anvāhāryapacana; "O Śaṃsya, you guarded my cattle; give them back to me!"—having inhaled over the āhavanīya, he attends [upon the fires] with the virāj steps as before.

6.26.5.b.m: He modifies the formula: "you have guarded."

6.26.6.a.m: As in the attendance upon the fires, here [occurs] the attendance with kindling sticks and upon the quarters.

6.26.7.a.s: navamīṃ cedatipravasenmitro janānyātayati prajānanniti maitryopasthāya mano jyotirjuṣatāmityāhutiṃ juhuyāt
6.26.7.a.d: नवमीं चेदतिप्रवसेन्मित्रो जनान्यातयति प्रजानन्निति मैत्र्योपस्थाय मनो ज्योतिर्जुषतामित्याहुतिं जुहुयात्
6.26.7.a.m: If he stays away beyond the ninth [day], having attended [upon the fire] with the verse to Mitra: "Mitra, knowing, arranges the people," he should offer the oblation: "May the mind enjoy the light."

6.26.8.a.m: Kindling stick, oblation, attendance—thus some teach the order.

6.27.1.a.m: Regarding this they say: "The fire is not to be attended upon. Who will awaken an elder who is fast asleep?

6.27.1.b.s: abhayaṃkarābhayaṃ me kuru svasti me 'stvabhayaṃ me astvityeva brūyāt /
6.27.1.b.d: अभयंकराभयं मे कुरु स्वस्ति मे ऽस्त्वभयं मे अस्त्वित्येव ब्रूयात् ।
6.27.1.b.m: One should merely say: 'O creator of fearlessness, make fearlessness for me; let there be well-being for me, let there be fearlessness for me!'"

6.27.1.c.m: With reference to the attendance before going on a journey and the attendance upon returning, the Vājasaneyins recite [this].

6.27.2.a.s: namo vo 'stu pravatsyāmi namo vo 'stu prāvātsyamiti bahvṛcāḥ
6.27.2.a.d: नमो वो ऽस्तु प्रवत्स्यामि नमो वो ऽस्तु प्रावात्स्यमिति बह्वृचाः
6.27.2.a.m: "Homage be to you; I am going on a journey; homage be to you; I have returned from a journey"—so [say] the Bahvṛcas.

6.27.3.a.s: gṛhā mā bibhīta mā vepiḍhvamūrjaṃ bibhrata emasi /
6.27.3.a.d: गृहा मा बिभीत मा वेपिढ्वमूर्जं बिभ्रत एमसि ।
6.27.3.a.m: "O houses, do not fear, do not tremble, bearing strength we come.

6.27.3.b.s: ūrjaṃ bibhradvaḥ suvaniḥ sumedhā gṛhānaimi manasā modamanaḥ //
6.27.3.b.d: ऊर्जं बिभ्रद्वः सुवनिः सुमेधा गृहानैमि मनसा मोदमनः ॥
6.27.3.b.m: Bearing strength, well-winning, wise, I come to the houses, rejoicing in mind.

6.27.3.c.m: Of which he thinks when dwelling away, in which there is much goodwill,

6.27.3.d.m: We invoke the houses; let them know us, knowing [them].

6.27.3.e.m: Invited are friends of abundant wealth, of sweet rejoicings;

6.27.3.f.s: ariṣṭāḥ sarvapūruṣā gṛhā naḥ santu sarvadā //
6.27.3.f.d: अरिष्टाः सर्वपूरुषा गृहा नः सन्तु सर्वदा ॥
6.27.3.f.m: Uninjured, with all people, may our houses always be!

6.27.3.g.m: Invited here are cows, invited are goats and sheep;

6.27.3.h.s: atho annasya kīlāla upahūto gṛheṣu na iti gṛhānabhyeti
6.27.3.h.d: अथो अन्नस्य कीलाल उपहूतो गृहेषु न इति गृहानभ्येति
6.27.3.h.m: And the nourishing juice of food is invited into our houses!"—with this he approaches the houses.

6.27.4.a.s: kṣemāya vaḥ śantyai prapadye śivaṃ śagmaṃ śaṃyoḥ śaṃyoriti praviśati
6.27.4.a.d: क्षेमाय वः शन्त्यै प्रपद्ये शिवं शग्मं शंयोः शंयोरिति प्रविशति
6.27.4.a.m: "For your safety, for your peace I enter, auspicious, beneficial, happiness and joy!"—with this he enters.

6.27.5.a.s: ūrjaṃ bibhradvaḥ sumanāḥ sumedhā gṛhānāgāṃ manasā modamānaḥ /
6.27.5.a.d: ऊर्जं बिभ्रद्वः सुमनाः सुमेधा गृहानागां मनसा मोदमानः ।
6.27.5.a.m: "Bearing strength, benevolent, wise, I have come to the houses, rejoicing in mind.

6.27.5.b.s: irāṃ vahanto ghṛtamukṣamāṇāsteṣvahaṃ sumanāhā saṃviśāmīti praviśya japati /
6.27.5.b.d: इरां वहन्तो घृतमुक्षमाणास्तेष्वहं सुमनाहा संविशामीति प्रविश्य जपति ।
6.27.5.b.m: Carrying food, sprinkling ghee, in them I benevolence enter"—having entered, he murmurs [this],

6.28.1.a.m: Intending to set out with his household, he offers the Vāstoṣpatīya oblation.

6.28.2.a.m: Before it is offered, they load the belongings onto the carts.

6.28.4.a.m: If there should be an ox-cart, they should drive it forward first, or set it aside.

6.28.5.a.s: yatra saṃhitā rātrīrvasetpañca sapta nava daśa vā tatprayāsyañjuhuyāt
6.28.5.a.d: यत्र संहिता रात्रीर्वसेत्पञ्च सप्त नव दश वा तत्प्रयास्यञ्जुहुयात्
6.28.5.a.m: Where he intends to stay continuous nights, five, seven, nine, or ten, intending to set out from there, he should offer [it].

6.28.6.a.m: Or, having stayed for a period of nine nights, returning, having stayed for one [night], intending to set out, he should offer [it].

6.28.7.a.m: The right [draft animal] is yoked, the left is unyoked.

6.28.7.b.s: api vāgniṣṭhasya dakṣiṇo yuktaḥ savyasya yoktraṃ parihṛtam /
6.28.7.b.d: अपि वाग्निष्ठस्य दक्षिणो युक्तः सव्यस्य योक्त्रं परिहृतम् ।
6.28.7.b.m: Or rather, the right [animal] of the [cart] stationed by the fire is yoked, and the yoke-strap of the left is placed around it.

6.28.8.a.s: vāstoṣpata ityanudrutyottarayā gārhapatye hutvāvakṣāṇāni saṃprakṣāpya pṛthagaraṇīṣvagnīnsamāropayate ye dhāryante
6.28.8.a.d: वास्तोष्पत इत्यनुद्रुत्योत्तरया गार्हपत्ये हुत्वावक्षाणानि संप्रक्षाप्य पृथगरणीष्वग्नीन्समारोपयते ये धार्यन्ते
6.28.8.a.m: Having repeated [the verse beginning with] "O Vāstoṣpati," having offered [an oblation] in the gārhapatya with the next [verse], and having quenched the burning coals, he causes the fires that are maintained to ascend separately onto the churning sticks.

6.28.9.a.m: Holding the two churning sticks over the fire, he murmurs: "This is your seasonal womb."

6.28.10.a.m: Or the sacrificer himself causes [them] to ascend into himself.

6.28.11.a.s: yā te agne yajñiyā tanūstayehyārohātmātmānamacchā vasūni kṛṇvannasme naryā purūṇi /
6.28.11.a.d: या ते अग्ने यज्ञिया तनूस्तयेह्यारोहात्मात्मानमच्छा वसूनि कृण्वन्नस्मे नर्या पुरूणि ।
6.28.11.a.m: "Which is your sacrificial body, O Agni, come with that, mount into my breath, onto myself, making for us many manly treasures.

6.28.11.b.s: yajño bhūtvā yajñamāsīda svāṃ yoniṃ jātavedo bhuva ājāyamānaḥ sa kṣaya ehīti hastaṃ pratāpya mukhāyāharate
6.28.11.b.d: यज्ञो भूत्वा यज्ञमासीद स्वां योनिं जातवेदो भुव आजायमानः स क्षय एहीति हस्तं प्रताप्य मुखायाहरते
6.28.11.b.m: Having become the sacrifice, sit upon the sacrifice, your own womb, O Jātavedas, being born from the earth, as that home, come!"—having warmed his hands, he draws [them] to his face.

6.28.12.a.s: vāsa upāvaroha jātavedaḥ punastvaṃ devebhyo havyaṃ vaha naḥ prajānan /
6.28.12.a.d: वास उपावरोह जातवेदः पुनस्त्वं देवेभ्यो हव्यं वह नः प्रजानन् ।
6.28.12.a.m: "Descend, O Jātavedas, to the dwelling; again do you, knowing, carry the oblation to the gods for us.

6.28.12.b.s: āyuḥ prajāṃ rayimasmāsu dhehyajasro dīdihi no duroṇa iti laukake 'gnāvaupāvarohayati
6.28.12.b.d: आयुः प्रजां रयिमस्मासु धेह्यजस्रो दीदिहि नो दुरोण इति लौकके ऽग्नावौपावरोहयति
6.28.12.b.m: Place life, offspring, wealth in us; unceasing, shine in our home!"—with this he causes [the fire] to descend into a worldly fire.

6.28.13.a.m: Or, having caused it to descend from the two churning sticks, he should churn [it].

6.28.14.a.s: yadaraṇyoḥ samārūḍhaḥ syānnirvartamāna etaṃ mantraṃ japet
6.28.14.a.d: यदरण्योः समारूढः स्यान्निर्वर्तमान एतं मन्त्रं जपेत्
6.28.14.a.m: If it was mounted onto the two churning sticks, turning back he should murmur this formula:

6.29.1.a.s: idaṃ śreyo 'vasānaṃ yadāgāṃ syone me dyāvāpṛthivī abhūtām /
6.29.1.a.d: इदं श्रेयो ऽवसानं यदागां स्योने मे द्यावापृथिवी अभूताम् ।
6.29.1.a.m: "This better settlement which I have reached, comfortable have heaven and earth been to me.

6.29.1.b.m: Free from disease may the intermediate regions be for me!

6.29.1.c.m: With cattle, with wealth, with horses, with men, with gold, with heroes, svāhā!"—having settled, he offers [this].

6.29.2.a.m: One who has established the fires should not eat of the new [grain] without having performed the Āgrayaṇa sacrifice.

6.29.3.a.m: He should sacrifice of the first ripe crops: of rice, of barley, [or] of millet.

6.29.4.a.m: On a new-moon day or on a full-moon day.

6.29.7.a.m: At the time of apportioning, he apportions an eight-potsherd [cake] for Agni from old rice.

6.29.8.a.m: "Just as one yokes the untrained with the trained, such is that," so is it known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

6.29.9.a.m: "With whatever sacrifice he may desire to succeed, he should certainly make there an eight-potsherd [cake] for Agni," so is it known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

6.29.10.a.s: navānāmitarāṇyaindrāgnaṃ dvādaśakapālamāgnendraṃ vā vaiśvadevaṃ payasi caruṃ saumyaṃ śyāmākaṃ caruṃ dyāvāpṛthivyamekakapālam
6.29.10.a.d: नवानामितराण्यैन्द्राग्नं द्वादशकपालमाग्नेन्द्रं वा वैश्वदेवं पयसि चरुं सौम्यं श्यामाकं चरुं द्यावापृथिव्यमेककपालम्
6.29.10.a.m: From the new [grains, he apportions] the others: a twelve-potsherd [cake] for Indra-Agni or for Agni-Indra, a mess of cooked grain in milk for the Viśvedevas, a mess of cooked millet for Soma, and a single-potsherd [cake] for Heaven and Earth.

6.29.11.a.m: Some teach the [cake] for Heaven and Earth [to come] before the one for Soma.

6.29.12.a.m: The sacrificial substance is apportioned, placed near, [and] unbesprinkled.

6.29.12.b.m: Then he offers the five ghee-oblations with [the verse beginning with] "To him with a hundred weapons, with a hundred virilities."

6.29.14.a.m: he proceeds with the rites starting with sprinkling.

6.29.15.a.m: There is one mortar and pestle, or [one] for each kind of grain.

6.29.16.a.m: For all [grains] the haviṣkṛt-call and the formula for pounding are [used].

6.29.18.a.m: Having poured out the last [portion], he releases speech.

6.29.19.a.m: This is the rule for other different grains when combined together.

6.29.20.a.m: At the time of decoration, he fills the one-pot-sherd [cake] with clarified butter,

6.29.21.a.m: or he places it [on the altar], making its upper surface visible.

6.29.22.a.m: At the time of the main offering, having lifted it up and placed it upon the barhis, having spread an underlayer in the juhu, laid [it down], brought along the remaining ghee, and basted it, he offers silently.

6.30.1.a.m: He should make the entire offering without turning it around, straight, firmly set, not with his hand.

6.30.2.a.d: यदि हुतः पर्यावर्तेत स्रुचो ऽग्रेण कल्पयेत्
6.30.2.a.m: If it should turn over after being offered, he should arrange it with the tip of the sruc,

6.30.4.a.m: When a boon has been given, it should be adjusted.

6.30.5.a.m: Having placed it and basted it, it should be offered again, say some.

6.30.6.a.s: api vā naikakapālaṃ kurvītājyena dyāvāpṛthivī yajeta
6.30.6.a.d: अपि वा नैककपालं कुर्वीताज्येन द्यावापृथिवी यजेत
6.30.6.a.m: Or indeed, he should not prepare a one-pot-sherd [cake]; he should sacrifice to Heaven and Earth with clarified butter.

6.30.7.a.s: ye prācīnamekāṣṭakāyā vatsā jāyante teṣāṃ prathamajaṃ dadāti /
6.30.7.a.d: ये प्राचीनमेकाष्टकाया वत्सा जायन्ते तेषां प्रथमजं ददाति ।
6.30.7.a.m: He gives the firstborn of the calves that are born before the Ekāṣṭakā.

6.30.8.a.s: bhadrānnaḥ śreyaḥ samanaiṣṭa devā iti yajamānabhāgaṃ prāśnāti
6.30.8.a.d: भद्रान्नः श्रेयः समनैष्ट देवा इति यजमानभागं प्राश्नाति
6.30.8.a.m: With: 'The gods have led us together from good to better,' he consumes the sacrificer's share.

6.30.9.a.s: sarveṣāṃ vā bhakṣāṇāṃ mantravatāṃ pratyāmnāyaḥ syāt
6.30.9.a.d: सर्वेषां वा भक्षाणां मन्त्रवतां प्रत्याम्नायः स्यात्
6.30.9.a.m: Or it may be a substitute for all portions accompanied by formulas.

6.30.10.a.s: agniḥ prathāmaḥ prāśnātu sa hi veda yathā haviḥ /
6.30.10.a.d: अग्निः प्रथामः प्राश्नातु स हि वेद यथा हविः ।
6.30.10.a.m: Agni must eat first, for he knows the oblation as it is;

6.30.10.b.m: May he, who belongs to all people, make the plants auspicious for us — [so he consumes the portion] of the millets.

6.30.11.a.m: The rite stands completed in the established manner.

6.30.12.a.m: Or he may perform the Āgrayaṇa sacrifice in conjunction with the new-moon day or the full-moon day.

6.30.13.a.m: Or he may perform the New-moon or Full-moon sacrifice with new grains.

6.30.14.a.s: api vāgnihotrīṃ vrīhistambaṃ yavastambaṃ vā grāsayitvā tasyāḥ payasā sāyaṃprātar juhuyāt
6.30.14.a.d: अपि वाग्निहोत्रीं व्रीहिस्तम्बं यवस्तम्बं वा ग्रासयित्वा तस्याः पयसा सायंप्रातर् जुहुयात्
6.30.14.a.m: Or, having fed a clump of rice or a clump of barley to the agnihotra cow, he may offer [the agnihotra] evening and morning with her milk.

6.30.15.a.s: api vā navānāṃ yavāgvā sāyaṃprātar juhuyāt
6.30.15.a.d: अपि वा नवानां यवाग्वा सायंप्रातर् जुहुयात्
6.30.15.a.m: Or he may offer [the agnihotra] evening and morning with barley-gruel from the new [grains].

6.30.16.a.s: api vā navānāṃ gārhapatye sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvāhavanīye juhuyādāgrayaṇadevatābhyaḥ sviṣṭakṛccaturthābhyaḥ
6.30.16.a.d: अपि वा नवानां गार्हपत्ये स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वाहवनीये जुहुयादाग्रयणदेवताभ्यः स्विष्टकृच्चतुर्थाभ्यः
6.30.16.a.m: Or, having cooked a mess of boiled grains from the new [grains] on the gārhapatya, he may offer it on the āhavanīya to the deities of the Āgrayaṇa, with the sviṣṭakṛt as the fourth.

6.30.17.a.s: api vā navānāṃ catuḥśarāvam odanaṃ paktvā caturo brāhmaṇān bhojayet
6.30.17.a.d: अपि वा नवानां चतुःशरावम् ओदनं पक्त्वा चतुरो ब्राह्मणान् भोजयेत्
6.30.17.a.m: Or, having cooked four dishes of boiled rice from the new [grains], he should feed four brahmins.

6.30.19.a.m: In that [rite] there are no [cakes] for Agni and of millet.

6.30.20.a.s: ya ūrdhvamekāṣṭakāyā vatsā jāyante teṣāṃ prathamajaṃ dadāti //
6.30.20.a.d: य ऊर्ध्वमेकाष्टकाया वत्सा जायन्ते तेषां प्रथमजं ददाति ॥
6.30.20.a.m: He gives the firstborn of the calves that are born after the Ekāṣṭakā.

6.30.20.b.s: etamu tyaṃ madhunā saṃyutaṃ yavaṃ sarasvatyā adhi manāvacarkṛṣuḥ indra āsītsīrapatiḥ śatakratuḥ kīnāśā āsanmarutaḥ sudānava iti yajamānabhāgaṃ prāśnāti //
6.30.20.b.d: एतमु त्यं मधुना संयुतं यवं सरस्वत्या अधि मनावचर्कृषुः इन्द्र आसीत्सीरपतिः शतक्रतुः कीनाशा आसन्मरुतः सुदानव इति यजमानभागं प्राश्नाति ॥
6.30.20.b.m: With: 'This barley, mixed with honey, which they plowed along the Sarasvatī for Manu, Indra was the lord of the plow, Śatakratu, and the bounteous Maruts were the plowmen,' he consumes the sacrificer's share.

6.30.20.c.s: sarveṣāṃ vā bhakṣāṇāṃ mantravatāṃ pratyāmnāyaḥ syāt
6.30.20.c.d: सर्वेषां वा भक्षाणां मन्त्रवतां प्रत्याम्नायः स्यात्
6.30.20.c.m: Or it may be a substitute for all portions accompanied by formulas.

6.30.21.a.m: The rite stands completed in the established manner.

6.31.1.a.s: yadi nānātantrāṃ śyāmākeṣṭiṃ kurvīta śyāmākānuddhartavā iti saṃpreṣyati
6.31.1.a.d: यदि नानातन्त्रां श्यामाकेष्टिं कुर्वीत श्यामाकानुद्धर्तवा इति संप्रेष्यति
6.31.1.a.m: If he performs the millet sacrifice as a separate ritual procedure, he gives the order: 'Take out the millets!'

6.31.2.a.m: For it there are seventeen sāmidhenī verses.

6.31.4.a.s: tvam agne saprathā asi juṣṭo hotā vareṇyaḥ /
6.31.4.a.d: त्वम् अग्ने सप्रथा असि जुष्टो होता वरेण्यः ।
6.31.4.a.m: You, O Agni, are wide-spread, the agreeable hotṛ, the worthy of choice;

6.31.4.b.m: through you they extend the sacrifice;

6.31.4.c.m: [and] 'Soma, those that are delightful to you' — [these are] the two containing the word *sat*.

6.31.4.d.s: preddho agna imo agna iti virājau
6.31.4.d.d: प्रेद्धो अग्न इमो अग्न इति विराजौ
6.31.4.d.m: 'Kindled forward, O Agni,' [and] 'These, O Agni' — [these are] the two Virāj verses.

6.31.5.a.s: vāso dakṣiṇā dadhimantho madhumantho madhuparko madhugluntho babhrurvā piṅgalaḥ
6.31.5.a.d: वासो दक्षिणा दधिमन्थो मधुमन्थो मधुपर्को मधुग्लुन्थो बभ्रुर्वा पिङ्गलः
6.31.5.a.m: The sacrificial gift is a garment, a curd-drink, a honey-drink, madhuparka, a lump of honey, or a brown or reddish-brown [cow].

6.31.6.a.m: The rite stands completed in the established manner.

6.31.7.a.d: हरितयवशाकशमीधान्यानां नवानां फलानामनिष्टे ऽपि प्राशने याथाकामी
6.31.7.a.m: With green barley, vegetables, and leguminous grains, as well as new fruits, there is freedom of choice regarding eating, even if no sacrifice has been performed.

6.31.8.a.m: Some teach a sacrifice of bamboo-barley.

6.31.9.a.m: When the bamboo-barley is ripe, he gives the order: 'Take out the bamboo-barley!'

6.31.10.a.m: For it there is this very procedure and this deity,

6.31.11.a.m: or it is dedicated to Agni, to Mitra-Varuṇa, or to Prajāpati.

6.31.12.a.s: sa pratnavaditi dve dhāyye catasra ājyabhāgayordaśa haviṣāṃ dve sviṣṭakṛtaḥ
6.31.12.a.d: स प्रत्नवदिति द्वे धाय्ये चतस्र आज्यभागयोर्दश हविषां द्वे स्विष्टकृतः
6.31.12.a.m: 'Like of old...' are the two dhāyyā verses, four for the two ājyabhāgas, ten for the oblations, and two for the sviṣṭakṛt.

6.31.13.a.s: vrīhibhiriṣṭvā vrīhibhireva yajetā yavebhyo darśapūrṇamāsāvevaṃ yavairā vrīhibhyo 'pi vā vrīhibhirevobhatraite ha vai sūpacaratamā bhavantīti bahvṛcabrāhmaṇam
6.31.13.a.d: व्रीहिभिरिष्ट्वा व्रीहिभिरेव यजेता यवेभ्यो दर्शपूर्णमासावेवं यवैरा व्रीहिभ्यो ऽपि वा व्रीहिभिरेवोभत्रैते ह वै सूपचरतमा भवन्तीति बह्वृचब्राह्मणम्
6.31.13.a.m: Having sacrificed with rice, he should sacrifice only with rice for the New and Full Moon sacrifices until the barley; likewise with barley until the rice; or he should sacrifice only with rice in both cases, for 'these indeed are the easiest to handle,' says the Bahvṛca Brāhmaṇa.

6.31.14.a.s: varṣāsu śyāmākairyajeta śaradi vrīhibhirvasante yavairyathartu veṇuyavair iti vijñāyate
6.31.14.a.d: वर्षासु श्यामाकैर्यजेत शरदि व्रीहिभिर्वसन्ते यवैर्यथर्तु वेणुयवैर् इति विज्ञायते
6.31.14.a.m: In the rainy season he should sacrifice with millet, in the autumn with rice, in the spring with barley, and according to the season with bamboo-barley — so it is understood.

7.1.1.a.m: One who performs the animal sacrifice conquers all worlds.

7.1.2.a.s: tena yakṣyamāṇo 'māvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ vā ṣaḍḍhotāraṃ manasānudrutyāhavanīye sagrahaṃ juhoti sūryaṃ te cakṣur iti
7.1.2.a.d: तेन यक्ष्यमाणो ऽमावास्यायां पौर्णमास्यां वा षड्ढोतारं मनसानुद्रुत्याहवनीये सग्रहं जुहोति सूर्यं ते चक्षुर् इति
7.1.2.a.m: Intending to sacrifice with it on the new-moon day or on the full-moon day, having recited the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ formula in his mind, he makes an offering with a graha on the āhavanīya with: 'The sun is your eye...'

7.1.3.a.m: He assigns an eleven-pot-sherd cake to Agni-Viṣṇu.

7.1.4.a.m: It is a substitute for adding fuel to the fires.

7.1.5.a.m: The rite stands completed in the established manner.

7.1.7.a.s: uru viṣṇo vikramasveti sruveṇāhavanīye yūpāhutiṃ juhoti
7.1.7.a.d: उरु विष्णो विक्रमस्वेति स्रुवेणाहवनीये यूपाहुतिं जुहोति
7.1.7.a.m: With the spoon, he offers the libation for the sacrificial post on the āhavanīya with: 'Stride wide, O Viṣṇu...'

7.1.8.a.m: Or [he offers an oblation] with the dipping-spoon filled four times.

7.1.10.a.m: Having recited a verse addressed to Viṣṇu, [the sacrificial post] is to be fetched.

7.1.12.a.m: Or having churned out fire in the vicinity of the sacrificial post, he should offer into that.

7.1.13.a.m: The adhvaryu takes the dipping spoon and the remainder of the clarified butter.

7.1.15.a.m: The trees fit for a sacrificial post are palāśa, khadira, bilva, and rauhītaka.

7.1.16.a.m: A palāśa post [is taken] by one desiring spiritual luster or desiring sacrifice.

7.1.16.b.m: A khadira post by one desiring heaven or desiring vigor.

7.1.16.c.m: A bilva post by one desiring food or desiring holy splendor.

7.1.16.d.m: A rauhītaka post by one desiring offspring or desiring eyesight.

7.1.17.a.s: same jātam aśākhājaṃ bahuparṇaśākham apratiśuṣkāgram asuṣiram avyāvṛttam aghūrṇam ṛjum ūrdhvam ūrdhvaśakalam agra īṣadupāvanataṃ prāg udak pratyag
7.1.17.a.d: समे जातम् अशाखाजं बहुपर्णशाखम् अप्रतिशुष्काग्रम् असुषिरम् अव्यावृत्तम् अघूर्णम् ऋजुम् ऊर्ध्वम् ऊर्ध्वशकलम् अग्र ईषदुपावनतं प्राग् उदक् प्रत्यग्
7.1.17.a.m: [It should be a tree] growing on level ground, not born from branches, having many leaves and branches, its top not dried up, not hollow, not twisted, not wavering, straight, standing upright, with bark turning upwards, slightly inclined at the top towards the east, north, or west.

7.1.18.a.m: [The tree for one] of whom he might desire 'May he be unstable' has been explained.

7.1.19.a.s: atikramya yūpyān yaṃ joṣayate tam abhimantrayate
7.1.19.a.d: अतिक्रम्य यूप्यान् यं जोषयते तम् अभिमन्त्रयते
7.1.19.a.m: Having passed by other trees fit for a post, he addresses the one he selects,

7.2.2.a.s: athainam upaspṛśati taṃ tvā juṣe vaiṣṇavaṃ devayajyāyā iti
7.2.2.a.d: अथैनम् उपस्पृशति तं त्वा जुषे वैष्णवं देवयज्याया इति
7.2.2.a.m: Then he touches it with: 'Thee, belonging to Viṣṇu, I accept for the sacrifice to the gods.'

7.2.3.a.s: devas tvā savitā madhvānaktv iti sruveṇa sarvato mūlaṃ paryaṇakti
7.2.3.a.d: देवस् त्वा सविता मध्वानक्त्व् इति स्रुवेण सर्वतो मूलं पर्यणक्ति
7.2.3.a.m: With the dipping spoon he anoints the base all around with: 'May the god Savitṛ anoint thee with honey.'

7.2.4.a.s: oṣadhe trāyasvainam ity ūrdhvāgraṃ darbham antardhāya svadhite mainaṃ hiṃsīr iti svadhitinā praharati
7.2.4.a.d: ओषधे त्रायस्वैनम् इत्य् ऊर्ध्वाग्रं दर्भम् अन्तर्धाय स्वधिते मैनं हिंसीर् इति स्वधितिना प्रहरति
7.2.4.a.m: Having placed a blade of darbha grass pointing upwards between [the axe and the tree] with: 'O plant, protect him,' he strikes with the axe with: 'O axe, do not harm him!'

7.2.5.a.m: He takes the chip that flies off first.

7.2.6.a.m: He should cut it at ankle-height, at knee-height, or so that it does not catch an axle.

7.2.7.a.s: divam agreṇa mā lekhīr iti prāñcaṃ pātayaty udañcaṃ prāñcam udañcaṃ vā
7.2.7.a.d: दिवम् अग्रेण मा लेखीर् इति प्राञ्चं पातयत्य् उदञ्चं प्राञ्चम् उदञ्चं वा
7.2.7.a.m: With: 'Do not scratch the sky with thy tip,' he causes it to fall towards the east, north, or northeast.

7.2.8.a.m: He offers into the stump with: 'O tree, grow with a hundred branches!'

7.2.9.a.s: sahasravalśā vi vayaṃ ruhemety ātmānaṃ pratyabhimṛśya yaṃ tvāyaṃ svadhitir ity anvagram adgāṃś chinatti
7.2.9.a.d: सहस्रवल्शा वि वयं रुहेमेत्य् आत्मानं प्रत्यभिमृश्य यं त्वायं स्वधितिर् इत्य् अन्वग्रम् अद्गांश् छिनत्ति
7.2.9.a.m: Having touched himself with: 'May we grow with a thousand branches,' he cuts off the twigs towards the tip with: 'The axe, which... to thee.'

7.2.10.a.s: acchinno rāyaḥ suvīra ity agraṃ parivāsayati
7.2.10.a.d: अच्छिन्नो रायः सुवीर इत्य् अग्रं परिवासयति
7.2.10.a.m: He trims the top with: 'Unsevered wealth, rich in heroes.'

7.2.12.a.m: Some teach from one cubit up to thirty-three cubits without interruption.

7.2.13.a.m: As high as the sacrificer with arms raised.

7.2.16.a.m: The measure of a man, however, is its lowest measure.

7.2.16.c.m: Some say: 'It should only be made larger.'

7.2.17.a.s: tryaratniś caturaratnir vā pālāśo nirūḍhapaśubandhasyāto 'nyaḥ saumyasyādhvarasyeti vājasaneyakam
7.2.17.a.d: त्र्यरत्निश् चतुररत्निर् वा पालाशो निरूढपशुबन्धस्यातो ऽन्यः सौम्यस्याध्वरस्येति वाजसनेयकम्
7.2.17.a.m: "Three cubits or four cubits of palāśa wood is for the independent animal sacrifice; other than that, it is for the soma sacrifice," thus says the Vājasaneyaka.

7.3.2.a.d: अष्टाश्रिर् अनुपूर्वो ऽग्रतो ऽणीयान् प्रज्ञाताग्निष्ठाश्रिर् अस्थूलो ऽनणुः
7.3.2.a.m: It has eight corners, tapering gradually towards the top, with the corner facing the fire well marked, neither too thick nor too slender.

7.3.3.a.m: From the shavings [are taken] the wooden chip and the chip for the churning stick.

7.3.4.a.s: agrāc caṣālaṃ pṛthamātram aṣṭāśri madhye saṃnatam
7.3.4.a.d: अग्राच् चषालं पृथमात्रम् अष्टाश्रि मध्ये संनतम्
7.3.4.a.m: From the top [is made] the top-ring, of the measure of a span, eight-cornered, narrowed in the middle.

7.3.5.a.s: yaṃ kāmayetānyo 'sya lokam abhyārohed iti tasyānyavṛkṣasya svarucaṣāle kuryāt
7.3.5.a.d: यं कामयेतान्यो ऽस्य लोकम् अभ्यारोहेद् इति तस्यान्यवृक्षस्य स्वरुचषाले कुर्यात्
7.3.5.a.m: [For a sacrificer] about whom he might desire, 'May another mount upon his world,' he should make the chip and the top-ring from another tree.

7.3.6.a.s: yāvad uttamam aṅgulikāṇḍaṃ tāvad ūrdhvaṃ caṣālād yūpasyātiriktaṃ dvyaṅgulaṃ tryaṅgulaṃ caturaṅgulaṃ vā
7.3.6.a.d: यावद् उत्तमम् अङ्गुलिकाण्डं तावद् ऊर्ध्वं चषालाद् यूपस्यातिरिक्तं द्व्यङ्गुलं त्र्यङ्गुलं चतुरङ्गुलं वा
7.3.6.a.m: As much as the upper joint of a finger, so much does the sacrificial post project above the top-ring: two finger-breadths, three finger-breadths, or four finger-breadths.

7.3.7.a.m: The altar ground of the independent animal sacrifice is the size of a chariot.

7.3.8.a.s: akṣasaṃmitā paścāttiryag īṣayā prācī vipathayugena purastād yāvatā vā bāhye chidre
7.3.8.a.d: अक्षसंमिता पश्चात्तिर्यग् ईषया प्राची विपथयुगेन पुरस्ताद् यावता वा बाह्ये छिद्रे
7.3.8.a.m: Crosswise at the back it is equal in measure to the axle; its length to the east is [the length of] the pole; in front [its width is] the yoke of a wagon, or as much as the two outer peg-holes.

7.3.9.a.s: aratnibhir vā caturbhiḥ paścāt ṣaḍbhiḥ prācī tribhiḥ purastāt
7.3.9.a.d: अरत्निभिर् वा चतुर्भिः पश्चात् षड्भिः प्राची त्रिभिः पुरस्तात्
7.3.9.a.m: Or [measured] by cubits: four at the back, six long to the east, three in front.

7.3.10.a.s: tāṃ vedaṃ kṛtvā darśapūrṇamāsavatsaṃnamanavarjaṃ prāg uttarāt parigrāhāt kṛtvāpareṇa yūpāvaṭadeśaṃ saṃcaram avaśiṣya vedyāmuttaravediṃ daśapadāṃ some karoti
7.3.10.a.d: तां वेदं कृत्वा दर्शपूर्णमासवत्संनमनवर्जं प्राग् उत्तरात् परिग्राहात् कृत्वापरेण यूपावटदेशं संचरम् अवशिष्य वेद्यामुत्तरवेदिं दशपदां सोमे करोति
7.3.10.a.m: Having made the broom, having performed [the rites] as in the New and Full Moon sacrifices, omitting the bending down, up to the northern tracing, leaving a passageway behind the place of the post-hole, he constructs upon the altar ground the high altar of ten paces in the soma sacrifice.

7.3.11.a.m: Some say it should be narrower in front.

7.3.12.a.s: tāṃ yugena yajamānasya vā padair vimāya śamyayā parimimīte
7.3.12.a.d: तां युगेन यजमानस्य वा पदैर् विमाय शम्यया परिमिमीते
7.3.12.a.m: Having measured it out with the yoke or with the steps of the sacrificer, he measures it around with the yoke-pin.

7.3.13.a.m: The high altar of the independent animal sacrifice is the size of a yoke-pin.

7.3.14.a.s: śamyāṃ purastād udagagrāṃ nidhāya sphyenodīcīm abhyantaram upalikhati vittāyanī me 'sīti /
7.3.14.a.d: शम्यां पुरस्ताद् उदगग्रां निधाय स्फ्येनोदीचीम् अभ्यन्तरम् उपलिखति वित्तायनी मे ऽसीति ।
7.3.14.a.m: Having laid down the yoke-pin in front with its tip pointing north, he outlines on the inside towards the north with the wooden sword, with: 'Thou art the finder of wealth for me.'

7.3.14.b.d: एवं दक्षिणतः प्राचीं तिक्तायनी मे ऽसीति ।
7.3.14.b.m: Similarly on the south towards the east, with: 'Thou art the finder of what is sharp for me.'

7.3.14.c.m: On the west towards the north, with: 'May it protect me from being distressed.'

7.3.14.d.s: uttarataḥ prācīm avatān mā vyathitam iti
7.3.14.d.d: उत्तरतः प्राचीम् अवतान् मा व्यथितम् इति
7.3.14.d.m: On the north towards the east, with: 'May it protect me from being afflicted.'

7.4.1.a.m: At a stride to the north from the northern shoulder of the altar ground is the pit.

7.4.2.a.s: tam uttaravedivat tūṣṇīṃ śamyayā parimitya devasya tvā savituḥ prasava ity abhrim ādāya parilikhitaṃ rakṣaḥ parilikhitā arātaya iti triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ parilikhya tūṣṇīṃ jānudaghnaṃ trivitastaṃ vā khatvottaravedyarthān pāṃsūn harati vider iti
7.4.2.a.d: तम् उत्तरवेदिवत् तूष्णीं शम्यया परिमित्य देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इत्य् अभ्रिम् आदाय परिलिखितं रक्षः परिलिखिता अरातय इति त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं परिलिख्य तूष्णीं जानुदघ्नं त्रिवितस्तं वा खत्वोत्तरवेद्यर्थान् पांसून् हरति विदेर् इति
7.4.2.a.m: Having measured it silently with the yoke-pin like the high altar, having taken the spade with: 'At the impulse of the god Savitṛ...,' having traced it three times sunwise with: 'The rakṣas is enclosed, the enemies are enclosed,' having dug it silently knee-deep or three spans deep, he takes out the earth meant for the high altar, with: 'Thou art the finder.'

7.4.3.a.m: He pours it out onto the high altar with: 'Thou art a lioness.'

7.4.4.a.s: etenaiva yo dvitīyasyām iti dvitīyaṃ yas tṛtīyasyām iti tṛtīyam
7.4.4.a.d: एतेनैव यो द्वितीयस्याम् इति द्वितीयं यस् तृतीयस्याम् इति तृतीयम्
7.4.4.a.m: In this very way, [he takes and pours] the second [load] with: 'Who in the second...,' the third with: 'Who in the third...'

7.4.5.a.s: tūṣṇīṃ caturthaṃ hṛtvoru prathasvoru te yajñapatiḥ prathatām it prathayitvā dhruvāsīti śamyayā saṃhatya devebhyaḥ kalpasvety abhimantrya devebhyaḥ śundhasvety adbhir avokṣya devebhyaḥ śumbhasveti sikatābhir avakīrya prokṣaṇīśeṣam uttarata uttaravedyai ninīyāpo ripraṃ nirvahateti sphyenodīcīm ekasphyāṃ niḥsārya vibhrāḍ bṛhat pibatu somyaṃ madhvāyur dadhad yajñapatāv avihrutam /
7.4.5.a.d: तूष्णीं चतुर्थं हृत्वोरु प्रथस्वोरु ते यज्ञपतिः प्रथताम् इत् प्रथयित्वा ध्रुवासीति शम्यया संहत्य देवेभ्यः कल्पस्वेत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य देवेभ्यः शुन्धस्वेत्य् अद्भिर् अवोक्ष्य देवेभ्यः शुम्भस्वेति सिकताभिर् अवकीर्य प्रोक्षणीशेषम् उत्तरत उत्तरवेद्यै निनीयापो रिप्रं निर्वहतेति स्फ्येनोदीचीम् एकस्फ्यां निःसार्य विभ्राड् बृहत् पिबतु सोम्यं मध्वायुर् दधद् यज्ञपताव् अविह्रुतम् ।
7.4.5.a.m: Having brought the fourth [load] silently, having spread it with: 'Spread wide, may the lord of sacrifice spread wide for thee,' having compacted it with the yoke-pin with: 'Thou art firm,' having addressed it with: 'Be fit for the gods,' having sprinkled it with water with: 'Be clean for the gods,' having scattered sand over it with: 'Be adorned for the gods,' having poured out the remainder of the sprinkling water to the north of the high altar, having cleared [a line] towards the north with the wooden sword, the breadth of one sword, with: 'May the waters carry away the impurity,' / with: 'May the radiant, the great drink the honeyed soma, / bestowing unimpaired life on the lord of sacrifice;

7.4.5.b.s: vātajūto yo abhirakṣati tmanā prajāḥ piparti bahudhā virājatīty uttaravedyā antān kalpayati
7.4.5.b.d: वातजूतो यो अभिरक्षति त्मना प्रजाः पिपर्ति बहुधा विराजतीत्य् उत्तरवेद्या अन्तान् कल्पयति
7.4.5.b.m: He who, impelled by the wind, protects by himself, / fosters the creatures, shining brightly in many ways,' / he shapes the edges of the high altar.

7.5.1.a.s: athāsyā madhye prādeśamātrīṃ gopadamātrīm aśvaśaphamātrīṃ vottaranābhiṃ catuḥsraktiṃ kṛtvā catuḥśikhaṇḍe yuvatī kanīne ghṛtapratīke bhuvanasya madhye /
7.5.1.a.d: अथास्या मध्ये प्रादेशमात्रीं गोपदमात्रीम् अश्वशफमात्रीं वोत्तरनाभिं चतुःस्रक्तिं कृत्वा चतुःशिखण्डे युवती कनीने घृतप्रतीके भुवनस्य मध्ये ।
7.5.1.a.m: Then in its middle, having made a four-cornered upper navel of the measure of a span, of the measure of a cow-foot, or of the measure of a horse-hoof, with: 'Four-braided, youthful, maiden-like, with face of clarified butter, in the middle of the world;

7.5.1.b.s: tayor devā adhisaṃvasanta uttame nāka iha mādayantām ity ubhe abhimantryendraghoṣas tvā vasubhiḥ purastāt pātv ity etair yathāliṅgam uttaravediṃ prokṣati
7.5.1.b.d: तयोर् देवा अधिसंवसन्त उत्तमे नाक इह मादयन्ताम् इत्य् उभे अभिमन्त्र्येन्द्रघोषस् त्वा वसुभिः पुरस्तात् पात्व् इत्य् एतैर् यथालिङ्गम् उत्तरवेदिं प्रोक्षति
7.5.1.b.m: Dwelling together upon them, may the gods rejoice here in the highest heaven,' / having addressed both [the high altar and the navel], he sprinkles the high altar with these [formulas] according to their characteristic marks: 'May Indra's shout protect thee with the Vasus from the front;'

7.5.2.a.s: tvaṣṭā tvā rūpair upariṣṭāt pātv iti madhyam
7.5.2.a.d: त्वष्टा त्वा रूपैर् उपरिष्टात् पात्व् इति मध्यम्
7.5.2.a.m: the center with: 'May Tvaṣṭṛ protect thee with the forms from above.'

7.5.3.a.s: prokṣaṇīśeṣaṃ dakṣiṇata uttaravedyai ninayec chucā tvārpayāmīti dveṣyaṃ manasā dhyāyan
7.5.3.a.d: प्रोक्षणीशेषं दक्षिणत उत्तरवेद्यै निनयेच् छुचा त्वार्पयामीति द्वेष्यं मनसा ध्यायन्
7.5.3.a.m: To the south of the northern altar, he should pour out the remainder of the sprinkling water with [the formula], 'With sorrow I afflict you,' meditating in mind upon someone he hates.

7.5.4.a.s: pūrvavad ekasphyāṃ dakṣiṇato niḥsārya juhvāṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā sarvatra hiraṇyam upāsyann akṣṇayottaravedim uttaranābhiṃ vā vyāghārayati
7.5.4.a.d: पूर्ववद् एकस्फ्यां दक्षिणतो निःसार्य जुह्वां पञ्चगृहीतं गृहीत्वा सर्वत्र हिरण्यम् उपास्यन्न् अक्ष्णयोत्तरवेदिम् उत्तरनाभिं वा व्याघारयति
7.5.4.a.m: Having removed [the dirt] to the south by a wooden sword's breadth as before, having taken five ladlings [of clarified butter] into the juhū, casting in gold everywhere, he crosswise makes a libation of clarified butter upon the northern altar or upon the northern navel,

7.5.5.a.s: dakṣiṇam aṃsam uttarāṃ śroṇiṃ dakṣiṇām uttaram aṃsaṃ madhyam iti siṃhīr asīty etaiḥ pratimantram
7.5.5.a.d: दक्षिणम् अंसम् उत्तरां श्रोणिं दक्षिणाम् उत्तरम् अंसं मध्यम् इति सिंहीर् असीत्य् एतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
7.5.5.a.m: to the southern corner, the northern hip, the southern [hip], the northern corner, and the middle, each with its respective mantra, beginning with 'You are a lioness.'

7.5.6.a.s: bhūtebhyas tveti srucam udgṛhya pautudravaiḥ paridhibhir uttaravediṃ paridadhāti viśvāyur asīti madhyamaṃ dhruvakṣid asīti dakṣiṇam acyutakṣid asīty uttaram
7.5.6.a.d: भूतेभ्यस् त्वेति स्रुचम् उद्गृह्य पौतुद्रवैः परिधिभिर् उत्तरवेदिं परिदधाति विश्वायुर् असीति मध्यमं ध्रुवक्षिद् असीति दक्षिणम् अच्युतक्षिद् असीत्य् उत्तरम्
7.5.6.a.m: Having raised the ladle with [the formula], 'For the living beings, you,' he encloses the northern altar with enclosing sticks of pūtudru wood: the middle one with 'You are long life,' the southern one with 'You are dwelling firm,' the northern one with 'You are dwelling unshaken.'

7.5.7.a.m: He offers all oblations at the junction of the enclosing sticks.

7.6.1.a.s: agner bhasmāsīty uttaravedyāṃ saṃbhārān nivapati gulgulu sugandhitejanaṃ śvetām ūrṇāstukāṃ petvasyāntarāśṛṅgīyāṃ lūnasyālūnapūrvasya vā
7.6.1.a.d: अग्नेर् भस्मासीत्य् उत्तरवेद्यां संभारान् निवपति गुल्गुलु सुगन्धितेजनं श्वेताम् ऊर्णास्तुकां पेत्वस्यान्तराशृङ्गीयां लूनस्यालूनपूर्वस्य वा
7.6.1.a.m: With [the formula], 'You are the ash of Agni,' he scatters the substances onto the northern altar: bdellium, fragrant reed-grass, a tuft of white wool, [and wool] from between the horns of a ram that has been shorn or has never been shorn before.

7.6.2.a.s: vyāghāraṇaprabhṛti saṃbhāranivapanāntam uttaravedyām upary agnau dhāryamāṇa eke samāmananti
7.6.2.a.d: व्याघारणप्रभृति संभारनिवपनान्तम् उत्तरवेद्याम् उपर्य् अग्नौ धार्यमाण एके समामनन्ति
7.6.2.a.m: Some teach that [the rites] from the libation of clarified butter up to the scattering of the substances [are performed] while fire is being held above the northern altar.

7.6.3.a.s: prokṣāntāṃ kṛtvodumbaraśākhābhiḥ plakṣaśākhābhir vā pracchādya vasati yady asadyaskālaḥ paśur bhavati
7.6.3.a.d: प्रोक्षान्तां कृत्वोदुम्बरशाखाभिः प्लक्षशाखाभिर् वा प्रच्छाद्य वसति यद्य् असद्यस्कालः पशुर् भवति
7.6.3.a.m: Having brought [the rites] up to the sprinkling to an end, having covered [the altar] with branches of udumbara or with branches of plakṣa, he remains overnight, if the animal sacrifice is not to be completed in one day.

7.6.4.a.s: āhavanīye praṇayanīyam idhmam ādīpya sikatābhir upayamyāgnaye praṇīyamānāyānubrūhīti saṃpreṣyati /
7.6.4.a.d: आहवनीये प्रणयनीयम् इध्मम् आदीप्य सिकताभिर् उपयम्याग्नये प्रणीयमानायानुब्रूहीति संप्रेष्यति ।
7.6.4.a.m:
Having kindled on the āhavanīya the firewood that is to be brought forward, having supported it with sand, he issues the call: 'Recite for Agni being brought forward!'

Or: 'Recite for [him] being brought forward!'

7.6.5.a.s: udyamyāgnim āhavanīya udyatahomaṃ juhoti yat te pāvaka cakṛmā kaccid āgaḥ pūrvo yat sann aparo bhavāsi /
7.6.5.a.d: उद्यम्याग्निम् आहवनीय उद्यतहोमं जुहोति यत् ते पावक चकृमा कच्चिद् आगः पूर्वो यत् सन्न् अपरो भवासि ।
7.6.5.a.m: Having lifted up the fire, he offers the lifting-up oblation into the āhavanīya: 'Whatever sin we have committed against you, O purifier, / in that you who are first become the last,

7.6.5.b.s: ghṛtena tvaṃ tanvaṃ vardhayasva mā mā hiṃsīr adhigataṃ purastāt svāheti
7.6.5.b.d: घृतेन त्वं तन्वं वर्धयस्व मा मा हिंसीर् अधिगतं पुरस्तात् स्वाहेति
7.6.5.b.m: strengthen your body with clarified butter; / do not injure me, having arrived in front, svāhā!'

7.6.6.a.s: prathamāyāṃ trir anūktāyām upayamanībhir upayamya harati
7.6.6.a.d: प्रथमायां त्रिर् अनूक्तायाम् उपयमनीभिर् उपयम्य हरति
7.6.6.a.m: When the first [verse] has been recited three times, supporting [it] with the supporting pans, he carries [the fire].

7.6.7.a.s: ūrṇāvantaṃ prathamaḥ sīda yonim iti hotur abhijñāyāgne bādhasva vi mṛdho nudasvāpāmīvā apa rakṣāṃsi sedha /
7.6.7.a.d: ऊर्णावन्तं प्रथमः सीद योनिम् इति होतुर् अभिज्ञायाग्ने बाधस्व वि मृधो नुदस्वापामीवा अप रक्षांसि सेध ।
7.6.7.a.m: Recognizing from the hotṛ [the verse], 'Sit first in the wool-clad womb,' [he recites]: 'O Agni, ward off, drive away the adversaries; drive away illness, drive away the rakṣases!

7.6.7.b.s: asmāt samudrād bṛhato divo no 'pāṃ bhūmānam upa naḥ sṛjeha //
7.6.7.b.d: अस्मात् समुद्राद् बृहतो दिवो नो ऽपां भूमानम् उप नः सृजेह ॥
7.6.7.b.m: From this ocean, from high heaven, / release for us here an abundance of waters!'

7.6.7.c.s: yajña pratitiṣṭha sumatau suśevā ā tvā vasūni purudhā viśantu /
7.6.7.c.d: यज्ञ प्रतितिष्ठ सुमतौ सुशेवा आ त्वा वसूनि पुरुधा विशन्तु ।
7.6.7.c.m: 'O sacrifice, stand firm in favor, very kind; / may riches enter into you in many ways!

7.6.7.d.s: dīrgham āyur yajamānāya kṛṇvann athāmṛtena jaritāram aṅgdhīha yajñaḥ pratyaṣṭhād iti saṃbhāreṣu pratiṣṭhāpya
7.6.7.d.d: दीर्घम् आयुर् यजमानाय कृण्वन्न् अथामृतेन जरितारम् अङ्ग्धीह यज्ञः प्रत्यष्ठाद् इति संभारेषु प्रतिष्ठाप्य
7.6.7.d.m: Creating a long life for the sacrificer, / then anoint the singer here with immortality! The sacrifice has stood firm'—having established [the fire] on the substances [with these words],

7.7.1.a.s: agneḥ purīṣam asīty uttarata upayamanīr nyupya manuṣvat tvā nidhīmahi manuṣvat samidhīmahi /
7.7.1.a.d: अग्नेः पुरीषम् असीत्य् उत्तरत उपयमनीर् न्युप्य मनुष्वत् त्वा निधीमहि मनुष्वत् समिधीमहि ।
7.7.1.a.m: having poured out the supporting pans to the north with [the formula], 'You are the soil of Agni,' having added fuel with: 'Like Manu we place you down, like Manu we kindle you;

7.7.1.b.s: agne manuṣvad aṅgiro devān devāyate yajety upasamidhya dvādaśagṛhītena srucaṃ pūrayitvā sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvā iti saptavatyā pūrṇāhutiṃ juhoti
7.7.1.b.d: अग्ने मनुष्वद् अङ्गिरो देवान् देवायते यजेत्य् उपसमिध्य द्वादशगृहीतेन स्रुचं पूरयित्वा सप्त ते अग्ने समिधः सप्त जिह्वा इति सप्तवत्या पूर्णाहुतिं जुहोति
7.7.1.b.m: O sage Agni, like Manu sacrifice to the gods for the one who seeks the gods,' having filled the ladle with twelve ladlings, he offers the full oblation with the verse containing the word 'seven': 'Seven are your fuels, O Agni, seven your tongues.'

7.7.2.a.s: agnir vāyur ādityo viṣṇur yajñaṃ nayatu prajānan mainaṃ yajñahano vidan devebhyo yajñaṃ prabrūtāt pra pra yajñapatiṃ tira svāheti catasro 'timuktīr juhoti
7.7.2.a.d: अग्निर् वायुर् आदित्यो विष्णुर् यज्ञं नयतु प्रजानन् मैनं यज्ञहनो विदन् देवेभ्यो यज्ञं प्रब्रूतात् प्र प्र यज्ञपतिं तिर स्वाहेति चतस्रो ऽतिमुक्तीर् जुहोति
7.7.2.a.m: He offers four liberation oblations: 'May Agni, Vāyu, Āditya, [and] Viṣṇu lead the sacrifice, knowing it; may the sacrifice-destroyers not find it; announce the sacrifice to the gods; extend the lord of the sacrifice forward, svāhā!'

7.7.3.a.s: eṣa paśubandhasyāhavanīyo yataḥ praṇayati sa gārhapatyaḥ
7.7.3.a.d: एष पशुबन्धस्याहवनीयो यतः प्रणयति स गार्हपत्यः
7.7.3.a.m: This is the āhavanīya of the animal sacrifice; that from which he brings [the fire] forward is the gārhapatya.

7.7.4.a.s: praṇīte ced agnihotrakāla etasminn evāgnihotraṃ juhuyāt
7.7.4.a.d: प्रणीते चेद् अग्निहोत्रकाल एतस्मिन्न् एवाग्निहोत्रं जुहुयात्
7.7.4.a.m: If, after it has been brought forward, the time for the agnihotra arrives, he should offer the agnihotra in this [new fire] alone.

7.7.5.a.m: Likewise elsewhere when the ritual procedure has progressed.

7.7.7.a.s: trayoviṃśatidārur idhma āśvavālaḥ prastara aikṣavī vidhṛtī kārṣmaryamayāḥ paridhayaḥ
7.7.7.a.d: त्रयोविंशतिदारुर् इध्म आश्ववालः प्रस्तर ऐक्षवी विधृती कार्ष्मर्यमयाः परिधयः
7.7.7.a.m: The firewood consists of twenty-three sticks of wood; the grass bunch is made of horse-tail grass; the two dividers are made of sugarcane; the enclosing sticks are made of kārṣmarya wood.

7.8.1.a.m: Having strewn grass around the fires, he proceeds to the rite beginning with the washing of hands.

7.8.2.a.m: He arranges the utensils according to purpose:

7.8.3.a.s: sphyam agnihotrahavaṇīṃ vasāhomahavanīṃ dvitīyāṃ juhūṃ pṛṣadājyadhānīṃ dvitīyām upabhṛtaṃ dve ājyasthālyau hṛdayaśūlam asiṃ kumbhīṃ plakṣaśākhāṃ śākhāpavitraṃ kārṣmaryamayyau vapāśrapaṇyau dviśūlām ekaśūlāṃ caudumbaraṃ maitrāvaruṇadaṇḍam āsyadaghnaṃ cubukadaghnaṃ vā raśane ca
7.8.3.a.d: स्फ्यम् अग्निहोत्रहवणीं वसाहोमहवनीं द्वितीयां जुहूं पृषदाज्यधानीं द्वितीयाम् उपभृतं द्वे आज्यस्थाल्यौ हृदयशूलम् असिं कुम्भीं प्लक्षशाखां शाखापवित्रं कार्ष्मर्यमय्यौ वपाश्रपण्यौ द्विशूलाम् एकशूलां चौदुम्बरं मैत्रावरुणदण्डम् आस्यदघ्नं चुबुकदघ्नं वा रशने च
7.8.3.a.m: the wooden sword, the agnihotra ladle, the ladle for offering the fat, a second juhū, the receptacle for speckled butter, a second upabhṛt, two pots for clarified butter, the heart-spit, the knife, the cooking pot, a branch of plakṣa, a branch strainer, two fat-cooking spits of kārṣmarya wood—one two-pronged and one single-pronged—and the Maitrāvaruṇa's staff of udumbara wood, mouth-high or chin-high, and two cords.

7.8.4.a.s: pavitre kṛtvā yajamāna vācaṃ yaccheti saṃpreṣyati
7.8.4.a.d: पवित्रे कृत्वा यजमान वाचं यच्छेति संप्रेष्यति
7.8.4.a.m: Having made two strainers, he issues the call: 'Sacrificer, restrain speech!'

7.8.5.a.s: vāgyataḥ pātrāṇi saṃmṛśya prokṣaṇīḥ saṃskṛtya brāhmaṇam āmantrya pātrāṇi prokṣaty atra vācaṃ visṛjate /
7.8.5.a.d: वाग्यतः पात्राणि संमृश्य प्रोक्षणीः संस्कृत्य ब्राह्मणम् आमन्त्र्य पात्राणि प्रोक्षत्य् अत्र वाचं विसृजते ।
7.8.5.a.m: Restraining his speech, having touched the utensils, having prepared the sprinkling water, having addressed the Brahman priest, he sprinkles the utensils; at this point he releases his speech.

7.8.5.b.s: sphyam ādāyottaraṃ parigrāhaṃ parigṛhya darśapūrṇamāsavat saṃpreṣyati /
7.8.5.b.d: स्फ्यम् आदायोत्तरं परिग्राहं परिगृह्य दर्शपूर्णमासवत् संप्रेष्यति ।
7.8.5.b.m: Having taken the wooden sword, having made the northern enclosing line, he issues the call as in the New and Full Moon sacrifices.

7.8.5.c.m: He modifies the end of the ritual call to: 'Wet with clarified butter [and] curds!'

7.8.6.a.s: srucāṃ saṃmārjanakāle sruvaṃ saṃmṛjya tasyāvṛtā svadhitim
7.8.6.a.d: स्रुचां संमार्जनकाले स्रुवं संमृज्य तस्यावृता स्वधितिम्
7.8.6.a.m: At the time of cleansing the ladles, having cleansed the sruva, [he cleanses] the sacrificial knife according to its procedure;

7.8.7.a.m: the ladle for offering the fat like the juhū, the receptacle for speckled butter like the upabhṛt.

7.8.7.b.m: Having portioned out the clarified butter, he portions out the curds.

7.8.8.a.m: [Every rite] except placing on the fire is performed upon the curds.

7.8.9.a.s: naitasya dadhnaḥ saṃskāro vidyata ity aparam
7.8.9.a.d: नैतस्य दध्नः संस्कारो विद्यत इत्य् अपरम्
7.8.9.a.m: 'There is no consecration for these curds,' says another [authority].

7.9.1.a.m: At the time of taking the clarified butter, he takes four ladlings into the juhū, four into the upabhṛt.

7.9.2.a.s: dadhany ājyam ānīya mahīnāṃ payo 'sīti pṛṣadājyadhānyāṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ pṛṣadājyaṃ jyotir asi viśvarūpaṃ viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ samid iti vā
7.9.2.a.d: दधन्य् आज्यम् आनीय महीनां पयो ऽसीति पृषदाज्यधान्यां पञ्चगृहीतं पृषदाज्यं ज्योतिर् असि विश्वरूपं विश्वेषां देवानां समिद् इति वा
7.9.2.a.m: Having added clarified butter into the curds, he takes five ladlings of speckled butter into the receptacle for speckled butter with [the formula], 'You are the milk of the great ones,' or with 'You are light, omniform, the kindling stick of all the gods.'

7.9.4.a.m: At the time of setting down, he sets down the portions of clarified butter;

7.9.5.a.m: the receptacle for speckled butter like the upabhṛt.

7.9.6.a.s: pūrvavad ājyāny abhimantryāgreṇāhavanīyaṃ yūpāvaṭaṃ parilikhaty ardham antarvedy ardhaṃ bahirvedi
7.9.6.a.d: पूर्ववद् आज्यान्य् अभिमन्त्र्याग्रेणाहवनीयं यूपावटं परिलिखत्य् अर्धम् अन्तर्वेद्य् अर्धं बहिर्वेदि
7.9.6.a.m: Having consecrated the portions of clarified butter as before, he outlines the post-pit to the front of the āhavanīya, half inside the altar ground and half outside the altar ground.

7.9.7.a.m: The taking of the spade and the outlining are as before.

7.9.8.a.m: Then he digs so that the butt will not be exposed.

7.9.9.a.s: agreṇāvaṭaṃ prāñcaṃ yūpaṃ nidhāya yat te śikvaḥ parāvadhīt takṣā hastena vāsyā /
7.9.9.a.d: अग्रेणावटं प्राञ्चं यूपं निधाय यत् ते शिक्वः परावधीत् तक्षा हस्तेन वास्या ।
7.9.9.a.m: Having placed the post to the front of the pit pointing east, [he recites]: 'What the clever carpenter with hand, with axe has cut away of you,

7.9.9.b.s: āpas tat sarvaṃ jīvalāḥ śundhantu śucayaḥ śucim iti yūpaṃ prakṣālyāthainaṃ yavamatībhiḥ prokṣati /
7.9.9.b.d: आपस् तत् सर्वं जीवलाः शुन्धन्तु शुचयः शुचिम् इति यूपं प्रक्षाल्याथैनं यवमतीभिः प्रोक्षति ।
7.9.9.b.m: may the living, pure waters purify all that, [making] the pure [pure]'—having washed the post [with this verse], he then sprinkles it with [water] containing barley:

7.9.9.c.s: pṛthivyai tveti mūlam antarikṣāya tveti madhyaṃ dive tvety agram
7.9.9.c.d: पृथिव्यै त्वेति मूलम् अन्तरिक्षाय त्वेति मध्यं दिवे त्वेत्य् अग्रम्
7.9.9.c.m: 'For the earth, you,' the base; 'For the intermediate space, you,' the middle; 'For the sky, you,' the top.

7.9.10.a.s: śundhatāṃ lokaḥ pitṛṣadana iti prokṣaṇīśeṣam avaṭe 'vanīya yavo 'sīti yavam avāsya pitṝṇāṃ sadanam asīti barhiṣāvastīrya svāveśo 'sīti prathamaparāpātinaṃ śakalam avāsya ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī āpṛṇethām iti sruveṇa śakale hutvā
7.9.10.a.d: शुन्धतां लोकः पितृषदन इति प्रोक्षणीशेषम् अवटे ऽवनीय यवो ऽसीति यवम् अवास्य पितॄणां सदनम् असीति बर्हिषावस्तीर्य स्वावेशो ऽसीति प्रथमपरापातिनं शकलम् अवास्य घृतेन द्यावापृथिवी आपृणेथाम् इति स्रुवेण शकले हुत्वा
7.9.10.a.m: Having poured the remainder of the sprinkling water into the pit with 'Let the world, the seat of the fathers, be cleansed,' having cast in a barleycorn with 'You are barley,' having strewn it with sacrificial grass with 'You are the seat of the fathers,' having cast in the chip that first flew off with 'You are easy of entrance,' having offered on the chip with the sruva with 'May heaven and earth be filled with clarified butter,'

7.10.1.a.s: yūpāyājyamānāyānubrūhīti saṃpreṣyaty ajyamānāyānubrūhy añjmo yūpam anubrūhīti vā
7.10.1.a.d: यूपायाज्यमानायानुब्रूहीति संप्रेष्यत्य् अज्यमानायानुब्रूह्य् अञ्ज्मो यूपम् अनुब्रूहीति वा
7.10.1.a.m: he issues the call: 'Recite for the post being anointed!' or 'Recite for [it] being anointed!' or 'Recite: we anoint the post!'

7.10.2.a.m: Then the sacrificer anoints it from the top with unheated clarified butter by means of the chip.

7.10.3.a.s: aindram asīti caṣālam aktvā supippalābhyas tvauṣadhībhya iti pratimucya devas tvā savitā madhvānaktv iti sruveṇa saṃtatam avicchindann agniṣṭhām aśrim anakty oparāt
7.10.3.a.d: ऐन्द्रम् असीति चषालम् अक्त्वा सुपिप्पलाभ्यस् त्वौषधीभ्य इति प्रतिमुच्य देवस् त्वा सविता मध्वानक्त्व् इति स्रुवेण संततम् अविच्छिन्दन्न् अग्निष्ठाम् अश्रिम् अनक्त्य् ओपरात्
7.10.3.a.m: Having anointed the post-cap with 'You belong to Indra,' having fastened it on with 'For the plants bearing good fruit, you,' [the adhvaryu] continuously, without interruption, anoints the fire-facing corner [of the post] with the sruva down to the butt with 'May the divine Savitṛ anoint you with honey.'
