7.10.4.a.m: At the place of the cord, he strokes the post all around three times.

7.10.5.a.s: añjanādi yūpaṃ yajamāno notsṛjaty ā parivyayaṇāt
7.10.5.a.d: अञ्जनादि यूपं यजमानो नोत्सृजत्य् आ परिव्ययणात्
7.10.5.a.m: Beginning with the anointing, the sacrificer does not release the post until the girding.

7.10.6.a.m: He issues the call: 'Recite for the post being raised!' or 'Recite for [it] being raised!'

7.10.7.a.m: He raises it with [the formula], 'Prop up the sky, fill the intermediate space!'

7.10.8.a.m: He places it down into the pit with [the words], 'To your domains!'

7.10.9.a.s: viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi paśyateti dvābhyām āhavanīyenāgniṣṭhāṃ saṃminoti
7.10.9.a.d: विष्णोः कर्माणि पश्यतेति द्वाभ्याम् आहवनीयेनाग्निष्ठां संमिनोति
7.10.9.a.m: With the two verses, 'Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu,' he aligns the fire-facing corner with the āhavanīya.

7.10.10.a.m: [The rule concerning] him whom he may desire [to endow] with splendor has [already] been stated.

7.10.11.a.m: The top of the sacrificial post is inclined toward the āhavanīya, its base sunk down.

7.10.12.a.s: anāvir uparaṃ kṛtvā brahmavaniṃ tvā kṣatravanim iti pradakṣiṇaṃ pāṃsubhiḥ paryūhya brahma dṛṃha kṣatraṃ dṛmheti maitrāvaruṇadaṇḍena samaṃ bhūmiparidṛṃhaṇaṃ kṛtvā
7.10.12.a.d: अनाविर् उपरं कृत्वा ब्रह्मवनिं त्वा क्षत्रवनिम् इति प्रदक्षिणं पांसुभिः पर्यूह्य ब्रह्म दृंह क्षत्रं दृम्हेति मैत्रावरुणदण्डेन समं भूमिपरिदृंहणं कृत्वा
7.10.12.a.m: Having made the base-peg hidden, having covered it clockwise with soil with "Thee, wining the priesthood, winning the nobility!", and having made the earth firm and level with the Maitrāvaruṇa's staff with "Strengthen the priesthood, strengthen the nobility!"

7.11.1.a.s: un nambhaya pṛthivīm ity adbhiḥ pariṣiñcati
7.11.1.a.d: उन् नम्भय पृथिवीम् इत्य् अद्भिः परिषिञ्चति
7.11.1.a.m: He sprinkles water around it with "Moisten the earth!"

7.11.2.a.m: There are two ropes made of darbha grass.

7.11.2.b.s: dviguṇā dvivyāyāmā paśuraśanā triguṇā trivyāyāmā yūpasya
7.11.2.b.d: द्विगुणा द्विव्यायामा पशुरशना त्रिगुणा त्रिव्यायामा यूपस्य
7.11.2.b.m: The animal's rope is two-stranded and two fathoms long; the sacrificial post's rope is three-stranded and three fathoms long.

7.11.3.a.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasava iti raśanām ādāya viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi paśyateti saraśanena pāṇinā yūpam unmārṣṭi
7.11.3.a.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इति रशनाम् आदाय विष्णोः कर्माणि पश्यतेति सरशनेन पाणिना यूपम् उन्मार्ष्टि
7.11.3.a.m: Taking the rope with "At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ...", he wipes upwards along the sacrificial post with the hand holding the rope, with "Look upon the works of Viṣṇu!"

7.11.4.a.s: tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ity agraṃ prekṣate /
7.11.4.a.d: तद् विष्णोः परमं पदम् इत्य् अग्रं प्रेक्षते ।
7.11.4.a.m: With "That highest step of Viṣṇu...", he looks at the top.

7.11.4.b.m: He gives the ritual call: "Recite for the sacrificial post being wound around!"

7.11.5.a.s: parivīr asīti nābhidaghne raśanayā triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ yūpaṃ parivyayati madhyadeśe vā
7.11.5.a.d: परिवीर् असीति नाभिदघ्ने रशनया त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं यूपं परिव्ययति मध्यदेशे वा
7.11.5.a.m: With "Thou art girded around...", he winds the rope around the sacrificial post three times clockwise at navel-height, or at the middle part.

7.11.6.a.m: [The rule concerning] him whom he may desire [to endow] with vigor has [already] been stated.

7.11.7.a.s: adho dūraṃ parivyayed vṛṣṭikāmasyopari dūram avṛṣṭikāmasyety eke
7.11.7.a.d: अधो दूरं परिव्ययेद् वृष्टिकामस्योपरि दूरम् अवृष्टिकामस्येत्य् एके
7.11.7.a.m: According to some, he should wind it far below for one desiring rain, far above for one not desiring rain.

7.11.8.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta stry asya jayetety upānte tasya vyatiṣajya na praveṣṭayet
7.11.8.a.d: यं कामयेत स्त्र्य् अस्य जयेतेत्य् उपान्ते तस्य व्यतिषज्य न प्रवेष्टयेत्
7.11.8.a.m: For him whom he may desire that a female child be born to him, having entangled it near the end, he should not tuck it in.

7.11.9.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta pumān asya jāyetety āntaṃ tasya praveṣṭyāṇimati sthavimat pravīya divaḥ sūnur asīti svarum ādāyāntarikṣasya tvā sānāvavagūhāmīty uttareṇāgniṣṭhāṃ madhyame raśaṇāguṇe 'vagūhati
7.11.9.a.d: यं कामयेत पुमान् अस्य जायेतेत्य् आन्तं तस्य प्रवेष्ट्याणिमति स्थविमत् प्रवीय दिवः सूनुर् असीति स्वरुम् आदायान्तरिक्षस्य त्वा सानाववगूहामीत्य् उत्तरेणाग्निष्ठां मध्यमे रशणागुणे ऽवगूहति
7.11.9.a.m: For him whom he may desire that a male child be born to him, having tucked it in right up to the end, having passed the thick end into the thin end, taking the chip with "Thou art the son of heaven!", he tucks it into the middle strand of the rope to the north of the corner facing the fire with "I tuck thee into the ridge of the intermediate region!"

7.11.10.b.m: "Into the lower two," says the Vājasaneyaka.

7.12.1.a.m: They bathe the victim, excluding one with a broken horn, a one-eyed one, a mutilated one, a castrated one, a lame one, and one with seven hooves.

7.12.2.a.s: yady aṅgahīnaḥ syād aṅgato vā virujyeta
7.12.2.a.d: यद्य् अङ्गहीनः स्याद् अङ्गतो वा विरुज्येत
7.12.2.a.m: If it should be deficient in a limb or injured in a limb,

7.12.3.a.s: athaikeṣāṃ vaiṣṇavīm āgnāvaiṣṇavīṃ sārasvatīṃ barhaspatyām iti ca hutvā prayojayet
7.12.3.a.d: अथैकेषां वैष्णवीम् आग्नावैष्णवीं सारस्वतीं बर्हस्पत्याम् इति च हुत्वा प्रयोजयेत्
7.12.3.a.m: then according to some [teachers], having offered oblations with the formulas to Viṣṇu, to Agni and Viṣṇu, to Sarasvatī, and to Bṛhaspati, he should employ it.

7.12.4.a.s: yo 'pannadan malaṃ tat paśūnām iti vijñāyate
7.12.4.a.d: यो ऽपन्नदन् मलं तत् पशूनाम् इति विज्ञायते
7.12.4.a.m: "That which has not shed its teeth is the refuse of animals," so it is known.

7.12.5.a.m: With "For food thee!" he takes two blades of sacrificial grass.

7.12.5.b.s: upavīr asīti plakṣaśākhāṃ bahuparṇaśākhām apratiśuṣkāgrām asuṣirām
7.12.5.b.d: उपवीर् असीति प्लक्षशाखां बहुपर्णशाखाम् अप्रतिशुष्काग्राम् असुषिराम्
7.12.5.b.m: With "Thou art approaching!", [he takes] a plakṣa branch, rich in leaves, whose tip is not dried up, and which is not hollow.

7.12.6.a.s: yaṃ kāmayetāpaśuḥ syād ity aparṇayā tasya śuṣkāgrayopākuryāt
7.12.6.a.d: यं कामयेतापशुः स्याद् इत्य् अपर्णया तस्य शुष्काग्रयोपाकुर्यात्
7.12.6.a.m: For him whom he desires should be without cattle, he should dedicate [the victim] with a leafless branch that has a dried-up tip.

7.12.8.a.s: barhirbhyāṃ plakṣaśākhayā ca purastāt pratyañcaṃ paśum upākaroti /
7.12.8.a.d: बर्हिर्भ्यां प्लक्षशाखया च पुरस्तात् प्रत्यञ्चं पशुम् उपाकरोति ।
7.12.8.a.m: With the two blades of sacrificial grass and the plakṣa branch, he dedicates the victim from the east, facing west.

7.12.8.b.s: upo devān daivīr viśaḥ prajāpater jāyamānā iti caitābhyām upaspṛśann indrāgnibhyāṃ tvā juṣṭam upākaromīti
7.12.8.b.d: उपो देवान् दैवीर् विशः प्रजापतेर् जायमाना इति चैताभ्याम् उपस्पृशन्न् इन्द्राग्निभ्यां त्वा जुष्टम् उपाकरोमीति
7.12.8.b.m: Touching [it] with both of these, with "Approach the gods, the divine clans, being born from Prajāpati!", [he dedicates it] with "Thee, agreeable to Indra and Agni, I dedicate!"

7.12.9.a.s: pañcakṛtvo devatopadeśanam upākaraṇe niyojane prokṣaṇe vapāyā uddharaṇe hṛdayasyābhighāraṇa iti
7.12.9.a.d: पञ्चकृत्वो देवतोपदेशनम् उपाकरणे नियोजने प्रोक्षणे वपाया उद्धरणे हृदयस्याभिघारण इति
7.12.9.a.m: There is recitation of the deity five times: at the dedicating, at the binding, at the sprinkling, at the extracting of the omentum, and at the basting of the heart.

7.12.10.a.s: prajānantaḥ pratigṛhṇanti pūrva iti pañca hutvāgniṃ manthati
7.12.10.a.d: प्रजानन्तः प्रतिगृह्णन्ति पूर्व इति पञ्च हुत्वाग्निं मन्थति
7.12.10.a.m: Having offered five [oblations] with "The knowing ones received the first...", he churns the fire.

7.12.11.a.m: Or else, having churned the fire, he may dedicate [the victim].

7.12.12.a.s: agner janitram asīty adhimanthanaṃ śakalaṃ nidadhāti /
7.12.12.a.d: अग्नेर् जनित्रम् असीत्य् अधिमन्थनं शकलं निदधाति ।
7.12.12.a.m: He sets down the churning-chip with "Thou art the birthplace of Agni!"

7.12.12.b.m: Two darbha blades pointing east, with "Ye two are the testicles!"

7.12.13.a.m: He takes the lower fire-drill with "Thou art Urvaśī!"

7.12.14.a.s: devo vāṃ savitā madhvānaktv ity ājyasthālyā bile 'ṅktvā ghṛtenākte vṛṣaṇaṃ dadhāthām ity ubhe abhimantryāyur asīti samavadhāya
7.12.14.a.d: देवो वां सविता मध्वानक्त्व् इत्य् आज्यस्थाल्या बिले ऽङ्क्त्वा घृतेनाक्ते वृषणं दधाथाम् इत्य् उभे अभिमन्त्र्यायुर् असीति समवधाय
7.12.14.a.m: Having anointed them at the opening of the clarified-butter pot with "May the divine Savitṛ anoint the two of you with honey!", having addressed both with "Anointed with clarified butter, may ye two bear the male!", and having placed them together with "Thou art life-span!"

7.13.1.a.m: He gives the ritual call: "Recite for Agni being churned!"

7.13.2.a.s: prathamāyāṃ trir anūktāyāṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇam agniṃ manthati /
7.13.2.a.d: प्रथमायां त्रिर् अनूक्तायां त्रिः प्रदक्षिणम् अग्निं मन्थति ।
7.13.2.a.m: When the first [verse] has been recited thrice, he churns the fire three times clockwise.

7.13.2.b.s: gāyatraṃ chando 'nuprajāyasveti prathamaṃ traiṣṭubham iti dvitīyaṃ jāgatam iti tṛtīyam
7.13.2.b.d: गायत्रं छन्दो ऽनुप्रजायस्वेति प्रथमं त्रैष्टुभम् इति द्वितीयं जागतम् इति तृतीयम्
7.13.2.b.m: The first time with "Be born according to the Gāyatrī metre!", the second time with "according to the Triṣṭubh [metre]!", the third time with "according to the Jagatī [metre]!"

7.13.3.a.m: Then he churns as rapidly as possible.

7.13.4.a.s: yadi mathyamāno na jāyeta rākṣoghnīr anubrūyāt
7.13.4.a.d: यदि मथ्यमानो न जायेत राक्षोघ्नीर् अनुब्रूयात्
7.13.4.a.m: If [the fire] being churned should not be produced, [the hotṛ] should recite demon-slaying verses.

7.13.5.a.m: When it is produced, he gives the ritual call: "Recite for [him] born!"

7.13.5.b.m: While carrying it forward: "For [him] being carried forward!"

7.13.6.a.s: bhavataṃ naḥ samanasāv ity agreṇottaraṃ paridhim āhavanīye praharati saṃdhinā vā
7.13.6.a.d: भवतं नः समनसाव् इत्य् अग्रेणोत्तरं परिधिम् आहवनीये प्रहरति संधिना वा
7.13.6.a.m: With "Be ye two of one mind for us!", he throws [it] into the āhavanīya in front of the northern enclosing stick, or at the joint.

7.13.7.a.s: agnāvagniś carati praviṣṭa iti prahṛtya sruveṇābhijuhoti
7.13.7.a.d: अग्नावग्निश् चरति प्रविष्ट इति प्रहृत्य स्रुवेणाभिजुहोति
7.13.7.a.m: Having thrown it, he offers an oblation over it with the sruva-spoon, with "Fire entered into fire moves..."

7.13.8.a.s: sāvitreṇa raśanām ādāya paśor dakṣiṇe bāhau parivīyordhvam utkṛṣyartasya tvā devahaviḥ pāśenārabha iti dakṣiṇe 'rdhaśirasi pāśenākṣṇayā pratimucya dharṣā mānuṣān ity uttarato yūpasya niyunakti
7.13.8.a.d: सावित्रेण रशनाम् आदाय पशोर् दक्षिणे बाहौ परिवीयोर्ध्वम् उत्कृष्यर्तस्य त्वा देवहविः पाशेनारभ इति दक्षिणे ऽर्धशिरसि पाशेनाक्ष्णया प्रतिमुच्य धर्षा मानुषान् इत्य् उत्तरतो यूपस्य नियुनक्ति
7.13.8.a.m: Taking the rope with the verse to Savitṛ, winding it around the right foreleg of the animal, pulling it upward, and fastening it across on the right side of the head with the noose with "With the noose of cosmic order I seize thee, sacrificial offering of the gods!", he binds [the animal] to the north of the sacrificial post with "Overcome human beings!"

7.13.10.a.m: He sprinkles [the animal] with "I sprinkle thee for the waters, for the plants!"

7.13.11.a.m: He makes it drink with "Thou art the drinker of the waters!"

7.13.12.a.s: svāttaṃ citsadevaṃ havyamāpo devīḥ svadatainam ity upariṣṭād adhastāt sarvataś ca prokṣya vedaṃ nidhāya sāmidhenībhyaḥ pratipadyate
7.13.12.a.d: स्वात्तं चित्सदेवं हव्यमापो देवीः स्वदतैनम् इत्य् उपरिष्टाद् अधस्तात् सर्वतश् च प्रोक्ष्य वेदं निधाय सामिधेनीभ्यः प्रतिपद्यते
7.13.12.a.m: Having sprinkled it from above, from below, and on all sides with "The sacrificial offering is agreeable, even divine; O divine waters, make it sweet!", and having set down the veda, he proceeds to the kindling verses.

7.14.1.a.s: srucyam āghārya pratyākramya juhvā paśuṃ samanakti
7.14.1.a.d: स्रुच्यम् आघार्य प्रत्याक्रम्य जुह्वा पशुं समनक्ति
7.14.1.a.m: Having poured the sruc-ghee, having stepped back, he anoints the animal with the juhū-spoon:

7.14.2.a.s: saṃ te prāṇo vāyunā gacchatām iti śirasi /
7.14.2.a.d: सं ते प्राणो वायुना गच्छताम् इति शिरसि ।
7.14.2.a.m: on the head with "May thy breath unite with the wind!"

7.14.2.b.m: on the shoulder-joints with "Thy limbs with the worthy of sacrifice!"

7.14.2.c.m: on the rump with "The master of sacrifice with the benediction!"

7.14.3.a.s: dhruvāsamañjanādi karma pratipadyate samānam ā pravarāt
7.14.3.a.d: ध्रुवासमञ्जनादि कर्म प्रतिपद्यते समानम् आ प्रवरात्
7.14.3.a.m: He undertakes the ritual beginning with the anointing of the dhruvā-ladle, which is the same up to the pravara.

7.14.5.a.s: daivaṃ ca mānuṣaṃ ca hotārau vṛtvā punar āśrāvya maitrāvaruṇaṃ pravṛṇīte mitrāvaruṇau praśāstārau praśāstrād iti
7.14.5.a.d: दैवं च मानुषं च होतारौ वृत्वा पुनर् आश्राव्य मैत्रावरुणं प्रवृणीते मित्रावरुणौ प्रशास्तारौ प्रशास्त्राद् इति
7.14.5.a.m: Having chosen the divine and human hotṛs, and having called for the response again, he chooses the Maitrāvaruṇa with "Mitra and Varuṇa are the two directors, from the directorship..."

7.14.6.a.m: While the animal stands, he offers the eleven fore-offerings.

7.14.7.a.m: He gives the first ritual call with "Urge for the kindling-sticks!"

7.14.8.a.m: Having poured together [the clarified butter] at the fourth and eighth [fore-offerings] and having sacrificed ten [of them], he leaves butter remaining for the eleventh.

7.14.9.a.s: tān yajamānaḥ prākṛtair āditaś caturbhiś caturo 'numantrya caturthasyānumantraṇena duraḥprabhṛtīṃs trīn uttamena śeṣam
7.14.9.a.d: तान् यजमानः प्राकृतैर् आदितश् चतुर्भिश् चतुरो ऽनुमन्त्र्य चतुर्थस्यानुमन्त्रणेन दुरःप्रभृतींस् त्रीन् उत्तमेन शेषम्
7.14.9.a.m: The sacrificer, having addressed the [first] four with the four basic [formulas] from the beginning, [addresses] the three beginning with 'the doors' with the formula of the fourth, and the rest with the last [formula].

7.14.10.a.m: Stepping back, he anoints the chip of the sacrificial post and the sacrificial knife with the juhū.

7.14.10.b.s: triḥ svaruṃ sakṛt svadhiter anyatarāṃ dhārām
7.14.10.b.d: त्रिः स्वरुं सकृत् स्वधितेर् अन्यतरां धाराम्
7.14.10.b.m: He anoints the chip of the sacrificial post three times, and one or the other edge of the sacrificial knife once.

7.14.11.a.s: svarum antardhāya svadhitinā paśuṃ samanakti ghṛtenāktau paśuṃ trāyethām iti śirasi
7.14.11.a.d: स्वरुम् अन्तर्धाय स्वधितिना पशुं समनक्ति घृतेनाक्तौ पशुं त्रायेथाम् इति शिरसि
7.14.11.a.m: Interposing the chip of the sacrificial post, he anoints the animal all over on its head with the sacrificial knife, with: 'Anointed with clarified butter, protect the victim!'

7.14.12.a.m: Or not with the sacrificial knife, [but] with the chip of the sacrificial post alone.

7.14.13.a.m: With the anointed [edge] he cuts portions from the cooked [victim], and with the other he carves the animal.

7.14.14.a.s: śamitre svadhitiṃ prayacchann āha śamitar eṣā te 'śriḥ spaṣṭāstv iti
7.14.14.a.d: शमित्रे स्वधितिं प्रयच्छन्न् आह शमितर् एषा ते ऽश्रिः स्पष्टास्त्व् इति
7.14.14.a.m: Handing the sacrificial knife to the slaughterer, he says: 'O slaughterer, let this edge of yours be distinct!'

7.15.1.a.m: He gives the call: 'Recite for [the fire] being carried around [the victim]!'

7.15.1.b.m: Or: 'Recite for the fire carried around!'

7.15.2.a.s: āhavanīyād ulmukam ādāyāgnīdhraḥ pari vājapatiḥ kavir iti triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ paryagni karoti paśuṃ yūpam āhavanīyaṃ śāmitradeśaṃ cātvālam /
7.15.2.a.d: आहवनीयाद् उल्मुकम् आदायाग्नीध्रः परि वाजपतिः कविर् इति त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं पर्यग्नि करोति पशुं यूपम् आहवनीयं शामित्रदेशं चात्वालम् ।
7.15.2.a.m: Taking a firebrand from the āhavanīya, the agnīdh carries the fire around the victim, the sacrificial post, the āhavanīya, the slaughtering place, and the cātvāla pit, three times sunwise, with: 'Around the lord of strength, the sage...'

7.15.3.a.m: Having thrown back the firebrand, he walks counter-sunwise around [them] three times.

7.15.4.a.s: prajānantaḥ pratigṛhṇanti pūrva iti paryagnau kriyamāṇe 'pāvyāni juhoty ekaṃ dve trīṇi catvāri vā
7.15.4.a.d: प्रजानन्तः प्रतिगृह्णन्ति पूर्व इति पर्यग्नौ क्रियमाणे ऽपाव्यानि जुहोत्य् एकं द्वे त्रीणि चत्वारि वा
7.15.4.a.m: While the fire is being carried around, he offers the apāvya oblations with: 'Knowing, the earlier ones accept...', one, two, three, or four.

7.15.5.a.m: 'Diverse in form are the animals of Paśupati, and alike.'

7.15.5.b.s: teṣāṃ yaṃ vavrire devās taṃ svarāḍ anumanyatām iti dvitīyām
7.15.5.b.d: तेषां यं वव्रिरे देवास् तं स्वराड् अनुमन्यताम् इति द्वितीयाम्
7.15.5.b.m: 'Among them, whichever the gods have chosen, let the sovereign ruler consent to that'—with this second [verse he offers the second].

7.15.6.a.m: With: 'Those who, while being bound...', [he offers] while [the victim] is being unfastened.

7.15.6.b.m: With: 'Those who unfasten...', [he offers] while it is being led forth.

7.15.7.a.s: revatīr yajñapatiṃ priyadhā viśateti vapāśrapaṇībhyāṃ paśum anvārabhete adhvaryur yajamānaś ca /
7.15.7.a.d: रेवतीर् यज्ञपतिं प्रियधा विशतेति वपाश्रपणीभ्यां पशुम् अन्वारभेते अध्वर्युर् यजमानश् च ।
7.15.7.a.m: With: 'O wealthy ones, enter the lord of sacrifice affectionately!', the adhvaryu and the sacrificer touch the victim with the two omentum-cooking spits.

7.15.7.b.s: āśrāvya pratyāśrāvite saṃpreṣyaty upapreṣya hotar havyā devebhya iti
7.15.7.b.d: आश्राव्य प्रत्याश्राविते संप्रेष्यत्य् उपप्रेष्य होतर् हव्या देवेभ्य इति
7.15.7.b.m: Having called for attention and having been responded to, he issues the call: 'Prompt [the gods], hotṛ, [to receive] the offerings for the gods!'

7.15.8.a.s: prāsmā agniṃ bharata stṛṇīta barhir iti hotur abhijñāyāhavanīyād ulmukam ādāyāgnīdhraḥ pūrvaḥ pratipadyate
7.15.8.a.d: प्रास्मा अग्निं भरत स्तृणीत बर्हिर् इति होतुर् अभिज्ञायाहवनीयाद् उल्मुकम् आदायाग्नीध्रः पूर्वः प्रतिपद्यते
7.15.8.a.m: Recognizing [the words] of the hotṛ, 'Carry forward the fire for him, strew the barhis!', the agnīdh, taking a firebrand from the āhavanīya, goes forward first.

7.15.10.a.s: uro aṃtarikṣety antarā cātvālotkarāv udañcaṃ paśuṃ nayanti
7.15.10.a.d: उरो अंतरिक्षेत्य् अन्तरा चात्वालोत्कराव् उदञ्चं पशुं नयन्ति
7.15.10.a.m: With: 'O wide atmosphere...', they lead the victim northward between the cātvāla pit and the rubbish heap.

7.15.11.a.m: 'Different is the breath of the sacrificer from that of the animal,' the adhvaryu murmurs.

7.16.1.a.s: ūvadhyagohaṃ pārthivaṃ khanatād ity abhijñāyovadhyagohaṃ khanati
7.16.1.a.d: ऊवध्यगोहं पार्थिवं खनताद् इत्य् अभिज्ञायोवध्यगोहं खनति
7.16.1.a.m: Recognizing [the words]: 'Dig an earthly ditch for the bowel contents!', he digs a ditch for the bowel contents.

7.16.2.a.m: He sets down the firebrand in the place around which the fire was carried.

7.16.4.a.s: taṃ dakṣiṇena pratyañcaṃ paśum avasthāpya pṛthivyāḥ saṃpṛcaḥ pāhīti tasyādhastād barhir upāsyaty upākaraṇayor anyatarat
7.16.4.a.d: तं दक्षिणेन प्रत्यञ्चं पशुम् अवस्थाप्य पृथिव्याः संपृचः पाहीति तस्याधस्ताद् बर्हिर् उपास्यत्य् उपाकरणयोर् अन्यतरत्
7.16.4.a.m: Having halted the victim to the south of it facing west, he throws under it a barhis with: 'Protect from contact with the earth!', either of the two [blades used at] the dedication.

7.16.5.a.m: On it they quiet [the victim] with its head facing west and its feet facing north.

7.16.6.a.s: amāyuṃ kṛṇvantaṃ saṃjñapayatety uktvā parāṅ āvartate 'dhvaryuḥ
7.16.6.a.d: अमायुं कृण्वन्तं संज्ञपयतेत्य् उक्त्वा पराङ् आवर्तते ऽध्वर्युः
7.16.6.a.m: Having said: 'Quiet it without making it utter a bleat!', the adhvaryu turns away.

7.16.7.a.s: svarvid asi svar vittvā svar ihi svar mahyaṃ svaḥ paśubhyaḥ /
7.16.7.a.d: स्वर्विद् असि स्वर् वित्त्वा स्वर् इहि स्वर् मह्यं स्वः पशुभ्यः ।
7.16.7.a.m: 'You are the finder of heaven; having found heaven, go to heaven; heaven for me, heaven for the cattle!'

7.16.7.b.s: lokavid asi lokaṃ vittvā lokam ihi lokaṃ mahyaṃ lokaṃ paśubhyaḥ /
7.16.7.b.d: लोकविद् असि लोकं वित्त्वा लोकम् इहि लोकं मह्यं लोकं पशुभ्यः ।
7.16.7.b.m: 'You are the finder of the world; having found the world, go to the world; the world for me, the world for the cattle!'

7.16.7.c.s: gātuvid asi gātuṃ vittvā gātum ihi gātuṃ mahyaṃ gātuṃ paśubhyaḥ /
7.16.7.c.d: गातुविद् असि गातुं वित्त्वा गातुम् इहि गातुं मह्यं गातुं पशुभ्यः ।
7.16.7.c.m: 'You are the finder of the path; having found the path, go along the path; the path for me, the path for the cattle!'

7.16.7.d.s: nāthavid asi nāthaṃ vittvā nātham ihi nāthaṃ mahyaṃ nāthaṃ paśubhyaḥ /
7.16.7.d.d: नाथविद् असि नाथं वित्त्वा नाथम् इहि नाथं मह्यं नाथं पशुभ्यः ।
7.16.7.d.m: 'You are the finder of refuge; having found refuge, go to refuge; refuge for me, refuge for the cattle!'

7.16.7.e.s: na vā uv etan mriyase na riṣyasi devām̐ ideṣi pathibhiḥ sugebhiḥ yatra yanti sukṛto nāpi duṣkṛtastatra tvā devaḥ savitā dadhātu //
7.16.7.e.d: न वा उव् एतन् म्रियसे न रिष्यसि देवाम्̐ इदेषि पथिभिः सुगेभिः यत्र यन्ति सुकृतो नापि दुष्कृतस्तत्र त्वा देवः सविता दधातु ॥
7.16.7.e.m: 'Indeed you do not die here, nor are you harmed; you go to the gods along paths easy to traverse; / where the doers of good deeds go, not the evildoers, there may the god Savitṛ place you!'

7.16.7.f.m: [And] this [verse]: 'From the quarters to the guardians of the quarters...'

7.16.7.g.s: viśvā āśā madhunā saṃsṛjāmyanamīvā āpa oṣadhayo bhavantu /
7.16.7.g.d: विश्वा आशा मधुना संसृजाम्यनमीवा आप ओषधयो भवन्तु ।
7.16.7.g.m: 'I unite all the quarters with sweetness; let the waters and plants be free from disease!'

7.16.7.i.s: agṛbhītāḥ paśvaḥ santu sarva ity uktvā parāṅ āvartate yajamānaḥ //
7.16.7.i.d: अगृभीताः पश्वः सन्तु सर्व इत्य् उक्त्वा पराङ् आवर्तते यजमानः ॥
7.16.7.i.m: Having said: 'Let all the cattle be unseized!', the sacrificer turns away.

7.16.7.j.s: nānā prāṇo yajamānasya paśunety adhvaryur japati
7.16.7.j.d: नाना प्राणो यजमानस्य पशुनेत्य् अध्वर्युर् जपति
7.16.7.j.m: 'Different is the breath of the sacrificer from that of the animal,' the adhvaryu murmurs.

7.17.1.a.s: yāsām ūdhaś caturbilaṃ madhoḥ pūrṇaṃ ghṛtasya ca /
7.17.1.a.d: यासाम् ऊधश् चतुर्बिलं मधोः पूर्णं घृतस्य च ।
7.17.1.a.m: 'Those whose four-apertured udder is full of honey and clarified butter, /'

7.17.1.b.s: tā naḥ santu payasvatīr asmin goṣṭhe vayovṛdhaḥ //
7.17.1.b.d: ता नः सन्तु पयस्वतीर् अस्मिन् गोष्ठे वयोवृधः ॥
7.17.1.b.m: 'let them be full of milk for us, thriving in vigour in this pen! /'

7.17.1.c.s: iha paśavo viśvarūpā ramantām asmin yajñe viśvavido ghṛtācīḥ /
7.17.1.c.d: इह पशवो विश्वरूपा रमन्ताम् अस्मिन् यज्ञे विश्वविदो घृताचीः ।
7.17.1.c.m: 'Here let the all-formed cattle revel; in this sacrifice, [the spoons] that know all, turned toward clarified butter; /'

7.17.1.d.s: agniṃ kulāyam abhisaṃvasānā asmām̐ avantu payasā ghṛteneti pṛṣadājyam avekṣamāṇau vāgyatāv āsāte adhvaryur yajamānaś ca
7.17.1.d.d: अग्निं कुलायम् अभिसंवसाना अस्माम्̐ अवन्तु पयसा घृतेनेति पृषदाज्यम् अवेक्षमाणौ वाग्यताव् आसाते अध्वर्युर् यजमानश् च
7.17.1.d.m: dwelling together around Agni the nest, let them favor us with milk and clarified butter!'—gazing at the curd-butter mixture, the adhvaryu and the sacrificer sit restraining their speech.

7.17.2.a.s: indrasya bhagaḥ suvite dadhātanemaṃ yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ ca sūrau /
7.17.2.a.d: इन्द्रस्य भगः सुविते दधातनेमं यज्ञं यजमानं च सूरौ ।
7.17.2.a.m: 'Place Indra's share in prosperity, this sacrifice and the sacrificer in the sun! /'

7.17.2.b.s: yo no dveṣṭy anu taṃ ravasvānāgaso yajamānasya vīrā iti ca vāśyamāne 'vekṣete
7.17.2.b.d: यो नो द्वेष्ट्य् अनु तं रवस्वानागसो यजमानस्य वीरा इति च वाश्यमाने ऽवेक्षेते
7.17.2.b.m: Whoever hates us, roar after him! Guiltless are the heroes of the sacrificer!'—and if [the victim] bleats, they gaze [at it with this verse].

7.17.3.a.s: yat paśur māyum akṛteti saṃjñapte saṃjñaptahomaṃ juhoti
7.17.3.a.d: यत् पशुर् मायुम् अकृतेति संज्ञप्ते संज्ञप्तहोमं जुहोति
7.17.3.a.m: When it has been quieted, he offers the quieted-offering with: 'That the animal made a bleat...'

7.17.4.a.s: śamitāra upetaneti vapāśrapaṇībhyāṃ paśum upaito 'dhvaryur yajamānaś ca
7.17.4.a.d: शमितार उपेतनेति वपाश्रपणीभ्यां पशुम् उपैतो ऽध्वर्युर् यजमानश् च
7.17.4.a.m: With: 'O slaughterers, approach!', the adhvaryu and the sacrificer approach the victim with the two omentum-cooking spits.

7.17.5.a.s: paśoḥ pāśaṃ pramuñcaty aditiḥ pāśaṃ pramumoktv etam iti
7.17.5.a.d: पशोः पाशं प्रमुञ्चत्य् अदितिः पाशं प्रमुमोक्त्व् एतम् इति
7.17.5.a.m: He unfastens the cord of the animal with: 'May Aditi unfasten this cord!'

7.17.6.a.s: saṃveṣṭya raśanāṃ grīvāsu nidhāyaikaśūlayopasajya cātvāla udasyaty arātīyantam adharaṃ karomīti
7.17.6.a.d: संवेष्ट्य रशनां ग्रीवासु निधायैकशूलयोपसज्य चात्वाल उदस्यत्य् अरातीयन्तम् अधरं करोमीति
7.17.6.a.m: Having coiled the cord, placed it around [the victim's] neck, and fastened it with the single spit, he throws it into the cātvāla pit with: 'I bring down him who acts maliciously!'

7.17.7.a.s: yady abhicared arātīyantam adharaṃ kṛṇomi yaṃ dviṣmas tasmin pratimuñcāmi pāśam iti tayā vṛkṣaṃ sthāṇuṃ stambhaṃ vāpidadhyāt
7.17.7.a.d: यद्य् अभिचरेद् अरातीयन्तम् अधरं कृणोमि यं द्विष्मस् तस्मिन् प्रतिमुञ्चामि पाशम् इति तया वृक्षं स्थाणुं स्तम्भं वापिदध्यात्
7.17.7.a.m: If he would practice sorcery, he should fasten it onto a tree, a stump, or a post with: 'I bring down him who acts maliciously; onto him whom we hate I fasten the cord!'

7.18.1.a.m: Then the pratiprasthātṛ brings forward the wife [of the sacrificer].

7.18.2.a.s: namas ta ātāneti patny ādityam upatiṣṭhate
7.18.2.a.d: नमस् त आतानेति पत्न्य् आदित्यम् उपतिष्ठते
7.18.2.a.m: The wife worships the sun with: 'Homage to you, O Outstretched One!'

7.18.3.a.s: anarvā prehīti prācīm udānayaty anumantrayata ity eke
7.18.3.a.d: अनर्वा प्रेहीति प्राचीम् उदानयत्य् अनुमन्त्रयत इत्य् एके
7.18.3.a.m: He leads her forward facing east with: 'Advance unobstructed!'; or he addresses her [with this], say some.

7.18.4.a.s: āpo devīḥ śuddhāyuva iti cātvāle patny apo 'vamṛśaty ṛtvijo yajamānaś ca
7.18.4.a.d: आपो देवीः शुद्धायुव इति चात्वाले पत्न्य् अपो ऽवमृशत्य् ऋत्विजो यजमानश् च
7.18.4.a.m: With: 'O divine waters, purifying...', the wife touches the water in the cātvāla pit, and [so do] the officiating priests and the sacrificer.

7.18.6.a.m: With water he invigorates all the breath-openings of the animal.

7.18.7.a.s: sarvāṇy aṅgāny adhvaryur abhiṣiñcati patny āpyāyayati /
7.18.7.a.d: सर्वाण्य् अङ्गान्य् अध्वर्युर् अभिषिञ्चति पत्न्य् आप्याययति ।
7.18.7.a.m: The adhvaryu sprinkles all the limbs; the wife invigorates [them].

7.18.7.c.s: vāk ta āpyāyatām ity etair yathāliṅgam
7.18.7.c.d: वाक् त आप्यायताम् इत्य् एतैर् यथालिङ्गम्
7.18.7.c.m: With the [formulas] beginning with: 'May your speech be invigorated...', according to their characteristic marks.

7.18.8.a.s: yā te prāṇāñ chug jagāmeti hṛdayadeśam
7.18.8.a.d: या ते प्राणाञ् छुग् जगामेति हृदयदेशम्
7.18.8.a.m: [He touches] the region of the heart with: “May the sorrow that has gone to your vital breaths…”

7.18.9.a.m: The penis with: “May your penis swell…”

7.18.10.a.m: The feet with: “Pure are the moving [feet]…”

7.18.11.a.s: ekaikam āpyāyya japati śam adbhya iti purā stokānāṃ bhūmeḥ prāpaṇāt
7.18.11.a.d: एकैकम् आप्याय्य जपति शम् अद्भ्य इति पुरा स्तोकानां भूमेः प्रापणात्
7.18.11.a.m: Having made each [limb] swell, he mutters: “Homage to the waters!” before drops reach the ground.

7.18.12.a.s: śam oṣadhībhyaḥ śaṃ pṛthivyā iti bhūmyāṃ śesaṃ ninīyauṣadhe trāyasvainam ity upākaraṇayor avaśiṣṭaṃ dakṣiṇena nābhim antardhāya svadhite mainaṃ hiṃsīr iti svadhitinā pārśvatas tiryag ācchyati
7.18.12.a.d: शम् ओषधीभ्यः शं पृथिव्या इति भूम्यां शेसं निनीयौषधे त्रायस्वैनम् इत्य् उपाकरणयोर् अवशिष्टं दक्षिणेन नाभिम् अन्तर्धाय स्वधिते मैनं हिंसीर् इति स्वधितिना पार्श्वतस् तिर्यग् आच्छ्यति
7.18.12.a.m: Having poured the remainder on the ground with: “Homage to the plants, homage to the earth!” [and] having placed what was left of the two upākaraṇa [grass-blades] south of the navel with: “O plant, protect him!”, he cuts sideways along the flank with the knife, [saying:] “O knife, do not harm him!”

7.18.13.a.m: With his left hand he takes the tip of the sacrificial grass.

7.18.14.a.s: atha madhyaṃ yata ācchyati tad ubhayato lohitenāṅktvā rakṣasāṃ bhāgo 'sīty uttaram aparam avāntaradeśaṃ nirasyāthainat savyena padābhitiṣṭhatīdam ahaṃ rakṣo 'vabādha idam ahaṃ rakṣo 'dhamaṃ tamo nayāmīti
7.18.14.a.d: अथ मध्यं यत आच्छ्यति तद् उभयतो लोहितेनाङ्क्त्वा रक्षसां भागो ऽसीत्य् उत्तरम् अपरम् अवान्तरदेशं निरस्याथैनत् सव्येन पदाभितिष्ठतीदम् अहं रक्षो ऽवबाध इदम् अहं रक्षो ऽधमं तमो नयामीति
7.18.14.a.m: Then, having smeared its middle on both sides with blood from where he cuts, [and] having thrown it toward the north-western intermediate direction with: “You are the portion of the Rakṣases,” he steps on it with his left foot, [saying:] “Here I trample the Rakṣas; here I lead the Rakṣas to the lowest darkness.”

7.19.1.a.s: iṣe tveti vapām utkhidya ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī prorṇvāthām iti vapayā dviśūlāṃ pracchādyorje tveti taniṣṭhe 'ntata ekaśūlayopatṛṇatti
7.19.1.a.d: इषे त्वेति वपाम् उत्खिद्य घृतेन द्यावापृथिवी प्रोर्ण्वाथाम् इति वपया द्विशूलां प्रच्छाद्योर्जे त्वेति तनिष्ठे ऽन्तत एकशूलयोपतृणत्ति
7.19.1.a.m: Having pulled out the omentum with: “For sap thee!”, having covered the two-pronged spit with the omentum with: “Do you two, Heaven and Earth, cover [yourselves] with fat!”, he pierces it at the end on the thinnest [part] with the one-pronged spit, [saying:] “For strength thee!”

7.19.2.a.s: devebhyaḥ kalpasvety abhimantrya devebhyaḥ śūndhasvety adbhir avokṣya devebhyaḥ śūmbhasveti svadhitinā vapāṃ nimṛjyācchinno rāyaḥ suvīra indrāgnibhyāṃ tvā juṣṭām utkṛntāmīty utkṛntati
7.19.2.a.d: देवेभ्यः कल्पस्वेत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य देवेभ्यः शून्धस्वेत्य् अद्भिर् अवोक्ष्य देवेभ्यः शूम्भस्वेति स्वधितिना वपां निमृज्याच्छिन्नो रायः सुवीर इन्द्राग्निभ्यां त्वा जुष्टाम् उत्कृन्तामीत्य् उत्कृन्तति
7.19.2.a.m: Having addressed it with: “Be fit for the gods!”, having sprinkled it with water with: “Be pure for the gods!”, having wiped the omentum with the knife with: “Be adorned for the gods!”, he cuts it off with: “Unsevered [be] the wealth with noble heroes; I cut you off, acceptable to Indra and Agni.”

7.19.3.a.s: muṣṭinā śamitā vapoddharaṇam apidhāyāsta ā vapāyā homāt
7.19.3.a.d: मुष्टिना शमिता वपोद्धरणम् अपिधायास्त आ वपाया होमात्
7.19.3.a.m: Covering the incision for extracting the omentum with his fist, the slaughterer sits until the offering of the omentum.

7.19.4.a.s: pratyuṣṭaṃ rakṣaḥ pratyuṣṭā arātaya iti śāmitre vapāṃ pratitapya namaḥ sūryasya saṃdṛśa ity ādityam upasthāyorv antarikṣam anv ihīty abhipravrajati
7.19.4.a.d: प्रत्युष्टं रक्षः प्रत्युष्टा अरातय इति शामित्रे वपां प्रतितप्य नमः सूर्यस्य संदृश इत्य् आदित्यम् उपस्थायोर्व् अन्तरिक्षम् अन्व् इहीत्य् अभिप्रव्रजति
7.19.4.a.m: Having heated the omentum at the Śāmitra [fire] with: “Scorched is the Rakṣas, scorched are the enemies!”, having attended the sun with: “Homage to the sight of the sun!”, he walks forward with: “Go along the wide atmosphere!”

7.19.5.a.m: Taking a piece of a firebrand, the agnīdh proceeds first.

7.19.6.a.m: The sacrificer touches the omentum-spits from behind again.

7.19.7.a.m: He throws the piece of firebrand back into the āhavanīya.

7.19.8.a.s: nirdagdhaṃ rakṣo nirdagdhā arātaya ity āhavanīyasyāntame 'ṅgāre vapāṃ nikūḍyāntarā yūpam āhavanīyaṃ ca dakṣiṇātihṛtya pratiprasthātre prayacchati
7.19.8.a.d: निर्दग्धं रक्षो निर्दग्धा अरातय इत्य् आहवनीयस्यान्तमे ऽङ्गारे वपां निकूड्यान्तरा यूपम् आहवनीयं च दक्षिणातिहृत्य प्रतिप्रस्थात्रे प्रयच्छति
7.19.8.a.m: Having singed the omentum over the nearest coal of the āhavanīya with: “Burned away is the Rakṣas, burned away are the enemies!”, [and] having brought it across to the south between the sacrificial post and the āhavanīya, he gives it to the pratiprasthātṛ.

7.19.9.a.m: Seated to the south, the pratiprasthātṛ roasts it at the āhavanīya.

7.20.1.a.s: vāyo vīhi stokānām iti barhiṣo 'gram adhastād vapāyā upāsyati
7.20.1.a.d: वायो वीहि स्तोकानाम् इति बर्हिषो ऽग्रम् अधस्ताद् वपाया उपास्यति
7.20.1.a.m: He throws the tip of the sacrificial grass under the omentum with: “O Vāyu, enjoy the drops!”

7.20.2.a.s: tvām u te dadhire havyavāham iti sruveṇa vapām abhijuhoti
7.20.2.a.d: त्वाम् उ ते दधिरे हव्यवाहम् इति स्रुवेण वपाम् अभिजुहोति
7.20.2.a.m: With the dipping spoon he makes an offering over the omentum with: “Thee indeed they established as the bearer of oblations…”

7.20.3.a.m: When the drops have appeared, he gives the ritual call: “Recite [the invitatory verse] for the drops!”

7.20.4.a.s: alohinīṃ suśṛtāṃ kṛtvā supippalā oṣadhīḥ kṛdhīti dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇyāṃ barhiṣi plakṣaśākhāyām āsādya prayutā dveṣāṃsīti vapāśrapaṇī pravṛhya nidhāya ghṛtavati śabde juhūpabhṛtāv ādāya dakṣiṇātikramyāśrāvya pratyāśrāvite saṃpreṣyati svāhākṛtībhyaḥ preṣya svāhākṛtibhyaḥ preṣyeti vā
7.20.4.a.d: अलोहिनीं सुशृतां कृत्वा सुपिप्पला ओषधीः कृधीति दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोण्यां बर्हिषि प्लक्षशाखायाम् आसाद्य प्रयुता द्वेषांसीति वपाश्रपणी प्रवृह्य निधाय घृतवति शब्दे जुहूपभृताव् आदाय दक्षिणातिक्रम्याश्राव्य प्रत्याश्राविते संप्रेष्यति स्वाहाकृतीभ्यः प्रेष्य स्वाहाकृतिभ्यः प्रेष्येति वा
7.20.4.a.m: Having made it free of blood and well cooked, having placed it down on a plakṣa branch on the sacrificial grass on the southern hip of the altar ground with: “Make the plants fruitful!”, having pulled off and deposited the omentum-spits with: “Separated are the hatreds!”, when there is a sizzling sound, taking the juhū and upabhṛt, having stepped across to the south, having called for the response, when the response is given, he gives the ritual call: “Prompt for the Svāhā-cries!” or “Prompt for the Svāhā-offerings!”

7.20.5.a.s: vaṣaṭkṛte hutvā pratyākramya śeṣeṇa dhruvām abhighārya pṛṣadājyam abhighārayatyatha vapām /
7.20.5.a.d: वषट्कृते हुत्वा प्रत्याक्रम्य शेषेण ध्रुवाम् अभिघार्य पृषदाज्यम् अभिघारयत्यथ वपाम् ।
7.20.5.a.m: Having offered when the vaṣaṭ-call is made, having returned, he bastes the dhruvā with the remainder, bastes the speckled butter, and then the omentum;

7.20.9.a.s: svāhā devebhya iti pūrvaṃ parivapyaṃ hutvā juhvām upastīrya hiraṇyaśakalam avadhāya kṛtsnāṃ vapām avadāya hiraṇyaśakalam upariṣṭāt kṛtvābhighārayati
7.20.9.a.d: स्वाहा देवेभ्य इति पूर्वं परिवप्यं हुत्वा जुह्वाम् उपस्तीर्य हिरण्यशकलम् अवधाय कृत्स्नां वपाम् अवदाय हिरण्यशकलम् उपरिष्टात् कृत्वाभिघारयति
7.20.9.a.m: Having offered the first parivapya with: “Svāhā to the gods!”, having spread an underlayer [of butter] in the juhū, having put a piece of gold in it, having cut off the whole omentum, [and] having placed a piece of gold on top, he bastes [it].

7.20.10.a.m: Thus it becomes a fivefold cutting.

7.20.11.a.m: Even for one who cuts fourfold, it should be a fivefold cutting only.

7.21.1.a.s: indrāgnibhyāṃ chāgasya vapāyā medaso 'nubrūhīndrāgnibhyāṃ chāgasya vapāyā medasaḥ preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau
7.21.1.a.d: इन्द्राग्निभ्यां छागस्य वपाया मेदसो ऽनुब्रूहीन्द्राग्निभ्यां छागस्य वपाया मेदसः प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौ
7.21.1.a.m: “Recite for Indra and Agni of the fat of the goat's omentum,” [and] “Prompt for Indra and Agni for the fat of the goat's omentum,” are the two ritual calls.

7.21.2.a.s: jātavedo vapayā gaccha devān iti vaṣaṭkṛte hutvā pratyākramya devebhyaḥ svāhety uttaraṃ parivapyaṃ hutvā vapoddharaṇam abhighārayaty uttaratas tiṣṭhan
7.21.2.a.d: जातवेदो वपया गच्छ देवान् इति वषट्कृते हुत्वा प्रत्याक्रम्य देवेभ्यः स्वाहेत्य् उत्तरं परिवप्यं हुत्वा वपोद्धरणम् अभिघारयत्य् उत्तरतस् तिष्ठन्
7.21.2.a.m: Having offered when the vaṣaṭ-call is made with: “O Jātavedas, go to the gods with the omentum!”, having returned, having offered the second parivapya with: “To the gods, svāhā!”, standing to the north, he bastes the incision for extracting the omentum.

7.21.3.a.s: pratiprasthātāhavanīye vapāśrapaṇī praharati svāhordhvanabhasaṃ mārutaṃ gacchatam iti prācīṃ dviśūlāṃ pratīcīm ekaśūlām /
7.21.3.a.d: प्रतिप्रस्थाताहवनीये वपाश्रपणी प्रहरति स्वाहोर्ध्वनभसं मारुतं गच्छतम् इति प्राचीं द्विशूलां प्रतीचीम् एकशूलाम् ।
7.21.3.a.m: The pratiprasthātṛ throws the two omentum-spits into the āhavanīya with: “Svāhā! Go ye two to the high sky, to the Maruts!”, the two-pronged one eastward and the one-pronged one westward;

7.21.4.a.m: Then the adhvaryu pours the oblational remnant over them.

7.21.5.a.s: atra yajamāno varaṃ dadāty anaḍvāhaṃ tisro vā dhenūs tisro vā dakṣiṇāḥ
7.21.5.a.d: अत्र यजमानो वरं ददात्य् अनड्वाहं तिस्रो वा धेनूस् तिस्रो वा दक्षिणाः
7.21.5.a.m: Here the sacrificer gives a boon: an ox, or three cows, or three sacrificial gifts.

7.21.6.a.m: Having stepped out together with the wife, they sprinkle themselves at the pit with five [verses]:

7.21.6.b.s: āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuva iti tisraḥ //
7.21.6.b.d: आपो हि ष्ठा मयोभुव इति तिस्रः ॥
7.21.6.b.m: The three: “Waters indeed are ye, joyful…”;

7.21.6.c.s: idam āpaḥ pravahatāvadyaṃ ca malaṃ ca yat /
7.21.6.c.d: इदम् आपः प्रवहतावद्यं च मलं च यत् ।
7.21.6.c.m: “Carry away, O waters, this whatever is blameworthy and foul,

7.21.6.d.s: yad vābhidudrohānṛtaṃ yad vā śepe abhīruṇam //
7.21.6.d.d: यद् वाभिदुद्रोहानृतं यद् वा शेपे अभीरुणम् ॥
7.21.6.d.m: and whatever falsehood I have practiced maliciously, or whatever I have sworn recklessly;

7.21.6.e.m: may the waters release me from that sin, from every distress!

7.21.6.f.m: I release myself from the curse, I release myself from Varuṇa,

7.21.6.g.m: I release myself from Yama's fetter, from every sin against the gods, and from sin against men.”

7.22.1.a.m: He undertakes the rite beginning with the setting down of the vessels for the animal cake.

7.22.2.a.m: The arrangement of the vessels is according to the purpose.

7.22.3.a.s: nirvapaṇakāle vrīhimayaṃ paśupuroḍāśaṃ nirvapaty ekādaśakapālaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ vā
7.22.3.a.d: निर्वपणकाले व्रीहिमयं पशुपुरोडाशं निर्वपत्य् एकादशकपालं द्वादशकपालं वा
7.22.3.a.m: At the time of pouring out the oblation, he pours out the animal cake made of rice, on eleven potsherds or on twelve potsherds.

7.22.4.a.m: It has the deity of the animal [sacrifice].

7.22.5.a.m: Having released speech with the haviṣkṛt-call, he cuts up the animal.

7.22.6.a.s: hṛdayaṃ jihvā vakṣo yakṛd vṛkyau savyaṃ dor ubhe pārśve dakṣiṇā śroṇir gudatṛtīyam iti daivatāni /
7.22.6.a.d: हृदयं जिह्वा वक्षो यकृद् वृक्यौ सव्यं दोर् उभे पार्श्वे दक्षिणा श्रोणिर् गुदतृतीयम् इति दैवतानि ।
7.22.6.a.m: The heart, tongue, breast, liver, two kidneys, left foreleg, both flanks, right hip, [and] the third part of the rectum are the portions for the deity;

7.22.6.b.s: dakṣiṇaṃ doḥ savyā śroṇir gudatṛtīyam iti sauviṣṭakṛtāni /
7.22.6.b.d: दक्षिणं दोः सव्या श्रोणिर् गुदतृतीयम् इति सौविष्टकृतानि ।
7.22.6.b.m: the right foreleg, left hip, [and] the third part of the rectum are the portions for Sviṣṭakṛt;

7.22.6.c.s: klomānaṃ plīhānaṃ purītataṃ vaniṣṭhum adhyūdhnīṃ medo jāghanīm ity uddharati
7.22.6.c.d: क्लोमानं प्लीहानं पुरीततं वनिष्ठुम् अध्यूध्नीं मेदो जाघनीम् इत्य् उद्धरति
7.22.6.c.m: he extracts the lungs, spleen, pericardium, rectum, fatty part of the udder, fat, [and] the hindquarters.

7.22.7.a.m: He gives the ritual call: “Do not tear the intestine!”

7.22.8.a.m: The meaning is: “Do not turn it inside out.”

7.22.9.a.s: udakpavitre kumbhyāṃ paśumavadhāya śūle praṇīkṣya hṛdayaṃ śāmitre śrapayati
7.22.9.a.d: उदक्पवित्रे कुम्भ्यां पशुमवधाय शूले प्रणीक्ष्य हृदयं शामित्रे श्रपयति
7.22.9.a.m: Having placed the animal into a pot with northward strainers, [and] having pierced the heart with a spit, he roasts it at the Śāmitra [fire].

7.22.10.a.m: He undertakes the rite beginning with the pounding [of the grain].

7.22.11.a.m: Having performed the rite with the omentum, he performs the rite with the sacrificial cake;

7.22.12.a.m: “Recite for Indra and Agni of the cake,” [and] “Prompt for Indra and Agni for the cake,” are the two ritual calls;

7.22.12.b.m: or: “Recite for Indra and Agni of the cake being cut off,” [and] “Prompt for Indra and Agni for the cake.”

7.22.13.a.d: अग्नये ऽनुब्रूह्य् अग्नये प्रेष्येति स्विष्टकृतः संप्रैषौ
7.22.13.a.m: “Recite for Agni,” [and] “Prompt for Agni,” are the two ritual calls for Sviṣṭakṛt.

7.23.1.a.m: Having cut off the prāśitra portion [and] the iḍā, [he does] not [cut off] the sacrificer's portion.

7.23.2.a.m: [The rite of the cake] concludes starting with the oblations of the offering-material up to the iḍā.

7.23.3.a.s: upahutāṃ maitrāvaruṇaṣaṣṭhā bhakṣayitvā pūrvavat prastare mārjayitvā sruveṇa pṛṣadājyasyopahatya vedenopayamya triḥ pṛcchati śṛtaṃ havīḥ3 śamitar iti
7.23.3.a.d: उपहुतां मैत्रावरुणषष्ठा भक्षयित्वा पूर्ववत् प्रस्तरे मार्जयित्वा स्रुवेण पृषदाज्यस्योपहत्य वेदेनोपयम्य त्रिः पृच्छति शृतं हवीः3 शमितर् इति
7.23.3.a.m: Having partaken of [the iḍā] once invited, six including the Maitrāvaruṇa, and cleansed themselves on the grass bunch as before, scooping clotted butter with the sruva and holding a grass broom underneath, [the adhvaryu] asks three times: 'Is the offering-material cooked, O butcher?'

7.23.5.a.m: [He asks] the second time half-way [along the path], the third time upon arriving.

7.23.6.a.d: पूषा मा पशुपाः पात्विति प्रथमे ऽभिप्रव्रजति ।
7.23.6.a.m: At the first [question] he walks forward with: 'May Pūṣan protect me, the keeper of beasts!'

7.23.6.b.s: pūṣā mā pathipāḥ pātv iti dvitīye /
7.23.6.b.d: पूषा मा पथिपाः पात्व् इति द्वितीये ।
7.23.6.b.m: At the second with: 'May Pūṣan protect me, the guardian of the paths!'

7.23.6.c.m: At the third with: 'May Pūṣan protect me, the overlord!'

7.23.7.a.s: śūlāt pravṛhya hṛdayaṃ kumbhyām avadhāya saṃ te manasā mana iti pṛṣadājyena hṛdayam abhighārayaty uttarataḥ parikramya
7.23.7.a.d: शूलात् प्रवृह्य हृदयं कुम्भ्याम् अवधाय सं ते मनसा मन इति पृषदाज्येन हृदयम् अभिघारयत्य् उत्तरतः परिक्रम्य
7.23.7.a.m: Having pulled the heart off the spit and placed it in the cooking pot, stepping around to the north, he bastes the heart with clotted butter, [saying]: 'May your mind unite with the mind.'

7.23.8.a.s: ājyena paśuṃ yasta ātmā paśuṣu praviṣṭa iti
7.23.8.a.d: आज्येन पशुं यस्त आत्मा पशुषु प्रविष्ट इति
7.23.8.a.m: [He bastes] the animal [offerings] with clarified butter, [saying]: 'That self of yours which has entered into beasts...'

7.23.9.a.d: स्वाहोष्मणो ऽव्यथिष्या इत्य् उद्यन्तम् ऊस्माणम् अनुमन्त्रयते
7.23.9.a.m: He addresses the rising steam with: 'Hail to the steam! May you not tremble!'

7.23.10.a.s: paśuṃ haran pārśvato hṛdayaśūlaṃ dhārayaty anupaspṛśann ātmānam itarāṃś ca
7.23.10.a.d: पशुं हरन् पार्श्वतो हृदयशूलं धारयत्य् अनुपस्पृशन्न् आत्मानम् इतरांश् च
7.23.10.a.m: Carrying the animal [portions], he holds the heart-spit at his side, touching neither himself nor the others.

7.23.11.a.s: antarā yūpam āhavanīyaṃ ca dakṣiṇātihṛtya pañcahotrā ṣaḍḍhotrā vā dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇyām āsādya catasṛṣūpastṛnīte juhūpabhṛtor vasāhomahavanyāṃ samavattadhānyām iti
7.23.11.a.d: अन्तरा यूपम् आहवनीयं च दक्षिणातिहृत्य पञ्चहोत्रा षड्ढोत्रा वा दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोण्याम् आसाद्य चतसृषूपस्तृनीते जुहूपभृतोर् वसाहोमहवन्यां समवत्तधान्याम् इति
7.23.11.a.m: Having carried them across to the south between the sacrificial post and the āhavanīya, and set them down on the southern hip of the altar ground with the Pañcahotṛ or the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ [formula], he spreads an under-layer into four [receptacles]: into the juhū and upabhṛt, into the ladle for the fat offering, and into the vessel for cut-off portions.

7.23.12.a.s: juhūpabhṛtor hiraṇyaśakalāv avadhāya barhiṣi plakṣaśākhāyām avadānāny avadyan saṃpreṣyati
7.23.12.a.d: जुहूपभृतोर् हिरण्यशकलाव् अवधाय बर्हिषि प्लक्षशाखायाम् अवदानान्य् अवद्यन् संप्रेष्यति
7.23.12.a.m: Having placed gold chips into the juhū and upabhṛt, while cutting the portions upon the sacrificial grass on a branch of the plakṣa, he issues the call:

7.24.1.a.m: 'Recite for the Manotā [hymn] for the offering-material being portioned out.'

7.24.2.b.m: then of the tongue, then of the breast; as he pleases for the rest.

7.24.3.a.m: 'He cuts from the middle of the rectum'—thus it is stated.

7.24.5.a.m: Cutting twice each for the principal deities, he places [the portions] into the juhū;

7.24.5.b.m: once each into the upabhṛt for the Sviṣṭakṛt offerings.

7.24.6.a.s: gudaṃ traidhaṃ vibhajya sthavimad upayaḍbhyo nidhāya madhyamaṃ dvaidhaṃ vibhajya daivateṣv avadadhāti /
7.24.6.a.d: गुदं त्रैधं विभज्य स्थविमद् उपयड्भ्यो निधाय मध्यमं द्वैधं विभज्य दैवतेष्व् अवदधाति ।
7.24.6.a.m: Having divided the rectum into three, having set aside the thickest [part] for the supplementary offerings and divided the middle [part] into two, he places [one half] among the deity offerings;

7.24.6.b.m: the thinnest among the Sviṣṭakṛt offerings.

7.24.7.a.s: api vā dvaidhaṃ vibhajya sthavimad upayaḍbhyo nidhāyetarat traidhaṃ vibhajya madhyaṃ dvaidhaṃ vibhajya daivateṣv avadadhāti /
7.24.7.a.d: अपि वा द्वैधं विभज्य स्थविमद् उपयड्भ्यो निधायेतरत् त्रैधं विभज्य मध्यं द्वैधं विभज्य दैवतेष्व् अवदधाति ।
7.24.7.a.m: Or having divided it into two, having set aside the thickest [part] for the supplementary offerings and divided the other into three, and divided the middle into two, he places [one half] among the deity offerings;

7.24.7.b.m: the thinnest among the Sviṣṭakṛt offerings, the thickest in the iḍā.

7.24.8.a.s: tredhā medo 'vadyati dvibhāgaṃ srucos tṛtīyaṃ samavattadhānyām
7.24.8.a.d: त्रेधा मेदो ऽवद्यति द्विभागं स्रुचोस् तृतीयं समवत्तधान्याम्
7.24.8.a.m: He cuts the omentum fat into three: two portions into the two ladles, the third into the vessel for cut-off portions.

7.24.9.a.s: yūṣe medo 'vadhāya medasā srucau prāvṛtya hiraṇyaśakalāv upariṣṭātkṛtvābhighārayati
7.24.9.a.d: यूषे मेदो ऽवधाय मेदसा स्रुचौ प्रावृत्य हिरण्यशकलाव् उपरिष्टात्कृत्वाभिघारयति
7.24.9.a.m: Having placed fat in the broth, having covered the two ladles with fat, and having placed gold chips on top, he bastes [them].

7.24.10.a.m: In the vessel for cut-off portions he cuts the six first [portions for] the iḍā, the entrails as the seventh;

7.24.10.b.m: or from the six, with the entrails as the seventh.

7.24.11.a.m: He increases the iḍā with boneless pieces.

7.24.12.a.s: klomānaṃ plīhānaṃ purītatam ity anvavadhāya yūṣṇopasicyābhighārayati
7.24.12.a.d: क्लोमानं प्लीहानं पुरीततम् इत्य् अन्ववधाय यूष्णोपसिच्याभिघारयति
7.24.12.a.m: Having put the lungs, the spleen, and the pericardium alongside, and having poured over [them] with broth, he bastes [them].

7.25.1.a.s: apāṃ tvauṣadhīnāṃ rasaṃ gṛhṇāmīti vasāhomahavanyāṃ vasāhomaṃ gṛhṇāti
7.25.1.a.d: अपां त्वौषधीनां रसं गृह्णामीति वसाहोमहवन्यां वसाहोमं गृह्णाति
7.25.1.a.m: He takes the fat offering into the ladle for the fat offering with: 'I take you, the sap of waters, of plants.'

7.25.2.a.m: With the sacrificial knife he cuts the stream.

7.25.4.a.m: With a rib he stirs the fat offering, saying: 'You are prosperity.'

7.25.5.a.m: With the same [rib] he covers it, saying: 'By the course of the wind...';

7.25.5.b.m: or he stirs it with the sacrificial knife;

7.25.5.c.m: some say he covers it with the sacrificial knife.

7.25.6.a.s: atha yan na śīrṣṇo 'vadyati nāṃsayor nāṇūkasya nāparasakthyor anavadānīyāni
7.25.6.a.d: अथ यन् न शीर्ष्णो ऽवद्यति नांसयोर् नाणूकस्य नापरसक्थ्योर् अनवदानीयानि
7.25.6.a.m: Now, that which he does not cut: neither from the head, nor from the two shoulders, nor from the spine, nor from the two hind thighs—these are not to be portioned out.

7.25.7.a.s: tāni śṛtaiḥ saṃnidhāya saṃmṛśaty aindraḥ prāṇo aṅge-aṅga iti
7.25.7.a.d: तानि शृतैः संनिधाय संमृशत्य् ऐन्द्रः प्राणो अङ्गे-अङ्ग इति
7.25.7.a.m: Placing them together with the cooked [portions], he touches them, [saying]: 'Indra's breath in limb after limb...'

7.25.9.a.s: indrāgnibhyāṃ chāgasya haviṣo 'nubrūhīndrāgnibhyāṃ chāgasya haviṣaḥ preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau
7.25.9.a.d: इन्द्राग्निभ्यां छागस्य हविषो ऽनुब्रूहीन्द्राग्निभ्यां छागस्य हविषः प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौ
7.25.9.a.m: 'Recite for Indra and Agni for the goat offering-material; call upon [the hotṛ] for Indra and Agni for the goat offering-material'—[these are] the two calls.

7.25.10.a.s: yājyāyā ardharce pratiprasthātā vasāhomaṃ juhoti ghṛtaṃ ghṛtapāvānaḥ pibateti
7.25.10.a.d: याज्याया अर्धर्चे प्रतिप्रस्थाता वसाहोमं जुहोति घृतं घृतपावानः पिबतेति
7.25.10.a.m: At the half-verse of the consecratory verse, the pratiprasthātṛ offers the fat offering, [saying]: 'Drink clarified butter, you drinkers of clarified butter!'

7.25.11.a.s: udrekeṇa diśaḥ pradiśa iti pratidiśaṃ juhoti /
7.25.11.a.d: उद्रेकेण दिशः प्रदिश इति प्रतिदिशं जुहोति ।
7.25.11.a.m: With the residue he offers toward each quarter, [saying]: 'To the quarters, to the intermediate quarters';

7.25.12.a.s: prāñcam uttamaṃ saṃsthāpya namo digbhya ity upatiṣṭhate
7.25.12.a.d: प्राञ्चम् उत्तमं संस्थाप्य नमो दिग्भ्य इत्य् उपतिष्ठते
7.25.12.a.m: Having completed the last facing east, he pays reverence with: 'Homage to the quarters!'

7.25.14.a.m: Or here he may sacrifice toward the quarters;

7.25.14.b.m: or after Vanaspati, or after Sviṣṭakṛt.

7.25.15.a.s: pratyākramya juhvām upastīrya sakṛt pṛṣadājyasyopahatya dvir abhighārya vanaspataye 'nubrūhi vanaspataye preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau /
7.25.15.a.d: प्रत्याक्रम्य जुह्वाम् उपस्तीर्य सकृत् पृषदाज्यस्योपहत्य द्विर् अभिघार्य वनस्पतये ऽनुब्रूहि वनस्पतये प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौ ।
7.25.15.a.m: Having stepped back, spread an under-layer in the juhū, scooped clotted butter once, and basted twice: 'Recite for Vanaspati; call upon [the hotṛ] for Vanaspati' are the two calls;

7.25.16.a.m: As for Sviṣṭakṛt, the sacrificer accompanies with a formula.

7.25.17.a.s: uparyāhavanīye juhvāmaupabhṛtāni viparyasyann āhāgnaye sviṣṭakṛte 'nubrūhy agnaye sviṣṭakṛte preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau
7.25.17.a.d: उपर्याहवनीये जुह्वामौपभृतानि विपर्यस्यन्न् आहाग्नये स्विष्टकृते ऽनुब्रूह्य् अग्नये स्विष्टकृते प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौ
7.25.17.a.m: Turning the portions from the upabhṛt into the juhū over the āhavanīya, he says: 'Recite for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt; call upon [the hotṛ] for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt'—[these are] the two calls.

7.25.18.a.m: Having offered when the vaṣaṭ-call is made, and having stepped back, he places the two ladles in their place.

7.26.1.a.m: Here some prescribe the portioning of the iḍā.

7.26.3.a.m: Having spread an under-layer of fat, he bastes with fat.

7.26.4.a.s: yaṃ kāmayetāpaśuḥ syād ity amedaskaṃ tasmā ity uktam
7.26.4.a.d: यं कामयेतापशुः स्याद् इत्य् अमेदस्कं तस्मा इत्य् उक्तम्
7.26.4.a.m: 'For whomever he might desire that he be without cattle, [he should make it] fatless for him'—thus it is stated.

7.26.5.a.m: Invited, six including the Maitrāvaruṇa partake of it;

7.26.6.a.m: He prepares the entrails as a sixfold cut portion for the agnīdh.

7.26.7.a.m: He carries the udder with its surrounding flesh to the hotṛ.

7.26.8.a.s: agnīd aupayajān aṅgārān āharopayaṣṭar upasīda brahman prasthāsyāmaḥ samidham ādhāyāgnīt paridhīṃś cāgniṃ ca sakṛt-sakṛt saṃmṛḍḍhīti saṃpreṣyati
7.26.8.a.d: अग्नीद् औपयजान् अङ्गारान् आहरोपयष्टर् उपसीद ब्रह्मन् प्रस्थास्यामः समिधम् आधायाग्नीत् परिधींश् चाग्निं च सकृत्-सकृत् संमृड्ढीति संप्रेष्यति
7.26.8.a.m: He issues the call: 'Agnīdh, bring the embers for the subordinate offerings; subordinate sacrificer, sit down nearby; Brahman, we shall proceed; having laid on firewood, Agnīdh, wipe once each around the enclosing sticks and the fire.'

7.26.9.a.m: He brings the embers for the subordinate offerings from the āgnīdhra fire.

7.26.10.a.m: In the independent animal sacrifice, [he brings them] from the śāmitra fire to the northern hip of the altar ground.

7.26.11.a.s: gudakāṇḍam ekādaśadhā tiryak chittvāsaṃbhindann aparyāvartayann anūyājānāṃ vaṣaṭkṛte-vaṣaṭkṛta ekaikaṃ gudakāṇḍaṃ pratiprasthātā hastena juhoti samudraṃ gaccha svāhety etaiḥ pratimantram
7.26.11.a.d: गुदकाण्डम् एकादशधा तिर्यक् छित्त्वासंभिन्दन्न् अपर्यावर्तयन्न् अनूयाजानां वषट्कृते-वषट्कृत एकैकं गुदकाण्डं प्रतिप्रस्थाता हस्तेन जुहोति समुद्रं गच्छ स्वाहेत्य् एतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
7.26.11.a.m: Having cut the rectum into eleven pieces transversely, without splitting them and without turning them over, at each vaṣaṭ-call of the after-offerings the pratiprasthātṛ offers by hand one piece of the rectum each time, with each respective formula: 'Go to the ocean, svāhā!'

7.26.12.a.s: sarvāṇi hutvādbhyas tvauṣadhībhya iti barhiṣi lepaṃ nimṛjya mano me hārdi yaccheti japati /
7.26.12.a.d: सर्वाणि हुत्वाद्भ्यस् त्वौषधीभ्य इति बर्हिषि लेपं निमृज्य मनो मे हार्दि यच्छेति जपति ।
7.26.12.a.m: Having offered them all, having wiped off the ointment on the barhis with 'To the waters, to the plants!', he mutters: 'Restrain my mind in my heart!'

7.26.12.b.s: pṛṣadājyaṃ juhvām ānīya pṛṣadājyadhānīm upabhṛtaṃ kṛtvā tenaikādaśānūyājān yajati
7.26.12.b.d: पृषदाज्यं जुह्वाम् आनीय पृषदाज्यधानीम् उपभृतं कृत्वा तेनैकादशानूयाजान् यजति
7.26.12.b.m: Having poured the speckled butter into the juhū ladle and made the upabhṛt ladle the container for the speckled butter, he performs the eleven after-offerings with it.

7.26.13.a.m: He issues the call for the first: 'Urge for the gods!'

7.26.14.a.m: The sacrificer accompanies them with the standard formulas:

7.27.1.a.m: with the first formula, the first four and the tenth;

7.27.1.b.m: with the second, up to the lord of the forest (the tree);

7.27.2.a.s: uttarayor vikāreṣūbhau hotāraṃ codayato 'dhvaryur maitrāvaruṇaś ca yajeti
7.27.2.a.d: उत्तरयोर् विकारेषूभौ होतारं चोदयतो ऽध्वर्युर् मैत्रावरुणश् च यजेति
7.27.2.a.m: In the modifications of the latter two, both the adhvaryu and the maitrāvaruṇa prompt the hotṛ, saying: 'Recite the consecratory verse!'

7.27.3.a.m: At this point some authorities teach the anointing of the chip of the sacrificial post.

7.27.4.a.s: pratyākramya juhvāṃ svarum avadhāyānūyājānte juhoti dyām te dhūmo gacchatv antarikṣam arciḥ pṛthivīṃ bhasmanā pṛṇasva svāheti
7.27.4.a.d: प्रत्याक्रम्य जुह्वां स्वरुम् अवधायानूयाजान्ते जुहोति द्याम् ते धूमो गच्छत्व् अन्तरिक्षम् अर्चिः पृथिवीं भस्मना पृणस्व स्वाहेति
7.27.4.a.m: Stepping back and placing the chip of the post into the juhū ladle, he offers it at the end of the after-offerings with: 'Let your smoke go to the sky, your light to the atmosphere; fill the earth with ash, svāhā!'

7.27.5.a.m: The procedure is the same up to the responding call.

7.27.6.a.m: The call for the sūktavāka is modified.

7.27.7.a.s: taṃ maitrāvaruṇo brūyād agnim adya hotāram avṛṇīteti
7.27.7.a.d: तं मैत्रावरुणो ब्रूयाद् अग्निम् अद्य होतारम् अवृणीतेति
7.27.7.a.m: The maitrāvaruṇa should say it: 'Agni has today chosen the hotṛ...'

7.27.8.a.m: Excluding the dhruvā ladle, he pours libations over the enclosing sticks with four [formulas].

7.27.9.a.s: dakṣiṇena vihāraṃ jāghanīṃ hṛtvā tayā patnīḥ saṃyājayanti
7.27.9.a.d: दक्षिणेन विहारं जाघनीं हृत्वा तया पत्नीः संयाजयन्ति
7.27.9.a.m: Having carried the tail south of the sacred grounds, they perform the patnīsaṃyājas with it.

7.27.10.a.s: ājyena somatvaṣṭārāv iṣṭvottānāyai jāghanyai devānāṃ patnībhyo 'vadyati /
7.27.10.a.d: आज्येन सोमत्वष्टाराव् इष्ट्वोत्तानायै जाघन्यै देवानां पत्नीभ्यो ऽवद्यति ।
7.27.10.a.m: Having sacrificed to Soma and Tvaṣṭṛ with clarified butter, he cuts off a portion for the wives of the gods from the upper part of the tail;

7.27.10.b.m: from the lower part, for Agni the master of the house.

7.27.11.a.s: uttānāyai hotra iḍām avadyati nīcyā agnīdhe
7.27.11.a.d: उत्तानायै होत्र इडाम् अवद्यति नीच्या अग्नीधे
7.27.11.a.m: From the upper part he cuts off the iḍā for the hotṛ; from the lower part, for the agnīdh.

7.27.12.a.s: tāṃ patnyai prayacchati tāṃ sādhvaryave 'nyasmai vā brāhmaṇāya
7.27.12.a.d: तां पत्न्यै प्रयच्छति तां साध्वर्यवे ऽन्यस्मै वा ब्राह्मणाय
7.27.12.a.m: He hands it to the wife; she gives it to the adhvaryu or to another brāhmaṇa.

7.27.14.a.s: taṃ sa brāhmaṇāya yady abrāhmaṇo bhavati
7.27.14.a.d: तं स ब्राह्मणाय यद्य् अब्राह्मणो भवति
7.27.14.a.m: He [gives] it to a brāhmaṇa, if he is not a brāhmaṇa.

7.27.15.a.s: yajña yajñaṃ gaccheti trīṇi samiṣṭayajūṃṣi hutvānupaspṛśan hṛdayaśūlam udaṅ paretyāsaṃcare 'pa upaninīya śuṣkārdrayoḥ saṃdhāv udvāsayati śug asīti dveṣyaṃ manasā dhyāyan
7.27.15.a.d: यज्ञ यज्ञं गच्छेति त्रीणि समिष्टयजूंषि हुत्वानुपस्पृशन् हृदयशूलम् उदङ् परेत्यासंचरे ऽप उपनिनीय शुष्कार्द्रयोः संधाव् उद्वासयति शुग् असीति द्वेष्यं मनसा ध्यायन्
7.27.15.a.m: Having offered the three samiṣṭayajus formulas with 'O sacrifice, go to the sacrifice!', without touching it, going north with the heart-spit into an unfrequented spot and pouring water, he deposits it at the junction of the dry and the wet, contemplating in mind his enemy with: 'You are grief!'

7.27.16.a.s: sumitrā na āpa oṣadhaya iti tasmiṃś cātvāle vā sahapatnīkā mārjayitvā dhāmno-dhāmno rājann ud uttamam ity ādityam upasthāyaidho 'sy edhiṣīmahīty āhavanīye samidha ādhāyāpo anvacāriṣam ity upatiṣṭhante
7.27.16.a.d: सुमित्रा न आप ओषधय इति तस्मिंश् चात्वाले वा सहपत्नीका मार्जयित्वा धाम्नो-धाम्नो राजन्न् उद् उत्तमम् इत्य् आदित्यम् उपस्थायैधो ऽस्य् एधिषीमहीत्य् आहवनीये समिध आधायापो अन्वचारिषम् इत्य् उपतिष्ठन्ते
7.27.16.a.m: Having purified themselves with the wife at that [spot] or at the pit with 'May the waters and plants be friendly to us!', having paid reverence to the Sun with 'From abode to abode, O King...' and 'From the highest...', having placed firewood on the āhavanīya with 'You are kindling; may we kindle!', they attend upon it with 'I have followed the waters'.

7.28.1.a.d: इष्टिविधो वा अन्यः पशुबन्धः सोमविधो ऽन्यः ।
7.28.1.a.m: One kind of animal sacrifice follows the pattern of the primary sacrifice, another follows the pattern of the soma sacrifice.

7.28.1.b.s: sa yatraitadapaḥ praṇayati pūrṇapātraṃ ninayati viṣṇukramānkrāmati sa iṣṭividho 'to 'nyaḥ somavidha iti vājasaneyakam
7.28.1.b.d: स यत्रैतदपः प्रणयति पूर्णपात्रं निनयति विष्णुक्रमान्क्रामति स इष्टिविधो ऽतो ऽन्यः सोमविध इति वाजसनेयकम्
7.28.1.b.m: Where he conducts the waters, pours out the full cup, and strides the steps of Viṣṇu, that follows the pattern of the primary sacrifice; otherwise, it follows the pattern of the soma sacrifice: thus says the Vājasaneyaka.

7.28.2.a.s: yūpaṃ yajamāna upatiṣṭhate namaḥ svarubhyaḥ sannān māvagātāpaścāddaghvānnam bhūyāsam //
7.28.2.a.d: यूपं यजमान उपतिष्ठते नमः स्वरुभ्यः सन्नान् मावगातापश्चाद्दघ्वान्नम् भूयासम् ॥
7.28.2.a.m: The sacrificer pays reverence to the sacrificial post: 'Homage to the chips of the post! Having settled, do not fall down from me; may I be one whose food does not fail!'

7.28.2.b.s: śṛṅgāṇīvec chṛṅgiṇāṃ saṃdadṛśrire caṣālavantaḥ svaravaḥ pṛthivyām /
7.28.2.b.d: शृङ्गाणीवेच् छृङ्गिणां संददृश्रिरे चषालवन्तः स्वरवः पृथिव्याम् ।
7.28.2.b.m: 'Like horns of horned beasts the chips of the post with their top-rings have appeared on earth; /'

7.28.2.c.s: te devāsaḥ svaravas tasthivāṃso namaḥ sakhibhyaḥ sannān māvagāta //
7.28.2.c.d: ते देवासः स्वरवस् तस्थिवांसो नमः सखिभ्यः सन्नान् मावगात ॥
7.28.2.c.m: 'those divine chips of the post standing firm, homage to the friends! Having settled, do not fall down from me!'

7.28.2.d.m: And with: 'Hoping for good heroic sons...'

7.28.3.a.s: upasthāya yajña śaṃ ca ma iti japati
7.28.3.a.d: उपस्थाय यज्ञ शं च म इति जपति
7.28.3.a.m: Having paid reverence, he mutters: 'O sacrifice, peace and happiness for me!'

7.28.4.a.s: āhutyai vā etaṃ vanaspatibhyaḥ pracyāvayanty upayajya manuṣyāḥ prayānti /
7.28.4.a.d: आहुत्यै वा एतं वनस्पतिभ्यः प्रच्यावयन्त्य् उपयज्य मनुष्याः प्रयान्ति ।
7.28.4.a.m: Verily, they tear this [post] away from the forest trees for an oblation; having offered subordinates, the men depart.

7.28.4.b.m: The sacrificial post indeed takes upon itself whatever was ill-offered in the sacrifice.

7.28.4.c.s: yad yūpam upaspṛśed duriṣṭaṃ yajñasyāmuñcet tam abhimantrayeta vāyav eṣa te vāyav ity ekam /
7.28.4.c.d: यद् यूपम् उपस्पृशेद् दुरिष्टं यज्ञस्यामुञ्चेत् तम् अभिमन्त्रयेत वायव् एष ते वायव् इत्य् एकम् ।
7.28.4.c.m: If one should touch the post, one would take upon oneself whatever was ill-offered in the sacrifice; he should address it, if one post, with: 'O Vāyu, this is yours, O Vāyu!'

7.28.4.d.s: vāyav etau te vāyav iti dvau /
7.28.4.d.d: वायव् एतौ ते वायव् इति द्वौ ।
7.28.4.d.m: If two, with: 'O Vāyu, these two are yours, O Vāyu!'

7.28.4.e.s: vāyav ete te vāyav iti bahūn
7.28.4.e.d: वायव् एते ते वायव् इति बहून्
7.28.4.e.m: If many, with: 'O Vāyu, these are yours, O Vāyu!'

7.28.5.a.m: The independent animal sacrifice is dedicated to Indra-and-Agni, to Sūrya, or to Prajāpati.

7.28.6.a.m: He should sacrifice with it every year.

7.28.7.a.m: At the change of season, when fresh pasture appears, or at each solstice.

7.28.8.a.d: मांसीयन्ति ह वा अग्नयो ऽजुह्वतो यजमानस्य ।
7.28.8.a.m: Indeed, the fires crave meat from the non-sacrificing sacrificer.

7.28.8.b.m: They think only of the sacrificer.

7.28.8.d.m: In other fires people cook ordinary meat,

7.28.8.e.m: but for these [fires] there is no other expectation of meat.

7.28.8.f.s: yasyo caite bhavanti taṃ tato nānījānaṃ paśunā saṃvatsaro 'tīyāt /
7.28.8.f.d: यस्यो चैते भवन्ति तं ततो नानीजानं पशुना संवत्सरो ऽतीयात् ।
7.28.8.f.m: And for whomsoever these [fires] exist, a year must not pass without him sacrificing with an animal oblation.

7.28.8.g.s: āyuṣyo ha vā asyaiṣa ātmaniṣkrayaṇa iti vājasaneyakaṃ bhavati bhavati
7.28.8.g.d: आयुष्यो ह वा अस्यैष आत्मनिष्क्रयण इति वाजसनेयकं भवति भवति
7.28.8.g.m: 'This indeed brings long life for him, being a ransom for himself,' says the Vājasaneyaka. It is so.

8.1.1.a.s: akṣayyaṃ ha vai cāturmāsyayājinaḥ sukṛtaṃ bhavati
8.1.1.a.d: अक्षय्यं ह वै चातुर्मास्ययाजिनः सुकृतं भवति
8.1.1.a.m: Imperishable indeed is the merit of one who performs the four-month sacrifices (Cāturmāsyas).

8.1.2.a.s: phālugunyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ caitryāṃ vā vaiśvadevena yajate
8.1.2.a.d: फालुगुन्यां पौर्णमास्यां चैत्र्यां वा वैश्वदेवेन यजते
8.1.2.a.m: On the full moon of Phālguna or of Caitra, he sacrifices with the Vaiśvadeva.

8.1.3.a.s: pūrvasmin parvaṇi pañcahotāraṃ manasānudrutyāhavanīye sagrahaṃ hutvānvārambhaṇīyāmiṣṭiṃ nirvapati vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ pārjanyaṃ ca carum
8.1.3.a.d: पूर्वस्मिन् पर्वणि पञ्चहोतारं मनसानुद्रुत्याहवनीये सग्रहं हुत्वान्वारम्भणीयामिष्टिं निर्वपति वैश्वानरं द्वादशकपालं पार्जन्यं च चरुम्
8.1.3.a.m: On the preceding juncture, having recited the pañcahotṛ formula mentally and offered it with the graha libation into the āhavanīya, he presents the introductory sacrifice: a cake on twelve potsherds for Vaiśvānara and a pap for Parjanya.

8.1.4.a.s: vaiśvānaro na ūtyā pṛṣṭo divīti vaiśvānarasya yājyānuvākye //
8.1.4.a.d: वैश्वानरो न ऊत्या पृष्टो दिवीति वैश्वानरस्य याज्यानुवाक्ये ॥
8.1.4.a.m: "Vaiśvānara [hastens] to our aid" and "Established in heaven" are the invitatory and consecratory verses of the offering to Vaiśvānara.

8.1.4.b.m: "Sing forth to Parjanya, the son of heaven, the bounteous;

8.1.4.d.s: acchā vada tavasaṃ gīrbhirābhiḥ stuhi parjanyaṃ namasāvivāsa /
8.1.4.d.d: अच्छा वद तवसं गीर्भिराभिः स्तुहि पर्जन्यं नमसाविवास ।
8.1.4.d.m: "Address the mighty one with these songs, praise Parjanya, invite him with reverence:

8.1.4.e.s: kanikradadvṛṣabho jīradānū reto dadhātvoṣadhīṣu garbhamiti pārjanyasya //
8.1.4.e.d: कनिक्रदद्वृषभो जीरदानू रेतो दधात्वोषधीषु गर्भमिति पार्जन्यस्य ॥
8.1.4.e.m: Bellowing, the bull of quick gifts deposits the seed in the plants as an embryo" [are the verses] for the offering to Parjanya.

8.1.4.f.m: He gives gold at the offering to Vaiśvānara, a milch-cow at the offering to Parjanya.

8.1.4.g.m: The iṣṭi concludes in the established manner.

8.1.5.a.m: He performs the Vaiśvadeva on ground sloping to the east.

8.1.6.a.m: As in the animal sacrifice, bringing forward the fire from the gārhapatya, he does not offer the udyata-oblation.

8.1.7.a.s: ūrṇāvantaṃ prathamaḥ sīda yonimiti hoturabhijñāyāhavanīyāyatana ūrṇāstukāṃ nidhāya tasyām agniṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
8.1.7.a.d: ऊर्णावन्तं प्रथमः सीद योनिमिति होतुरभिज्ञायाहवनीयायतन ऊर्णास्तुकां निधाय तस्याम् अग्निं प्रतिष्ठापयति
8.1.7.a.m: Upon recognizing the hotṛ's [verse], "Sit down, first one, in the woolly womb," having placed a tuft of wool in the āhavanīya hearth, he establishes the fire upon it.

8.1.8.a.m: Another [view is]: 'The bringing forward of the fire as in the animal sacrifice does not occur where there is no high altar (uttaravedi).'

8.1.9.a.m: Having added fuel to the fires and brought a branch, he drives away the calves for the curd (āmikṣā) sacred to the Viśve Devas.

8.1.10.a.m: The sacrificial grass and the grass bunch are made of budding shoots.

8.1.11.a.m: [The sacrificial grass is] tied in three bundles, and then into one single [bundle].

8.1.15.a.m: Having tied three bundles, he ties them together again into one.

8.1.16.a.m: As before, he has the evening milking milked for the curd sacred to the Viśve Devas.

8.2.1.a.s: śvobhute pātrasaṃsādanakāle pālāśaṃ vājinapātraṃ prayunakti srucaṃ vā
8.2.1.a.d: श्वोभुते पात्रसंसादनकाले पालाशं वाजिनपात्रं प्रयुनक्ति स्रुचं वा
8.2.1.a.m: On the next day, at the time of setting out the utensils, he prepares the whey-vessel made of palāśa wood, or a ladling spoon.

8.2.2.a.m: At the time of apportioning [the oblations], he apportions the eight oblations as handed down in the sacred text: "The [cake] on eight potsherds for Agni..."

8.2.3.a.m: Among these, the five [oblations] ending with the one to Pūṣan are common [to the seasonal sacrifices].

8.2.4.a.m: He cooks the oblation for Pūṣan out of flour.

8.2.5.a.m: Into the hot morning milk he pours the evening milk.

8.2.6.a.m: That which coagulates is the curd (āmikṣā);

8.2.8.b.s: mahīnāṃ payo 'sīti pṛṣadājyadhānyāṃ dvirājyaṃ gṛhṇāti dvirdadhi sakṛdājyam
8.2.8.b.d: महीनां पयो ऽसीति पृषदाज्यधान्यां द्विराज्यं गृह्णाति द्विर्दधि सकृदाज्यम्
8.2.8.b.m: With the formula, "You are the milk of the great ones," he scoops clarified butter twice into the speckled butter vessel, curd twice, and clarified butter once.

8.2.9.a.s: udvāsanakāla āmikṣāṃ saṃhatya dvayoḥ pātrayoruddhṛtya vājinaikadeśenopasiñcati
8.2.9.a.d: उद्वासनकाल आमिक्षां संहत्य द्वयोः पात्रयोरुद्धृत्य वाजिनैकदेशेनोपसिञ्चति
8.2.9.a.m: At the time of taking off [the oblations], having compacted the curd and scooped it out into two vessels, he sprinkles it with a portion of the whey.

8.2.10.a.m: At the time of garnishing, he fills up the single-potsherd cake with clarified butter or makes its surface visible, and sets down the oblations with the vyāhṛtis.

8.2.12.a.m: With the pañcahotṛ formula, the sacrificer touches all the oblations that have been set down.

8.2.13.a.m: The fire-churning and the kindling verses are as in the animal sacrifice.

8.2.15.a.m: Between the fourth and the last are the four animal [fore-offerings] beginning with the doors, whose consecratory verses are the opening words of the ritual calls.

8.2.17.a.s: pracaraṇakāla upāṃśu sāvitreṇa pracarya pūrvavadekakapālena pracarati
8.2.17.a.d: प्रचरणकाल उपांशु सावित्रेण प्रचर्य पूर्ववदेककपालेन प्रचरति
8.2.17.a.m: At the time of performance, having performed [the offering] to Savitṛ in a low voice, he performs [the offering] with the single-potsherd cake as before.

8.2.18.a.m: He offers an oblation over the single-potsherd cake with the names of the four months, "Madhu and Mādhava..."

8.2.19.a.s: dakṣiṇākāle prathamajaṃ vatsaṃ dadāti mithunau vā gāvau
8.2.19.a.d: दक्षिणाकाले प्रथमजं वत्सं ददाति मिथुनौ वा गावौ
8.2.19.a.m: At the time of the sacrificial gift, he gives a first-born calf or a pair of cattle.

8.2.20.a.s: pṛṣadājyaṃ juhvāmānīya pṛṣadājyadhānīmupabhṛtaṃ kṛtvā tena navānūyājānyajati
8.2.20.a.d: पृषदाज्यं जुह्वामानीय पृषदाज्यधानीमुपभृतं कृत्वा तेन नवानूयाजान्यजति
8.2.20.a.m: Having poured speckled butter into the juhū and used the speckled butter vessel as the upabhṛt, he offers the nine after-offerings with it.

8.3.1.a.m: The first eight are those of the animal sacrifice, omitting the ritual calls.

8.3.3.a.m: He gives the ritual call for the first: "Offer to the gods";

8.3.4.b.m: he hopes for the heavenly abode"—in the blessings of the sūktavāka the hotṛ follows [these words].

8.3.6.a.s: paridhīnprahṛtya saṃsrāvāntaṃ kṛtvā vājinapātra upastīryāntarvedi barhiranuviṣiñcanvājinaṃ gṛhṇāti
8.3.6.a.d: परिधीन्प्रहृत्य संस्रावान्तं कृत्वा वाजिनपात्र उपस्तीर्यान्तर्वेदि बर्हिरनुविषिञ्चन्वाजिनं गृह्णाति
8.3.6.a.m: Having cast the enclosing sticks [into the fire] and concluded with the scrapings, having spread an under-layer [of butter] in the whey-vessel, he takes the whey, continuously sprinkling the sacrificial grass inside the altar ground.

8.3.8.a.m: "Recite for the Vājins," "Offer to the Vājins," are the two ritual calls;

8.3.8.b.m: at the vaṣaṭ-call he offers with the goblet,

8.3.8.c.m: or with the ladling spoon that is being continuously sprinkled, and also at the secondary vaṣaṭ-call.

8.3.9.a.m: Kneeling with knees raised, the hotṛ offers without drawing breath.

8.3.10.a.m: He offers the after-oblation with: "O Agni, enjoy the whey."

8.3.11.a.s: trayāṇāṃ ha vai haviṣāṃ sviṣṭakṛtena samavadyati somasya vājinasya gharmasyeti
8.3.11.a.d: त्रयाणां ह वै हविषां स्विष्टकृतेन समवद्यति सोमस्य वाजिनस्य घर्मस्येति
8.3.11.a.m: Indeed, of three oblations he cuts portions together for the Sviṣṭakṛt: of soma, of whey, and of the gharma.

8.3.12.a.s: udrekeṇa paśubandhavaddiśaḥ pratījyāntarvedi śeṣaṃ sarve samupahūya bhakṣayanti
8.3.12.a.d: उद्रेकेण पशुबन्धवद्दिशः प्रतीज्यान्तर्वेदि शेषं सर्वे समुपहूय भक्षयन्ति
8.3.12.a.m: Having offered to the quarters with the residue as in the animal sacrifice, all, having invited one another inside the altar ground, partake of the remainder.

8.3.13.a.m: He addresses him by his ritual title: 'So-and-so, do invite [me]!'

8.3.15.a.m: The hotṛ partakes first, the sacrificer last.

8.3.15.b.m: The sacrificer is both first and last, say some.

8.3.16.a.s: vājināṃ bhakṣo avatu vājo asmām̐ retaḥ siktamamṛtaṃ balāya /
8.3.16.a.d: वाजिनां भक्षो अवतु वाजो अस्माम्̐ रेतः सिक्तममृतं बलाय ।
8.3.16.a.m: "May the partaking of the whey protect [us], may vigor [protect] us, the seed that is poured out, immortal, for strength.

8.3.16.b.s: sa na indriyaṃ draviṇaṃ dadhātu mā riṣāma vājinaṃ bhakṣayantaḥ /
8.3.16.b.d: स न इन्द्रियं द्रविणं दधातु मा रिषाम वाजिनं भक्षयन्तः ।
8.3.16.b.m: May it bestow on us power and wealth; may we not come to harm while partaking of the whey.

8.3.16.c.s: tasya te vājibhirbhakṣaṃkṛtasya vājibhiḥ sutasya vājipītasya vājinasyopahūtasyopahūto bhakṣayāmīti bhakṣayati
8.3.16.c.d: तस्य ते वाजिभिर्भक्षंकृतस्य वाजिभिः सुतस्य वाजिपीतस्य वाजिनस्योपहूतस्योपहूतो भक्षयामीति भक्षयति
8.3.16.c.m: From that [portion] of yours, prepared as food by the spirited, pressed by the spirited, drunk by the spirited, invited from the invited whey, I partake"—with this he partakes.

8.3.17.a.m: The samiṣṭayajus formulas are as in the animal sacrifice.

8.3.18.a.m: The offering is concluded in the established manner.

8.4.1.a.s: śvobhūte paurṇamāsyeṣṭvā prasūtā devena savitrā daivyā āpa undantu te tanuṃ dīrghāyutvāya varcasa ityupodya tryeṇyā śalalyekṣukāṇḍenekṣuśalākayā vā lauhena ca kṣureṇaudumbareṇa ni keśānvartayate vāpayate śmaśrūṇi
8.4.1.a.d: श्वोभूते पौर्णमास्येष्ट्वा प्रसूता देवेन सवित्रा दैव्या आप उन्दन्तु ते तनुं दीर्घायुत्वाय वर्चस इत्युपोद्य त्र्येण्या शलल्येक्षुकाण्डेनेक्षुशलाकया वा लौहेन च क्षुरेणौदुम्बरेण नि केशान्वर्तयते वापयते श्मश्रूणि
8.4.1.a.m: On the following day, having performed the Full Moon sacrifice, with the words: "Impelled by the god Savitṛ, may the divine waters moisten your body for long life and splendor," having moistened [his hair], he trims his hair and has his beard shaved with a porcupine quill having three white rings, a piece of reed or a reed splint, an iron razor, and [an implement] made of udumbara wood.

8.4.2.a.m: "Truth alone is the Highest, nothing goes beyond truth.

8.4.2.b.s: ṛte samudra āhita ṛte bhumiriyaṃ śritā //
8.4.2.b.d: ऋते समुद्र आहित ऋते भुमिरियं श्रिता ॥
8.4.2.b.m: In truth the ocean is placed; on truth this earth rests.

8.4.2.c.m: Agni, with his sharp flame, has overcome the heat [with his] neck;

8.4.2.d.m: the head is placed in heat by the splendor of Vaiśvānara.

8.4.2.e.m: With truth I turn it around; with reality I turn it around;

8.4.2.f.m: with austerity I turn it along; with what is auspicious I turn it toward; with what is pleasant I turn it toward"—with this formula he turns it around.

8.4.3.a.s: tadṛtaṃ tatsatyaṃ tadvrataṃ tacchakeyaṃ tena śakeyaṃ tena rādhyāsamiti yajamāno japati /
8.4.3.a.d: तदृतं तत्सत्यं तद्व्रतं तच्छकेयं तेन शकेयं तेन राध्यासमिति यजमानो जपति ।
8.4.3.a.m: "That is truth, that is reality, that is the vow; may I be capable of it, may I be capable through it, may I succeed through it"—thus the sacrificer mutters.

8.4.3.b.m: And he mutters the anuvāka [beginning with]: "The brāhmaṇa is the single hotṛ..."

8.4.4.a.m: His intermediate vows [continue] during the seasonal junctures.

8.4.5.a.m: He does not eat meat; he does not approach a woman;

8.4.11.a.m: Eating honey should be [his food], is one view.

8.4.11.b.m: It is for flavoring, is another view.

8.4.12.a.m: One who sacrifices at the seasons is indeed one [kind of sacrificer], and one who sacrifices with the Cāturmāsya sacrifices is another.

8.4.13.a.d: यो वसन्तो ऽभूत्प्रावृडभूच्छरदभूदिति यजते स ऋतुयाजी ।
8.4.13.a.m: He who sacrifices thinking, "Spring has come," "The rainy season has come," "Autumn has come," is one who sacrifices at the seasons.

8.4.13.b.m: Now he who [sacrifices] every four [months] is one who sacrifices with the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.

8.4.13.c.m: In spring he sacrifices with the Vaiśvadeva; in the rainy season with the Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifices;

8.4.13.d.m: in autumn with the Sākamedha sacrifices—thus it is known [from the scriptures].

8.5.1.a.m: Then, after four months, on the full moon day of Āṣāḍha or of Śravaṇā, having set out, he sacrifices with the Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifices.

8.5.2.a.m: "One should sacrifice when the brush has grown up"—so states a Brāhmaṇa of the Rigvedins.

8.5.3.a.m: Its procedure is like that of the Vaiśvadeva.

8.5.4.a.s: vedau kṛtvāgreṇa gārhapatyaṃ same prācī vedī bhavataḥ
8.5.4.a.d: वेदौ कृत्वाग्रेण गार्हपत्यं समे प्राची वेदी भवतः
8.5.4.a.m: Having made two altar grounds in front of the gārhapatya, they are equal and facing east.

8.5.5.a.m: The adhvaryu makes the northern one; the pratiprasthātṛ makes the southern one.

8.5.5.b.m: The adhvaryu operates in the northern sacrificial enclosure; the pratiprasthātṛ in the southern.

8.5.6.a.m: In both places the entire procedure is performed.

8.5.9.a.m: The brahman gives assent in the dual.

8.5.10.a.s: dvyaṅgulaṃ tryaṅgulaṃ caturaṅgulaṃ pṛthamātraṃ rathavartmamātraṃ sītāmātraṃ prādeśamātreṇa vā tiryagasaṃbhinne vedī bhavataḥ
8.5.10.a.d: द्व्यङ्गुलं त्र्यङ्गुलं चतुरङ्गुलं पृथमात्रं रथवर्त्ममात्रं सीतामात्रं प्रादेशमात्रेण वा तिर्यगसंभिन्ने वेदी भवतः
8.5.10.a.m: The two altar grounds are separated crosswise by two finger-breadths, three finger-breadths, four finger-breadths, the width of a palm, the width of a chariot rut, the width of a furrow, or by the measure of a span.

8.5.11.a.m: Between the two altar grounds is the movement path for the pratiprasthātṛ.

8.5.12.a.m: Carrying the stambayajus to the west of the northern altar ground, he does not pass around the adhvaryu.

8.5.16.a.m: Whatever the adhvaryu does, that the pratiprasthātṛ also does.

8.5.17.a.m: Whatever is to be done by speech, only the adhvaryu should do that,

8.5.18.a.m: or the recitations whose timing is simultaneous,

8.5.19.a.m: and the consecrations of common substances.

8.5.20.a.m: Having made [the trenches] before the northern enclosing line, he connects the two altar grounds by the single stroke of the wooden sword:

8.5.20.b.m: stepping forward from the northern hip of the southern [altar ground] to the southern shoulder of the northern [altar ground].

8.5.21.a.m: On the northern altar ground he strews the high altar as in the animal sacrifice.

8.5.22.a.m: At the proper time, they both carry forward the two fires from the gārhapatya, as in the animal sacrifice.

8.5.24.a.m: Between the two altar grounds the pratiprasthātṛ steps forward;

8.5.24.b.m: to the north of the northern altar ground, the adhvaryu.

8.5.25.a.m: First the adhvaryu establishes the fire on the high altar;

8.5.25.b.m: last, the pratiprasthātṛ on the southern [altar ground].

8.5.26.a.m: Having added fuel to the fires, the two [adhvaryu and pratiprasthātṛ] bring two separate branches.

8.5.28.a.m: The pratiprasthātṛ drives away the calves of the herd for the Maruts;

8.5.29.a.m: The dipping spoons are made of śamī wood or of gold.

8.5.30.a.m: According to their deities, the two [adhvaryu and pratiprasthātṛ] milk the evening milkings.

8.5.31.a.m: Or the Varuṇapraghāsa rites may take place on a single day.

8.5.32.a.m: If so, the curd preparation would be made with ordinary curd.

8.5.33.a.m: Some state that the curd and milk offering is a modification of the morning milking.

8.5.34.a.m: At the time of apportioning, he measures out the nine subsequent oblations, beginning with 'To Agni on eight potsherds'.

8.5.36.a.s: api vā pauṣṇaḥ karambhapātrāṇi meṣāviti yavānāṃ vrīhīṇāmitarāṇi
8.5.36.a.d: अपि वा पौष्णः करम्भपात्राणि मेषाविति यवानां व्रीहीणामितराणि
8.5.36.a.m: Alternatively, the oblation to Pūṣan, the karambha pots, and the two rams are of barley, while the others are of rice.

8.5.37.a.m: At this time, the pratiprasthātṛ silently measures out the barley meant for the karambha pots.

8.5.38.a.m: The adhvaryu measures out with a yajus formula [the barley] meant for the ram;

8.5.38.b.m: the pratiprasthātṛ [measures out that] meant for the ewe.

8.5.39.a.m: The deity of these two corresponds to that of the curds.

8.5.40.a.m: The wife makes the karambha pots out of unbaked dough.

8.5.41.a.m: There are as many as there are members of the sacrificer's household, including the women, with one extra.

8.5.42.a.m: The two effigies of the rams are made of unbaked dough.

8.5.43.a.m: The adhvaryu makes the ram; the pratiprasthātṛ the ewe.

8.6.1.a.m: To the female he gives female characteristics;

8.6.3.a.s: api vā purvedyuranvāhāryapacane vituṣāniva yavānkṛtvā teṣāmīṣadupataptānāṃ patnī karambhapātrāṇi karoti
8.6.3.a.d: अपि वा पुर्वेद्युरन्वाहार्यपचने वितुषानिव यवान्कृत्वा तेषामीषदुपतप्तानां पत्नी करम्भपात्राणि करोति
8.6.3.a.m: Or, on the previous day, having made the barley as if dehusked on the anvāhāryapacana, the wife makes the karambha pots out of them after they are slightly roasted.

8.6.4.a.s: atrāpi meṣaṃ meṣīṃ ca karotīti vājasaneyakam
8.6.4.a.d: अत्रापि मेषं मेषीं च करोतीति वाजसनेयकम्
8.6.4.a.m: Here too, she makes the ram and the ewe; thus the Vājasaneyaka says.

8.6.5.a.m: Having placed [the oblations] up to that for Indra-Agni on the fire, he places the ewe on eleven potsherds;

8.6.6.a.m: Or the two are cooked in an earthen pot.

8.6.7.a.m: Having placed the oblation for Ka on one potsherd on the fire and poured out [water] for the Āpyas, they carry forward the fires; thus the Vājasaneyaka says.

8.6.9.b.d: महीनां पयो ऽसीति पृषदाज्यधान्यां सकृदाज्यं गृह्णाति ।
8.6.9.b.m: with the verse 'You are the milk of the great ones,' he takes butter once into the vessel for speckled butter;

8.6.10.a.m: Or indeed, he may take it after mixing it in a shallow cup.

8.6.11.a.m: At the time of taking down, the two make the two effigies of the rams hairy with non-sheep wool.

8.6.12.a.m: In the absence of that, having affixed kuśa fibres, he places the ram in the [curd portion] for the Maruts;

8.6.13.a.m: Then upon the two he scatters śamī leaves and karīra fruits, more than a hundred or more than a thousand.

8.6.14.a.m: And having scattered them also into the karambha pots, he sets down the eight oblations on the northern altar ground.

8.6.15.a.s: ekāṃ mārutīṃ pratiprasthātā dakṣiṇasyāṃ karambhapātrāṇi ca
8.6.15.a.d: एकां मारुतीं प्रतिप्रस्थाता दक्षिणस्यां करम्भपात्राणि च
8.6.15.a.m: The pratiprasthātṛ sets down the single [oblation] for the Maruts and the karambha pots on the southern [altar ground].

8.6.16.a.m: Here the two exchange the effigies of the two rams:

8.6.17.a.m: he places the ewe in that for the Maruts;

8.6.18.a.m: As in the animal sacrifice, there are the two churning-sticks, the firewood-kindling verses, and nine fore-offerings and after-offerings.

8.6.19.a.m: With the verse 'We summon the gluttonous ones,' the pratiprasthātṛ leads forward the wife and makes her recite this [mantra].
