8.6.20.a.s: tāṃ pṛcchati patni kati te jārā iti
8.6.20.a.d: तां पृच्छति पत्नि कति ते जारा इति
8.6.20.a.m: He asks her: 'Wife, how many paramours do you have?'

8.6.21.a.m: Whomever she declares, he designates [saying]: 'May Varuṇa seize them!'

8.6.22.a.s: yajjāraṃ santaṃ na prabrūyātpriyaṃ jñātiṃ rundhyāt /
8.6.22.a.d: यज्जारं सन्तं न प्रब्रूयात्प्रियं ज्ञातिं रुन्ध्यात् ।
8.6.22.a.m: If she does not declare one who is a paramour, she would harm a dear kinsman.

8.6.22.b.m: She should declare: 'So-and-so is my paramour.'

8.6.22.c.m: 'Having designated him alone, she causes Varuṇa's noose to seize him,' so it is known.

8.6.23.a.m: The northern fire is swept clean, the southern is unswept.

8.6.23.b.s: athāntarā vedī gatvā yajamānaḥ patnī cottareṇa vottarāṃ vedimaiṣīke śūrpe karambhapātrāṇyopya śīrṣannadhinidhāya purastātpratyañcau tiṣṭhantau dakṣiṇe 'gnau śūrpeṇa juhutaḥ
8.6.23.b.d: अथान्तरा वेदी गत्वा यजमानः पत्नी चोत्तरेण वोत्तरां वेदिमैषीके शूर्पे करम्भपात्राण्योप्य शीर्षन्नधिनिधाय पुरस्तात्प्रत्यञ्चौ तिष्ठन्तौ दक्षिणे ऽग्नौ शूर्पेण जुहुतः
8.6.23.b.m: Then, having gone between the two altar grounds or along the north of the northern altar ground, having poured the karambha pots into a winnowing basket made of reed and placed it upon their heads, standing in front facing west, the sacrificer and his wife offer with the winnowing basket into the southern fire.

8.6.24.a.s: mo ṣū ṇa indreti yajamānaḥ puro 'nuvākyāmanvāha /
8.6.24.a.d: मो षू ण इन्द्रेति यजमानः पुरो ऽनुवाक्यामन्वाह ।
8.6.24.a.m: With 'Do not, O Indra,' the sacrificer recites the invitatory verse;

8.6.24.b.m: with 'What in the village,' both recite the consecratory verse.

8.6.25.a.m: Turning away, they whisper: 'The work-doers have done the work.'

8.6.26.a.m: Alternatively, the adhvaryu or the pratiprasthātṛ may make the offering;

8.6.26.b.m: the other two should touch along.

8.6.27.a.m: At this point, he sweeps the southern fire clean.

8.6.28.a.m: Having proceeded with [the offerings] ending with the one to Indra-Agni, the adhvaryu pauses.

8.6.29.a.s: atha pratiprasthātā pūrveṇa sahāvadānena mārutyāḥ sarvāṃ meṣīm avadyati /
8.6.29.a.d: अथ प्रतिप्रस्थाता पूर्वेण सहावदानेन मारुत्याः सर्वां मेषीम् अवद्यति ।
8.6.29.a.m: Then the pratiprasthātṛ cuts off the whole ewe from the [curds] for the Maruts along with the first portion;

8.6.29.b.m: with the subsequent portion, the śamī leaves and karīra fruits.

8.6.31.a.s: athādhvaryuḥ pūrveṇa sahāvadānena vāruṇyāḥ sarvaṃ meṣamavadyati /
8.6.31.a.d: अथाध्वर्युः पूर्वेण सहावदानेन वारुण्याः सर्वं मेषमवद्यति ।
8.6.31.a.m: Then the adhvaryu cuts off the whole ram from the [curds] for Varuṇa along with the first portion;

8.6.31.b.m: with the subsequent portion, the śamī leaves and karīra fruits.

8.7.1.a.m: "Recite for Ka," [and] "Sacrifice to Ka," are the two ritual calls for the [cake] on one potsherd.

8.7.2.a.m: He offers over the [cake] on one potsherd with the names of the four months: "Nabhas and Nabhasya..."

8.7.3.a.m: Now some cut off separate iḍās.

8.7.3.c.m: Cutting off together from the seven oblations, the adhvaryu hands [it] to the pratiprasthātṛ.

8.7.3.d.m: Upon it, the pratiprasthātṛ places along [the portion] of the Mārutyā oblation.

8.7.5.a.m: A bull that is past its prime, as it were, is the sacrificial gift.

8.7.6.a.m: He may, however, give more than that if he wishes.

8.7.8.a.m: "He hopes for the wellbeing of the full year."

8.7.8.b.m: "He hopes for the divine abode": the hotṛ adds [this] in the blessings of the Sūktavāka.

8.7.9.a.m: Both proceed with the two portions of vājina.

8.7.10.a.s: śesau samavanīyottare vihāre pūrvavadbhaksayantyā mā viśantvindava ā galgā dhavanīnāṃ rasena me rasaṃ pṛṇa /
8.7.10.a.d: शेसौ समवनीयोत्तरे विहारे पूर्ववद्भक्सयन्त्या मा विशन्त्विन्दव आ गल्गा धवनीनां रसेन मे रसं पृण ।
8.7.10.a.m: Pouring together the two remainders in the northern vedi, they consume it as before, [with]: "May the drops enter me; rushing forth from the shaking vessels, fill my essence with essence."

8.7.10.b.m: [The rest,] "Of you who have been made a drink by the swift ones...", is the same.

8.7.11.a.m: Excluding the full-vessel gift, he concludes the sacrifice as before.

8.7.12.a.m: In place of the full-vessel gift, there is the purificatory bath of the Soma sacrifice.

8.7.14.a.m: With the scrapings of the oblation to Varuṇa and with the husks, they perform the purificatory bath.

8.7.15.a.m: The husks acquire the ritual status of the soma dregs.

8.7.16.a.m: Some teach [a cake] on one potsherd for Varuṇa.

8.7.17.a.m: He does not [recite] the "life-giving" verse, nor the formula for stepping forth, nor does he sing a sāman.

8.7.18.a.m: Going to any direction for the purificatory bath is handed down in the texts.

8.7.19.a.m: They should not go down towards the north, say some.

8.7.20.a.m: In whichever direction they go, facing that way they should perform the ritual, say some.

8.7.21.a.m: They should go down into standing [pools] of flowing [waters].

8.7.23.a.s: udakānte staraṇāntāṃ vediṃ kṛtvā tasyāṃ havīṃṣi sādayati
8.7.23.a.d: उदकान्ते स्तरणान्तां वेदिं कृत्वा तस्यां हवींषि सादयति
8.7.23.a.m: At the water's edge, having made an altar ground extending up to the strewing, he places the oblations upon it.

8.7.25.a.s: śataṃ te rājanbhiṣajaḥ sahasramityapo dṛṣṭvā japati
8.7.25.a.d: शतं ते राजन्भिषजः सहस्रमित्यपो दृष्ट्वा जपति
8.7.25.a.m: Having looked at the water, he mutters: "A hundred are your medicines, O King, a thousand..."

8.7.26.a.m: They step upon the edge of the water with: "Trodden down is the fetter of Varuṇa."

8.7.27.a.m: Having plunged into the water, standing, they perform the purificatory bath.

8.7.28.a.m: Having thrown in a blade of grass, he makes the continuous libation with the dipping-spoon.

8.7.29.a.m: Or, if there should be grass there beforehand, he should offer on it.

8.8.1.a.m: He summons: "Agnīdh, wipe the waters three times."

8.8.2.a.s: āpo vājajito vājaṃ vaḥ sariṣyantīrvājaṃ jeṣyantīrvājinīrvājajito vājajityāyai saṃmārjmyapo annādā annādyāyeti mantraṃ saṃnamati
8.8.2.a.d: आपो वाजजितो वाजं वः सरिष्यन्तीर्वाजं जेष्यन्तीर्वाजिनीर्वाजजितो वाजजित्यायै संमार्ज्म्यपो अन्नादा अन्नाद्यायेति मन्त्रं संनमति
8.8.2.a.m: He adapts the formula: "O waters, winning the prize, about to run for your prize, about to win the prize, rich in prizes, winning the prize, I wipe you for winning the prize, eating food, for the eating of food."

8.8.3.a.m: He makes the continuous libation with the offering ladle with: "The face of Agni has entered into the waters."

8.8.4.a.m: The sacrificer recites over it: "You are speech belonging to Agni."

8.8.6.a.m: Having offered the fore-offerings without the barhis, he offers the two butter portions containing [verses on] water.

8.8.7.b.m: "Soma told me that within the waters are all medicines, / and Agni who brings good fortune to all, and the waters containing all medicines"—these are the two containing [verses on] water.

8.8.7.c.m: [The two verses are] the ones containing [words for] water.

8.8.8.a.s: niṣkāsasyāvadāya varuṇamiṣṭvā kṛtsnaṃ niṣkāsamavadāyāgnīvaruṇau sviṣṭakṛdarthe yajati
8.8.8.a.d: निष्कासस्यावदाय वरुणमिष्ट्वा कृत्स्नं निष्कासमवदायाग्नीवरुणौ स्विष्टकृदर्थे यजति
8.8.8.a.m: Cutting off from the scraping, having sacrificed to Varuṇa, cutting off the entire scraping, he sacrifices to Agni and Varuṇa in place of the Sviṣṭakṛt.

8.8.10.a.m: Or, bringing the butter from the upabhṛt into the juhū, he offers the two after-offerings without the barhis.

8.8.11.a.m: "Sacrifice to the two gods," he summons for the first.

8.8.12.a.s: tuṣāṇāṃ sthālīṃ pūrayitvāpsūpamārayati samudre te hṛdayamapsvantariti
8.8.12.a.d: तुषाणां स्थालीं पूरयित्वाप्सूपमारयति समुद्रे ते हृदयमप्स्वन्तरिति
8.8.12.a.m: Having filled a pot with the husks, he lets it sink in the water with: "Your heart is in the ocean, inside the waters."

8.8.13.a.m: Or rather, there is no purificatory bath belonging to a Soma sacrifice.

8.8.13.b.m: Silently, he should scatter the husks and scrapings into the water.

8.8.14.a.m: The wife unfastens the loop of the yoke-halter with: "Here I unloosen..."

8.8.15.a.s: devīrāpa ityavabhṛthaṃ yajamāno 'bhimantrya sumitrā na āpa oṣadhaya ityapaḥ pragāhya saśiraskāvanupamakṣantau snātaḥ patnī yajamānaśca
8.8.15.a.d: देवीराप इत्यवभृथं यजमानो ऽभिमन्त्र्य सुमित्रा न आप ओषधय इत्यपः प्रगाह्य सशिरस्कावनुपमक्षन्तौ स्नातः पत्नी यजमानश्च
8.8.15.a.m: The sacrificer addresses the purificatory bath with: "O divine waters..."; having plunged into the water with: "Friendly to us be the waters and the herbs...", the wife and the sacrificer bathe, including their heads, without dipping themselves under.

8.8.17.a.s: kāmamete vāsasī yasmai kāmayeyātaṃ tasmai dadyātām /
8.8.17.a.d: काममेते वाससी यस्मै कामयेयातं तस्मै दद्याताम् ।
8.8.17.a.m: They may give these two garments to whomsoever they wish.

8.8.17.b.m: "For they are not the garments of the consecrated," says the Vājasaneyaka.

8.8.18.a.s: udvayaṃ tamasasparītyādityamupasthāya pratiyuto varuṇasya paśa ityudakāntaṃ pratyasitvā samidhaḥ kṛtvāpratīkṣāstūṣṇīmetyaidho 'syedhiṣīmahītyāhavanīye samidha ādhāyāpo anvacāriṣamityupatiṣṭhante
8.8.18.a.d: उद्वयं तमसस्परीत्यादित्यमुपस्थाय प्रतियुतो वरुणस्य पश इत्युदकान्तं प्रत्यसित्वा समिधः कृत्वाप्रतीक्षास्तूष्णीमेत्यैधो ऽस्येधिषीमहीत्याहवनीये समिध आधायापो अन्वचारिषमित्युपतिष्ठन्ते
8.8.18.a.m: Having paid reverence to the sun with: "Rising out of the darkness...", having thrown [a grass-blade] back into the water's edge with: "Averted is the fetter of Varuṇa", having made fuel-sticks, having returned silently without looking back, having placed the fuel-sticks on the āhavanīya with: "You are kindling; may we be kindled", they revere [the fire] with: "I have followed the waters..."

8.8.19.a.m: Here, having sacrificed with the Full Moon sacrifice, the moistening and other acts [of tonsure] are repeated as before.

8.8.21.b.m: “Since the caldron revolved around the ends of the earth and the sky,

8.8.21.c.m: Agni, ruling with might, Varuṇa with thoughts,

8.8.21.d.m: Indra with the Maruts as comrades.”

8.8.21.e.m: The part starting with “Agni with the sharp...” is identical.

8.8.22.a.s: api vā snātvoptvā keśaśmaśrūṇyaraṇyoragnīnsamāropyodavasāya nirmathya paurṇamāsena yajate
8.8.22.a.d: अपि वा स्नात्वोप्त्वा केशश्मश्रूण्यरण्योरग्नीन्समारोप्योदवसाय निर्मथ्य पौर्णमासेन यजते
8.8.22.a.m: Or, having bathed, shaved hair and beard, mounted the fires upon the two kindling sticks, moved away [from the place of sacrifice], and churned out [fire], he sacrifices with the Full Moon sacrifice.

8.8.23.a.s: yajño ha vā eṣa yadvaruṇaparaghāsā nahyavakalpate yaduttaravedyāmagnihotraṃ juhuyāditi vājasaneyakam
8.8.23.a.d: यज्ञो ह वा एष यद्वरुणपरघासा नह्यवकल्पते यदुत्तरवेद्यामग्निहोत्रं जुहुयादिति वाजसनेयकम्
8.8.23.a.m: “This is indeed a [soma] sacrifice, namely the Varuṇapraghāsa rites; for it is not fitting that one should offer the agnihotra on the high altar ground,” says a Vājasaneyaka passage.

8.9.1.a.m: Then, after four months, having begun on the first junction day, he sacrifices for two days with the Sākamedha rites.

8.9.2.a.d: अग्नये ऽनीकवते पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालं निर्वपति साकं सूर्येणोद्यता
8.9.2.a.m: He pours out [grains for] a sacrificial cake on eight potsherds for Agni Anīkavat, together with the rising sun.

8.9.3.a.m: Or they proceed along with the rays.

8.9.4.a.m: The sacrifice concludes in the established manner.

8.9.5.a.m: At midday, [he offers] a pap to the Maruts Sāṃtapanas.

8.9.6.a.m: He does not throw the barhis after [into the fire].

8.9.7.a.m: The sacrifice concludes in the established manner.

8.9.8.a.s: marudbhyo gṛhamedhibhyaḥ sarvāsāṃ dugdhe sāyaṃ carum
8.9.8.a.d: मरुद्भ्यो गृहमेधिभ्यः सर्वासां दुग्धे सायं चरुम्
8.9.8.a.m: In the evening, [he offers] a pap in the milk of all [the cows] to the Maruts Gṛhamedhins.

8.9.9.a.m: What was the barhis of the Sāṃtapana [rite] is that of the Gṛhamedhīya.

8.9.10.a.m: Or there is no firewood and barhis.

8.9.10.c.m: No fore-offerings are offered, nor after-offerings.

8.9.11.a.m: Having driven away the calves without a yajus, he causes the cows to be milked without a strainer.

8.9.12.a.s: sa vai khalu parṇaśākhayā vatsānapākṛtya pavitrayati saṃdohya yathaitadamāvāsyāyāṃ kriyate taṃ caruṃ śrapayatītyeke
8.9.12.a.d: स वै खलु पर्णशाखया वत्सानपाकृत्य पवित्रयति संदोह्य यथैतदमावास्यायां क्रियते तं चरुं श्रपयतीत्येके
8.9.12.a.m: “Indeed, having driven away the calves with a branch of the parṇa tree, he purifies [the milk] with a strainer, milks them together just as is done on the New Moon day, and cooks that pap,” say some.

8.9.13.a.s: agnīnanvādhāya vedaṃ kṛtvāgnīnparistīrya pāṇiprakṣālanādi karma pratipadyate /
8.9.13.a.d: अग्नीनन्वाधाय वेदं कृत्वाग्नीन्परिस्तीर्य पाणिप्रक्षालनादि कर्म प्रतिपद्यते ।
8.9.13.a.m: Having added fuel to the fires, made the veda, and strewn grass around the fires, he proceeds to the rite beginning with the washing of the hands.

8.9.13.b.m: He sets out the utensils according to purpose.

8.9.14.a.m: [He places] a cooking pot in place of the potsherds.

8.10.1.a.m: having poured out four handfuls, he adds much [grain] more.

8.10.2.a.m: At the time of placing the potsherds, he places the cooking pot with the first potsherd mantra.

8.10.2.b.m: He adapts the mantra to: “Firm are you...”

8.10.2.c.m: At the time of purifying the flour, he purifies the rice grains.

8.10.3.a.s: adhiśrayaṇakāle prātardohavatsarvā yajamānasya gā dohayitvā tasmiñchrapayati
8.10.3.a.d: अधिश्रयणकाले प्रातर्दोहवत्सर्वा यजमानस्य गा दोहयित्वा तस्मिञ्छ्रपयति
8.10.3.a.m: At the time of placing [the pot] on the fire, having had all the cows of the sacrificer milked as in the morning milking, he cooks [the pap] in that [milk].

8.10.4.a.m: At the time of the ritual call, he calls for whatever is other than the firewood and barhis.

8.10.4.b.m: At the time of ladling the clarified butter, he takes it in the dhruvā ladle alone.

8.10.5.a.s: prokṣaṇīrabhimantrya brahmāṇamāmantrya vediṃ prokṣya prokṣaṇīśeṣaṃ ninīya pavitre apisṛjyāntarvedi vidhṛtī nidhāya dhruvāṃ ca sādayati
8.10.5.a.d: प्रोक्षणीरभिमन्त्र्य ब्रह्माणमामन्त्र्य वेदिं प्रोक्ष्य प्रोक्षणीशेषं निनीय पवित्रे अपिसृज्यान्तर्वेदि विधृती निधाय ध्रुवां च सादयति
8.10.5.a.m: Having consecrated the sprinkling waters, called upon the brahman priest, sprinkled the altar ground, poured out the residue of the sprinkling waters, inserted the two strainers, and placed the two separating blades inside the altar ground, he also places the dhruvā ladle down.

8.10.6.a.m: He adapts the mantra to: “May these two sit down...”

8.10.7.a.s: udvāsanakāle śaraṃ nidhāya yāvanto yajamānasyāmātyāstāvata odanānuddharati
8.10.7.a.d: उद्वासनकाले शरं निधाय यावन्तो यजमानस्यामात्यास्तावत ओदनानुद्धरति
8.10.7.a.m: At the time of taking down [the cooked food], having laid down a shallow bowl, he ladles out as many portions of boiled rice as there are members of the sacrificer’s household.

8.10.8.a.m: More than that, if there is abundant boiled rice.

8.10.9.a.m: He places them down, ladled out, purified, adorned, and besprinkled with clarified butter.

8.10.10.a.m: On the dakṣiṇāgni he cooks a neighboring portion of boiled rice for the wife.

8.10.12.a.m: The Vājasaneyins prescribe the ladling out of two [dishes]:

8.10.12.b.m: From the southern one he sacrifices to the Maruts Gṛhamedhins;

8.11.1.a.m: from the northern one, to [Agni] Sviṣṭakṛt.

8.11.2.a.s: odanayornimne kṛtvā tatrājyamānīya tata ājyārthānkuruta ājyasthālyā veti vājasaneyakam
8.11.2.a.d: ओदनयोर्निम्ने कृत्वा तत्राज्यमानीय तत आज्यार्थान्कुरुत आज्यस्थाल्या वेति वाजसनेयकम्
8.11.2.a.m: “Having made depressions in the two portions of boiled rice and poured clarified butter into them, from there he performs the actions requiring clarified butter, or from the pot of clarified butter,” says a Vājasaneyaka passage.

8.11.3.a.m: Doing so, he should not take it into the dhruvā ladle.

8.11.4.a.s: ājyabhāgābhyāṃ pracarya juhvāmupastīrya sarvataḥ samavadāya maruto gṛhamedhino yajati
8.11.4.a.d: आज्यभागाभ्यां प्रचर्य जुह्वामुपस्तीर्य सर्वतः समवदाय मरुतो गृहमेधिनो यजति
8.11.4.a.m: Having proceeded with the two clarified butter portions and made an underlayer in the juhū ladle, having cut off [portions] from every side, he sacrifices to the Maruts Gṛhamedhins.

8.11.5.a.m: Having cut off once from the northern half of all of them, [he sacrifices] to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt.

8.11.6.a.m: There is no prāśitra portion, nor the sacrificer’s portion.

8.11.8.a.m: Those dependents of the sacrificer who eat the remnants of the sacrificial food consume the remainders of the boiled rice.

8.11.8.b.m: Or the officiating priests or other brahmins [consume it].

8.11.9.a.m: Brahmins consume the boiled rice that is in the cooking pot.

8.11.10.a.s: suhitā etāṃ rātriṃ vasanti pratītā anavartimukhinaḥ
8.11.10.a.d: सुहिता एतां रात्रिं वसन्ति प्रतीता अनवर्तिमुखिनः
8.11.10.a.m: Satiated, trusting, with faces free from distress, they pass this night.

8.11.15.a.m: He sets down the pot without scraping it out.

8.11.16.a.m: He lays alongside it the stirring ladle and the spoon, unwiped.

8.11.17.a.d: पराचीनरात्रे ऽभिवान्याया अग्निहोत्र्यै च वत्सौ बध्नाति
8.11.17.a.m: In the latter part of the night, he ties the two calves to the foster cow and to the agnihotra cow.

8.11.18.a.m: At daybreak, before the agnihotra, they perform the rite with the full ladle;

8.11.19.a.s: śaraniṣkāsasya darvīṃ pūrayitvarṣabhamāhūya tasya ravate pūrṇā darvi parāpatetyanudrutyottarayā gārhapatye juhuyāt
8.11.19.a.d: शरनिष्कासस्य दर्वीं पूरयित्वर्षभमाहूय तस्य रवते पूर्णा दर्वि परापतेत्यनुद्रुत्योत्तरया गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात्
8.11.19.a.m: Having filled the ladle with the scraper-remnants of the boiled mess and having called a bull, when he roars, he should run along [with the ladle] and offer into the gārhapatya with the next verse: 'O full ladle, fly away...'.

8.11.20.a.m: If the bull does not roar, the brahman should say, 'Offer!'

8.11.21.a.s: yasya ravate juhoti tāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadāti
8.11.21.a.d: यस्य रवते जुहोति तां दक्षिणां ददाति
8.11.21.a.m: At whose roaring he offers, that [bull] he gives as the sacrificial gift.

8.11.22.a.s: marudbhyaḥ krīḍibhyaḥ svatavadbhyo vā puroḍāśaṃ saptakapālaṃ nirvapati /
8.11.22.a.d: मरुद्भ्यः क्रीडिभ्यः स्वतवद्भ्यो वा पुरोडाशं सप्तकपालं निर्वपति ।
8.11.22.a.m: He parcels out a sacrificial cake on seven potsherds for the playful Maruts, or for the mighty Maruts.

8.11.22.b.s: sākaṃ sūryeṇodyatā sākaṃ vā raśmibhiḥ pracaranti /
8.11.22.b.d: साकं सूर्येणोद्यता साकं वा रश्मिभिः प्रचरन्ति ।
8.11.22.b.m: They proceed [with the offering] along with the rising sun, or along with its rays.

8.11.22.c.m: The sacrifice is concluded in the established manner.

8.12.1.a.m: Then he initiates the framework of the Mahāhavis.

8.12.2.a.m: Its procedure is explained by the northern fire-enclosure of the Vāruṇapraghāsa rites.

8.12.3.a.m: At the time of parceling out, he parcels out the eight subsequent oblations, beginning with 'the cake on eight potsherds for Agni'.

8.12.4.a.s: aindrasya caroḥ sthāna indrāya vṛtraghne carumeke samāmananti //
8.12.4.a.d: ऐन्द्रस्य चरोः स्थान इन्द्राय वृत्रघ्ने चरुमेके समामनन्ति ॥
8.12.4.a.m: In place of the boiled mess for Indra, some prescribe a boiled mess for Indra the slayer of Vṛtra.

8.12.4.b.m: He performs the continuous pouring of the ghee with the ladle, saying: 'Agni has enjoyed the office of hotṛ, he has enjoyed the message; he has stood erect at the sacrifice;

8.12.4.c.s: avatāṃ tvā dyāvāpṛthivī ava taṃ dyāvāpṛthivī /
8.12.4.c.d: अवतां त्वा द्यावापृथिवी अव तं द्यावापृथिवी ।
8.12.4.c.m: may Heaven and Earth protect you; may Heaven and Earth protect him;

8.12.4.d.s: sviṣṭakṛdindrāya devebhyo bhava juṣāṇo asya haviṣo ghṛtasya vīhi svāheti srucyamāghārayati //
8.12.4.d.d: स्विष्टकृदिन्द्राय देवेभ्यो भव जुषाणो अस्य हविषो घृतस्य वीहि स्वाहेति स्रुच्यमाघारयति ॥
8.12.4.d.m: be the maker of good offerings to Indra and to the gods; enjoying this oblation of ghee, partake of it, svāhā!'

8.12.4.e.m: The sacrificer addresses [the offering] with: 'You are Speech related to Agni...'.

8.12.5.a.m: He offers upon the single potsherd with four names of the months, beginning with 'Sahas and Sahasya' [etc.].

8.12.5.b.m: The sacrificial gift is a milch cow, or an old bull.

8.12.5.c.m: He hopes for the well-being of the Idāvatsara year.

8.12.5.d.m: Among the blessings of the sūktavāka recitation, the hotṛ continues with: 'He hopes for the divine abode.'

8.12.5.f.m: he modifies the mantra as: 'I hope...'

8.12.6.a.m: He consigns the chaff of the cake for Indra and Agni to the waters.

8.12.7.a.m: The sacrifice is concluded in the established manner.

8.13.1.a.m: At that very time, he initiates the framework of the Pitṛyajña.

8.13.2.a.s: vedaṃ kṛtvāgreṇānvāhāryapacanaṃ yajamānamātrīṃ catuḥsraktiṃ vediṃ karoti
8.13.2.a.d: वेदं कृत्वाग्रेणान्वाहार्यपचनं यजमानमात्रीं चतुःस्रक्तिं वेदिं करोति
8.13.2.a.m: Having made the broom-bunch, he makes in front of the anvāhāryapacana a four-cornered altar ground measuring the sacrificer's size.

8.13.3.a.m: The corners face the cardinal directions, the middles face the intermediate directions.

8.13.5.a.m: The altar ground should not be excavated eastward,

8.13.5.e.m: it should be excavated in between both directions;

8.13.5.f.s: ubhaye hi devāśca pitaraścejyanta iti vijñāyate
8.13.5.f.d: उभये हि देवाश्च पितरश्चेज्यन्त इति विज्ञायते
8.13.5.f.m: for it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa]: 'Both gods and ancestors are sacrificed to.'

8.13.6.a.s: ye ke ca devasaṃyuktā mantrā devebhyaḥ pitṛbhya iti tānsaṃnamati /
8.13.6.a.d: ये के च देवसंयुक्ता मन्त्रा देवेभ्यः पितृभ्य इति तान्संनमति ।
8.13.6.a.m: And whatever mantras contain the word 'gods', he modifies them to 'gods and ancestors',

8.13.6.b.m: as in: 'O earth, place of sacrifice to gods and ancestors!'

8.13.7.a.m: Or there is no modification, because of the hearing of the other text.

8.13.8.a.m: Having acted [up to the step] before the second enclosing line, he brings fire from the dakṣiṇāgni and sets it up in the middle of the altar ground.

8.13.9.a.m: In this Pitṛyajña, the duties of the āhavanīya are performed [in that fire].

8.13.10.a.m: Having added fuel to the fires, he brings the firewood and the sacrificial grass.

8.13.13.a.m: The firewood is larger and longer in proportion to its purpose.

8.13.14.a.m: Having strewn grass around the fires, he proceeds to the rite beginning with the washing of hands.

8.13.14.b.m: The setting out of the vessels is according to the purpose.

8.13.15.a.s: nirvapaṇakāle sarvato vediṃ pariśrityottareṇa dvāraṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇataḥ prācīnāvītī havīṃṣi nirvapati /
8.13.15.a.d: निर्वपणकाले सर्वतो वेदिं परिश्रित्योत्तरेण द्वारं कृत्वा दक्षिणतः प्राचीनावीती हवींषि निर्वपति ।
8.13.15.a.m: At the time of parceling out, having screened the altar ground on all sides and having made an entrance to the north, he parcels out the oblations from the south, wearing his sacred cord over the right shoulder;

8.13.15.c.m: wearing the sacred cord over the left shoulder, for 'Soma accompanied by the ancestors,' as handed down in the text.

8.13.16.b.s: somāya pitṛmata ājyaṃ pitṛbhyo barhiṣadbhyaḥ ṣaṭkapālaṃ pitṛbhyo 'gniṣvāttebhyo dhānā agnaye kavyavāhanāya yamāya vā manthaṃ yamāyāṅgirasvate pitṛmate
8.13.16.b.d: सोमाय पितृमत आज्यं पितृभ्यो बर्हिषद्भ्यः षट्कपालं पितृभ्यो ऽग्निष्वात्तेभ्यो धाना अग्नये कव्यवाहनाय यमाय वा मन्थं यमायाङ्गिरस्वते पितृमते
8.13.16.b.m: Clarified butter for Soma accompanied by the ancestors, a cake on six potsherds for the ancestors seated on the grass, parched grains for the ancestors consumed by fire, and a mixed beverage for Agni bearer of the funeral offering or for Yama, [or] for Yama accompanied by the Aṅgirases and accompanied by the ancestors.

8.13.17.a.m: A water-jar serves as the vessel for the sprinkling water.

8.13.18.a.s: prokṣaṇyudrekeṇa yavānsaṃyutya triṣphalīkṛtāṃstaṇḍulānvibhāgamantreṇa vibhajya dhānārthānnidhāyetarānpiṣṭāni kṛtvā dakṣiṇārdhe gārhapatyasya ṣaṭkapālānyupadhāya dakṣiṇāgnau prathamena kapālamantreṇa dhānārthaṃ kapālamadhiśrayati
8.13.18.a.d: प्रोक्षण्युद्रेकेण यवान्संयुत्य त्रिष्फलीकृतांस्तण्डुलान्विभागमन्त्रेण विभज्य धानार्थान्निधायेतरान्पिष्टानि कृत्वा दक्षिणार्धे गार्हपत्यस्य षट्कपालान्युपधाय दक्षिणाग्नौ प्रथमेन कपालमन्त्रेण धानार्थं कपालमधिश्रयति
8.13.18.a.m: Having mixed barley with the remainder of the sprinkling water, having divided the husked rice that has been husked three times with the division mantra, having set aside [the grains] intended for the parched grains, having made the others into flour, and having arranged six potsherds in the southern half of the gārhapatya, he puts a potsherd for the parched grains onto the dakṣiṇāgni with the first potsherd mantra.

8.13.19.a.d: अधिश्रयणकाले ऽधिश्रयणमनत्रेण तण्डुलानोप्य बहुरूपा धानाः करोति
8.13.19.a.m: At the time of setting [them] over [the fire], having poured the rice grains with the mantra for setting over [the fire], he makes variegated parched grains.

8.13.20.a.m: For it is known: 'Being slightly scorched, they lie about.'

8.14.1.a.m: At the time of the ritual calls, he issues the ritual calls excluding the wife.

8.14.2.a.m: At the time of taking the clarified butter, he takes four portions of clarified butter to the north of the gārhapatya.

8.14.3.a.m: He proceeds to the rite beginning with the consecration of the sprinkling water.

8.14.4.a.s: sataraṇakāle barhiṣā triḥ prasavyaṃ vediṃ stṛṇanparyeti
8.14.4.a.d: सतरणकाले बर्हिषा त्रिः प्रसव्यं वेदिं स्तृणन्पर्येति
8.14.4.a.m: At the time of strewing, he walks around three times counter-clockwise, strewing the altar ground with sacrificial grass;

8.14.5.a.m: holding raised [grass bunches], he walks around three times in the opposite direction without strewing.

8.14.7.a.m: The taking and placing of the grass bunch are done silently.

8.14.9.a.m: He puts around two enclosing sticks,

8.14.12.a.s: yadi sarvānāvāhanakāle paridhīm̐raporṇviti vābhijñāya dakṣiṇaṃ madhyame paridhāvupasamasyet
8.14.12.a.d: यदि सर्वानावाहनकाले परिधीम्̐रपोर्ण्विति वाभिज्ञाय दक्षिणं मध्यमे परिधावुपसमस्येत्
8.14.12.a.m: If all, then at the time of summoning, recognising [the moment] or upon the words 'Uncover the enclosing sticks', he should push the southern one alongside the middle enclosing stick.

8.14.13.a.s: udvāsanakāle dhānā udvāsya vibhāgamantreṇa vibhajyārdhā ājyena saṃyauti
8.14.13.a.d: उद्वासनकाले धाना उद्वास्य विभागमन्त्रेण विभज्यार्धा आज्येन संयौति
8.14.13.a.m: At the time of taking off [the offerings], having taken off the parched barley grains and having divided them with the formula for division, he mixes half with clarified butter.

8.14.14.a.s: ardhāḥ piṣṭānāmāvṛtā saktūnkṛtvābhivānthāyai dugdhasyārdhaśarāve saktūnopyaikayekṣuśalākayekṣukāṇḍena vā dakṣiṇāmukhastriḥ prasavyamanārabhyopamanthati
8.14.14.a.d: अर्धाः पिष्टानामावृता सक्तून्कृत्वाभिवान्थायै दुग्धस्यार्धशरावे सक्तूनोप्यैकयेक्षुशलाकयेक्षुकाण्डेन वा दक्षिणामुखस्त्रिः प्रसव्यमनारभ्योपमन्थति
8.14.14.a.m: Having ground half into groats according to the procedure for flour, pouring the groats into half a bowl of milk from a cow that mates with a bull while pregnant, he stirs [them] three times counterclockwise with a single stalk of reed or a piece of sugarcane, facing south, without touching [the bowl with his hand].

8.14.15.a.m: Having placed the stir-stick in the beverage, he sets down the sacrificial offerings one by one.

8.14.16.a.s: dakṣiṇataḥ kaśipūpabarhaṇamāñjanamabhyañjanamudakumbhamityekaikaśa āsādya vedaṃ nidhāya sāmidhenībhyaḥ pratipadyate
8.14.16.a.d: दक्षिणतः कशिपूपबर्हणमाञ्जनमभ्यञ्जनमुदकुम्भमित्येकैकश आसाद्य वेदं निधाय सामिधेनीभ्यः प्रतिपद्यते
8.14.16.a.m: Having set down one by one to the south the grass mat and cushion, collyrium, unguent, and a water-pot, and having laid down the veda-broom, he proceeds to the kindling verses.

8.14.17.a.m: He issues the ritual call: 'Recite for Agni, for the gods, for the Ancestors, as he is being kindled.'

8.14.18.a.m: He recites one kindling verse three times,

8.14.19.a.s: ekāmanūyājasamidhamavaśiṣya samaśa idhmaṃ traidhaṃ vibhajya trirādadhāti
8.14.19.a.d: एकामनूयाजसमिधमवशिष्य समश इध्मं त्रैधं विभज्य त्रिरादधाति
8.14.19.a.m: Leaving aside one stick of kindling for the after-offerings, having divided the firewood equally into three parts, he puts [them] on three times.

8.14.21.a.m: He does not choose the ancestral seers, nor the hotṛ.

8.14.22.a.m: Having called for recitation, he says: 'Sit down, hotṛ.'

8.14.23.a.m: Having offered the fore-offerings without the barhis, he offers the two butter portions containing the word 'alive':

8.14.24.a.s: ā no agne suketunā rayiṃ viśvāyupoṣasam /
8.14.24.a.d: आ नो अग्ने सुकेतुना रयिं विश्वायुपोषसम् ।
8.14.24.a.m: 'Agni, with good guidance, grant us wealth, nourishment of a full lifespan

8.14.24.c.s: tvaṃ soma mahe bhagaṃ tvaṃ yūna ṛtāyate /
8.14.24.c.d: त्वं सोम महे भगं त्वं यून ऋतायते ।
8.14.24.c.m: 'You, Soma, bestow great fortune; you bestow skill

8.14.24.d.m: upon the youth who observes truth, so that he may live'—these are the two containing the word 'alive'.

8.14.25.a.m: Here some teach the enclosing of the altar ground with screens:

8.15.1.a.m: 'Having untied their sacred threads, they make them hang over the right shoulder;

8.15.1.b.m: the priests walk about in reverse;

8.15.1.c.m: they transpose the ladles, the offerings, and the screens.'

8.15.2.a.m: He places the upabhṛt to the south of the juhū;

8.15.2.b.s: dakṣiṇenopabhrtaṃ dhruvāṃ dakṣiṇena puroḍāśaṃ dhānāstā dakṣiṇena mantham
8.15.2.b.d: दक्षिणेनोपभ्र्तं ध्रुवां दक्षिणेन पुरोडाशं धानास्ता दक्षिणेन मन्थम्
8.15.2.b.m: the dhruvā to the south of the upabhṛt; the parched barley grains to the south of the sacrificial cake; and the stir-beverage to the south of them.

8.15.3.a.m: The juhū and the cake on six potsherds are placed in the same spot.

8.15.4.a.m: Some say the Brahman and the sacrificer [also change places].

8.15.5.a.m: There are six cuttings for those who make five cuttings, and five cuttings for those who make four cuttings.

8.15.6.a.m: Breaking through the sacrificial cake, he cuts [portions].

8.15.7.a.m: For one who makes five cuttings, he should cut twice from the first [offering].

8.15.8.a.d: जुह्वामुपस्तीर्य सोमाय पितृमते ऽनु स्वधेति संप्रेष्यति
8.15.8.a.m: Having spread under [clarified butter] in the juhū, he issues the ritual call: 'Svadha for Soma accompanied by the Ancestors!'

8.15.9.a.m: He takes a cutting once from the sacrificial cake, once from the parched barley grains, and once from the stir-beverage.

8.15.10.a.m: Having taken cuttings from the south side and having basted them, stepping across toward the north and standing facing south, he calls for recitation with: 'Bring svadhā!'

8.15.11.a.m: [The agnīdh] responds with: 'Let there be svadhā.'

8.15.11.b.m: He issues the ritual call: 'Offer svadhā to Soma accompanied by the Ancestors.'

8.15.11.c.m: With: 'We who make svadhā...', he offers.

8.15.11.d.m: He pronounces the vaṣaṭ-call with: 'Svadhā, reverence!'

8.15.12.a.m: However, rejecting the svadhā-call, he prescribes the calls and responses of the Bahvṛcas and Vājasaneyins.

8.15.15.a.s: tvaṃ soma pracikita ityetā āmnātā bhavanti
8.15.15.a.d: त्वं सोम प्रचिकित इत्येता आम्नाता भवन्ति
8.15.15.a.m: 'You, Soma, understand...'—these are handed down by tradition.

8.15.17.b.s: ye agniṣvāttā ye 'nagniṣvāttā aṃhomucaḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ /
8.15.17.b.d: ये अग्निष्वात्ता ये ऽनग्निष्वात्ता अंहोमुचः पितरः सोम्यासः ।
8.15.17.b.m: 'The Ancestors who are consumed by fire, and who are not consumed by fire, deliverers from distress, worthy of Soma,

8.15.17.c.d: परे ऽवरे मृतासो भवन्तो ऽधिब्रुवन्तु ते अवन्त्वस्मान् ॥
8.15.17.c.m: whether far or near, being departed, let them speak for us, let them aid us.'

8.15.17.d.s: vānyāyai dugdhe juṣamāṇāḥ karambhamudīrāṇā avare pare ca /
8.15.17.d.d: वान्यायै दुग्धे जुषमाणाः करम्भमुदीराणा अवरे परे च ।
8.15.17.d.m: 'Enjoying the porridge made with the milk of a cow mating while pregnant, rising up, those who are lower and those who are higher,

8.15.17.e.s: agniṣvāttā ṛtubhiḥ saṃvidānā indravanto haviridaṃ juṣantāmiti pitṛbhyo 'gniṣvāttebhyaḥ
8.15.17.e.d: अग्निष्वात्ता ऋतुभिः संविदाना इन्द्रवन्तो हविरिदं जुषन्तामिति पितृभ्यो ऽग्निष्वात्तेभ्यः
8.15.17.e.m: the Agniṣvāttas, being in accord with the seasons, accompanied by Indra, let them enjoy this oblation'—[these are] for the Agniṣvātta Ancestors.

8.15.18.a.m: They perform the Ancestor sacrifice in a low voice within the screened [enclosure].

8.15.19.a.m: According to this very procedure, he sacrifices to the Barhiṣad Ancestors and to the Agniṣvāttas.

8.15.20.a.m: He sacrifices to Agni Kavyavāhana in place of the Sviṣṭakṛt.

8.15.21.a.m: To whichever deity he sacrifices, he takes the first cutting from that [deity's] oblation.

8.15.23.a.m: He cuts the iḍā into the stir-beverage, or [takes] the stir-beverage itself [as the iḍā].

8.15.24.a.m: He places the stir-beverage into the hands of the hotṛ.

8.16.1.a.m: Likewise the brahman, the adhvaryu, the agnīdh, and the sacrificer.

8.16.3.a.s: samaśo vā prativibhajyāvaghreṇa bhakṣayitvā barhiṣi lepānnimṛjante
8.16.3.a.d: समशो वा प्रतिविभज्यावघ्रेण भक्षयित्वा बर्हिषि लेपान्निमृजन्ते
8.16.3.a.m: Or having divided it into equal parts and consumed [their shares] by smelling, they wipe off the remnants upon the barhis.

8.16.4.a.s: udakumbhamādāya yajamānaḥ śundhantāṃ pitara iti triḥ prasavyaṃ vediṃ pariṣiñcanparyeti
8.16.4.a.d: उदकुम्भमादाय यजमानः शुन्धन्तां पितर इति त्रिः प्रसव्यं वेदिं परिषिञ्चन्पर्येति
8.16.4.a.m: Taking a jar of water, the sacrificer goes around the altar ground three times from right to left, sprinkling it with the formula: 'May the ancestors be purified.'

8.16.5.a.s: nidhāya kumbhamayā viṣṭhā janayan karvarāṇīti trirapariṣiñcanpratiparyeti
8.16.5.a.d: निधाय कुम्भमया विष्ठा जनयन् कर्वराणीति त्रिरपरिषिञ्चन्प्रतिपर्येति
8.16.5.a.m: Setting down the jar, he goes back around three times without sprinkling, with the formula: 'Generating various forms, may these become adorned.'

8.16.6.a.s: haviḥśeṣānsaṃplomnāya piṇḍānkṛtvā tisṛṣu sraktiṣu nidadhāti pūrvasyāṃ dakṣiṇasyāmaparasyāmiti /
8.16.6.a.d: हविःशेषान्संप्लोम्नाय पिण्डान्कृत्वा तिसृषु स्रक्तिषु निदधाति पूर्वस्यां दक्षिणस्यामपरस्यामिति ।
8.16.6.a.m: Having collected the remnants of the oblation and formed them into rice-balls, he places them at three corners: at the eastern, at the southern, and at the western;

8.16.6.b.s: etatte tatāsau ye ca tvāmanvityetaiḥ pratimantram
8.16.6.b.d: एतत्ते ततासौ ये च त्वामन्वित्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
8.16.6.b.m: with these respective formulas: 'This is yours, father N.N., and of those who follow you.'

8.16.7.b.m: the sixth on the first rice-ball,

8.16.8.a.s: uttarasyāṃ sraktyāṃ riptalepaṃ nimṛjyātra pitaro yathābhāgaṃ mandadhvamityuktvodañco niṣkramya susaṃdṛśaṃ tvā vayamityaindryarcāhavanīyamupatiṣṭhanta aindrībhyāṃ vā
8.16.8.a.d: उत्तरस्यां स्रक्त्यां रिप्तलेपं निमृज्यात्र पितरो यथाभागं मन्दध्वमित्युक्त्वोदञ्चो निष्क्रम्य सुसंदृशं त्वा वयमित्यैन्द्र्यर्चाहवनीयमुपतिष्ठन्त ऐन्द्रीभ्यां वा
8.16.8.a.m: Having wiped off the smeared remnant on the northern corner, saying, 'Here, O ancestors, take delight according to your shares,' and stepping out towards the north, they worship the āhavanīya with the Indra verse, 'You of fair appearance we...', or with two Indra verses.

8.16.9.a.m: Having worshipped until they lose their breath, they worship the gārhapatya with the paṅkti verse: 'They have eaten, they have rejoiced...'

8.16.10.a.m: With that very verse they enter the enclosed area.

8.16.11.a.m: Here some prescribe the consuming and the sprinkling.

8.16.13.a.m: The rites from the application of collyrium up to the paṅkti verse are as in the Piṇḍapitṛyajña.

8.16.14.a.m: He returns with the paṅkti verse: 'What [we have done] in the intermediate space...'

8.16.15.a.m: Undoing their garments worn over the right shoulder (prācīnāvīta), they make them worn over the left shoulder (yajñopavīta).

8.16.15.b.m: The priests step around in reverse.

8.16.17.a.m: Having poured the ghee from the upabhṛt into the juhū, he offers the two after-offerings (anuyājas) without the barhis.

8.16.17.b.m: He issues the first call: 'Sacrifice to the two gods.'

8.16.18.a.m: At the time of the sūktavāka recitation, they wear their garments suspended around the neck (nivīta).

8.16.19.a.m: They do not perform the offerings to the wives of the gods (patnīsaṃyājas).

8.16.20.a.m: He does not offer the samiṣṭayajus.

8.17.1.a.m: He portions out one-pot potsherd cakes for each individual: as many as there are members of the sacrificer's household together with the women, and one more in addition.

8.17.2.a.s: yāvanto gṛhyāḥ smastebhyaḥ kamakaramiti nirupyamāṇeṣu yajamāno japati
8.17.2.a.d: यावन्तो गृह्याः स्मस्तेभ्यः कमकरमिति निरुप्यमाणेषु यजमानो जपति
8.17.2.a.m: While they are being portioned out, the sacrificer murmurs: 'As many as we are household members, for them I have made ease.'

8.17.4.a.m: He places them on the northern half of the gārhapatya.

8.17.5.a.s: tānabhighāryānabhighārya vodvāsyāntarvedyāsādya paśūnaṃ śrmāsīti mūte samāvapati
8.17.5.a.d: तानभिघार्यानभिघार्य वोद्वास्यान्तर्वेद्यासाद्य पशूनं श्र्मासीति मूते समावपति
8.17.5.a.m: Having basted them or without basting them, having taken them down and set them inside the altar ground, he pours them into a woven basket with the formula: 'You are the protection of cattle.'

8.17.7.a.m: According to some, they carry them out with the cover of a chest.

8.17.8.a.s: eka eva rudro na dvitīyāya tastha iti dakṣiṇāgnerekolmukaṃ dhūpāyaddharati
8.17.8.a.d: एक एव रुद्रो न द्वितीयाय तस्थ इति दक्षिणाग्नेरेकोल्मुकं धूपायद्धरति
8.17.8.a.m: With the formula, 'Rudra alone is one, he did not stand for a second,' he carries a smoking firebrand from the southern fire (dakṣiṇāgni).

8.17.9.a.s: uttarapūrvamavāntaradeśaṃ gatvākhuste urdra paśurityākhūtkara ekaṃ puroḍāśamupavapati
8.17.9.a.d: उत्तरपूर्वमवान्तरदेशं गत्वाखुस्ते उर्द्र पशुरित्याखूत्कर एकं पुरोडाशमुपवपति
8.17.9.a.m: Having gone to the north-eastern intermediate direction, he places one sacrificial cake on a molehill with the formula: 'This is your beast, O Rudra: the mole.'

8.17.10.a.s: asau te paśuriti vā dveṣyaṃ manasā dhyāyan
8.17.10.a.d: असौ ते पशुरिति वा द्वेष्यं मनसा ध्यायन्
8.17.10.a.m: Or meditating in his mind upon an enemy: 'That one is your beast.'

8.17.11.a.m: If he does not hate anyone, he should say: 'The mole is your beast.'

8.17.12.a.s: catuṣpatha ekolmukamupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya sarveṣāṃ puroḍāśānāmuttarārdhātsakṛtsakṛdavadāya madhyamenāntamenā vā palāśaparṇena juhoti
8.17.12.a.d: चतुष्पथ एकोल्मुकमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य सर्वेषां पुरोडाशानामुत्तरार्धात्सकृत्सकृदवदाय मध्यमेनान्तमेना वा पलाशपर्णेन जुहोति
8.17.12.a.m: Having laid down the single firebrand at a crossroads and strewn around it, having cut off once from the northern half of each of all the sacrificial cakes, he offers with the middle or the terminal leaf of a palāśa leaf.

8.18.1.a.s: eṣa te rudra bhāgaḥ saha svasrāmbikayā taṃ juṣasva svāheti bheṣajaṃ gava ityetābhyāṃ cātuṣpathamagniṃ pariṣiñcati /
8.18.1.a.d: एष ते रुद्र भागः सह स्वस्राम्बिकया तं जुषस्व स्वाहेति भेषजं गव इत्येताभ्यां चातुष्पथमग्निं परिषिञ्चति ।
8.18.1.a.m: With the formula, 'This is your share, O Rudra, along with your sister Ambikā; enjoy it, svāhā,' and with the verse, 'Medicine for the cow...', he sprinkles the fire at the crossroads.

8.18.1.b.m: The sacrificer murmurs: 'We have appeased Rudra, the mother.'

8.18.2.a.s: tryambakaṃ yajāmaha iti triḥ pradakṣiṇamagniṃ pariyanti
8.18.2.a.d: त्र्यम्बकं यजामह इति त्रिः प्रदक्षिणमग्निं परियन्ति
8.18.2.a.m: They go around the fire three times from left to right with the formula: 'We worship Tryambaka...'

8.18.3.a.m: 'We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant one who procures a husband.

8.18.3.b.s: urvārukamiva bandhanādito mukṣīya mā pateriti yajamānasya patikāmā parīyāt
8.18.3.b.d: उर्वारुकमिव बन्धनादितो मुक्षीय मा पतेरिति यजमानस्य पतिकामा परीयात्
8.18.3.b.m: Like a cucumber from its stem, from here may I be freed, not from a husband'—a woman of the sacrificer's household who desires a husband should go around [with this verse].

8.18.4.a.s: ūrdhvānpuroḍāśānudasya pratilabhya tryambakaṃ yajāmaha iti yajamānasyāñjalau samopya bhaga stha bhagasya vo lapsīyetyapādāyaitenaiva kalpena triḥ samāvapeyuḥ
8.18.4.a.d: ऊर्ध्वान्पुरोडाशानुदस्य प्रतिलभ्य त्र्यम्बकं यजामह इति यजमानस्याञ्जलौ समोप्य भग स्थ भगस्य वो लप्सीयेत्यपादायैतेनैव कल्पेन त्रिः समावपेयुः
8.18.4.a.m: Having tossed the sacrificial cakes upwards and caught them, having poured them together into the folded hands of the sacrificer with the formula 'We worship Tryambaka...', and taking them back with the formula 'You are fortune; may I obtain your fortune,' they should pour them together three times in this same manner.

8.18.5.a.m: And they should pour them together in this way for a woman desiring a husband, modifying the formula accordingly.

8.18.6.a.m: According to some, they pour them together after each round of going around.

8.18.7.a.m: He pours them into a woven basket, or into two woven baskets, or into several woven baskets.

8.18.8.a.s: eṣa te rudra bhāga iti vṛkṣa āsajati vṛkṣayorvṛkṣeṣu vā
8.18.8.a.d: एष ते रुद्र भाग इति वृक्ष आसजति वृक्षयोर्वृक्षेषु वा
8.18.8.a.m: With the formula, 'This is your share, O Rudra,' he hangs it on a tree, or on two trees, or on several trees.
